```text
# translate

A fast CLI/TUI translation tool for the terminal — one-shot from the shell or an
interactive live-translating TUI. Backed by an auto fallback chain over your
local LLM providers (copilot-proxy → Ollama), a free web API (Google), and a
dictionary, with typo-tolerant language resolution and translation history.

## Install

```sh
brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate               # macOS/Linux via Homebrew (builds from source)
go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest   # or with a Go toolchain, into $GOBIN (~/.local/bin)
```

## Build & run

```sh
go build -o translate .      # Go 1.25+ (developed on 1.26)
./translate "hola mundo" --to en          # one-shot
echo "bonjour" | ./translate --to en      # pipe
./translate                               # interactive TUI
```

First run writes a default config to `~/.config/translate/config.toml`; run
`./translate init` for a guided setup that probes which providers are up.

## Usage

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `translate <text>` / `… \| translate` | One-shot translation (streams to a TTY; plain text when piped) |
| `translate` (no args, TTY) | Interactive TUI |
| `translate --to <lang> --from <lang>` | Language override; both are fuzzy (`chinees` → `zh`) |
| `translate --json` | Emit the full structured result |
| `… \| translate --bilingual` (`-2`) | Bilingual pipe view: keep the original (with color) + translation beneath (stdin only) |
| `translate define <word>` | Dictionary lookup (bilingual: zh↔en local, or English API) |
| `translate history` / `history search <q>` | Recent history / fuzzy search (`--tsv`, `--json`) |
| `translate init` | Interactive config wizard (probes providers) |
| `translate config path\|show` · `lang resolve <q>` | Introspection helpers |

Flags: `--engine smartauto|auto|<provider>|google`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--tier default|fast|max`, `--preset concise|contextual|dictionary`, `--instructions`, `--pair`/`--pair-with`, `--bilingual`/`-2`, `--no-history`, `--debug`.
Env overrides: `TRANSLATE_TARGET`, `TRANSLATE_SOURCE`, `TRANSLATE_ENGINE`, `TRANSLATE_PROVIDER`, `TRANSLATE_MODEL`, `TRANSLATE_CONFIG`, `TRANSLATE_DEBUG`.
Precedence: **flag > env > `[cli]`/`[tui]` > `[general]` > default**.

### Per-front-end defaults (`[cli]` / `[tui]`)

The CLI (arguments or piped stdin) and the interactive TUI share `[general]`, but
either can override any subset of it via an optional `[cli]` or `[tui]` table — e.g.
a snappy concise CLI and a richer, higher-tier TUI:

```toml
[general]
preset = "contextual"
tier   = "fast"

[cli]                 # one-shot / piped translation
preset = "concise"

[tui]                 # interactive front-end
tier          = "max"
live_translate = true
```

Only keys you list are overridden; the rest inherit `[general]`. Flags and env vars
still win over both.

## TUI keys

`↵` translate · live-debounce auto-translates ~700ms after you stop typing (off by default) ·
`^y` copy · `^l` toggle live · `^e` cycle engine · `^t` target language · `^p` model ·
`^o` style · `^g` toggle pair mode · `^u` clear · `⇥` switch input/output focus · `^r` history · `⌥↵` newline · `^c`/`esc` quit.

`⇥` (Tab) moves keyboard focus between the input box and the result box; the focused
box gets an accent border. With the result focused, `↑/↓ j/k PgUp/PgDn g/G space` scroll
it; typing any character snaps focus back to the input. A mouse click focuses the box
it lands in.

## Engines & fallback

The `auto` engine tries `chain.order` in turn, failing over **before the first
token** (so a down provider switches cleanly; a mid-stream error surfaces rather
than restarting):

- **copilot-proxy** — OpenAI-compatible at `http://localhost:4141/v1`, no API key.
  Default tier is **fast** (`claude-haiku-4-5`); `--tier default` → `claude-sonnet-5`,
  `--tier max` → `claude-opus-4-8`. Claude models are served only via the proxy's
  Anthropic Messages endpoint (`/v1/messages`) — the engine routes `claude-*` ids
  there automatically (they 400 on `/chat/completions`).
- **Ollama** — `http://localhost:11434/v1` (offline; `llama3.2:3b`).
- **Google** — free, keyless; also reports the detected source language.
- **openrouter** — configured but off the default chain; needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.

> ⚠️ Using a GitHub Copilot subscription to back non-GitHub tools (copilot-proxy)
> may violate Copilot's Terms of Service. Reorder `chain.order` (drop `copilot`,
> lead with `ollama`/`google`) in the config if that matters to you.

Config lives at `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, history at
`~/.local/share/translate/history.jsonl`, last-pair state at
`~/.local/state/translate/state.json` (XDG-honored on macOS and Linux).

### Smart auto (`smartauto`)

The recommended default (choose it in `translate init`). It routes by input shape:
a **single word/term** is looked up in the dictionary (with the same LLM fallback as
`smart-dict` on a miss), while a **phrase or sentence** is translated by the LLM. Set
`engine = "smartauto"` in `[general]` (or `--engine smartauto`). It composes with
pair mode, so a single word and a full sentence both translate in the right direction.

### Pair mode (bidirectional)

With `pair = true` + `pair_with`, the tool detects which of the two languages your
input is in and translates it into the **other** — one box, both directions
(`你好 → hi`, `test → 測試`). For a CJK/non-CJK pair (e.g. `zh-TW`⇄`en`) direction is
decided by script, so even short input routes correctly; the LLM translate prompt is
also told to detect-and-route and to **never echo** the input. `pair_with` must differ
from the target (`translate init` enforces this; a degenerate config warns).

### Bilingual mode (`--bilingual` / `-2`)

Pipe colored docs and read both languages at once — inspired by Immersive
Translate. `cmd | translate --to <lang> --bilingual` keeps each original block
verbatim (its ANSI/color intact) and prints the translation beneath each **prose**
block, dimmed on a TTY:

```sh
tldr rg | translate --to zh-TW --bilingual     # or -2
```

Indented command/example blocks are echoed **untranslated** (so `rg pattern` stays
runnable), and blank-line spacing is preserved. It is opt-in and **stdin-only** —
never the pipe default, so plain `cmd | translate | less`/`grep` stays clean
single-output. Best for prose docs (tldr, man, `--help`); tabular output
(`ls -l`, `git status`) and hard-wrapped prose don't interleave cleanly.
`--json`/`--learn` take precedence. Design notes + why per-word recoloring was
rejected: [`backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md`](backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md).

Two strategies, via `--bilingual-mode`:

- **`doc`** (default) — one **context-aware** call: the whole document is sent as
  numbered segments (prose to translate, commands as context), so the model knows a
  bare `rg` is the command being documented (not an abbreviation), stays in one
  target variant, and doesn't leak reasoning. Fewer tokens than per-block, and needs
  an LLM provider.
- **`blocks`** — the older per-block strategy (each block translated in isolation,
  concurrent, works with any engine). `doc` automatically falls back to this when no
  LLM is available or the structured reply can't be parsed.

Separately, ANSI escapes are now **stripped from piped input** before translating,
so colored input (e.g. `grep --color=always`) no longer pollutes the prompt.

### Debugging

`--debug` (or `TRANSLATE_DEBUG=1`, or `[general] debug = true`) logs the intermediate
decisions — resolved settings, pair routing, word-vs-phrase classification, dictionary
hit/miss, and chain fallback. The one-shot CLI logs to **stderr**; the TUI logs to
`~/.local/state/translate/debug.log` (its alt-screen hides stderr).

## Dictionary mode

`^e` cycles to the dictionary engine (or use `translate define <word>`). It is an
**offline bilingual** dictionary that routes by script — Chinese → CC-CEDICT
(zh→en), English → ECDICT (en→zh):

```sh
translate dict update all      # one-time ~67 MB download/build into ~/.local/share/translate/dict
```

Until then, English lookups fall back to dictionaryapi.dev (`[dict] api_fallback`),
and Chinese lookups prompt you to run the update. Misses show a ranked "did you
mean" list. Set `[dict] source = "api"` to use only dictionaryapi.dev.

### Smart dictionary (`smart-dict`)

A distinct engine that keeps the offline dictionary fast and deterministic, but on
a miss — no entry, or a fuzzy match too far off — falls back to the LLM for a gloss
plus example sentences (never silently: the result carries a `⚠ … defined via <provider> (LLM)`
warning). Close typos (edit distance ≤ `[smartdict] close_distance`, default 1) still
show "did you mean" without calling the LLM.

```sh
translate define serendipity        # exact ECDICT entry
translate define zzzznotaword       # miss → LLM definition (⚠ warning on stderr)
translate define helllo             # distance-1 typo → "did you mean: hello, …"
translate define --plain <word>     # force the offline dictionary, no LLM fallback
```

`translate define` uses smart-dict whenever an LLM provider is reachable
(`[smartdict] define_default`, `--smart`/`--plain` to force); in the TUI, `^e`
cycles to a `smart-dict` engine alongside the plain `dictionary`.

```toml
[smartdict]
close_distance = 1            # en edit-distance ≤ this stays "did you mean"; beyond → LLM
preset         = "dictionary" # LLM output style for the fallback
define_default = true         # `translate define` prefers smart-dict when a provider is up
```

Data: **CC-CEDICT** (CC BY-SA 4.0, © Paul Andrew Denisowski / MDBG) and
**ECDICT** (MIT, © skywind3000).
```
</details></tool-use>

56	// NewRootCmd builds the root command and its subcommands.
57	func NewRootCmd() *cobra.Command {
58		root := &cobra.Command{
59			Use:   "translate [text...]",
60			Short: "Fast terminal translation (CLI + TUI)",
61			Long: "translate is a fast CLI/TUI translator.\n\n" +
62				"  translate \"hola mundo\" --to en    one-shot\n" +
63				"  echo hola | translate --to en       pipe\n" +
64				"  translate                           interactive TUI",
65			Version:       buildVersion(),
66			SilenceUsage:  true,
67			SilenceErrors: true,
68			// ArbitraryArgs lets bare text fall through to translation while exact
69			// subcommands (config, lang, …) still route. Without it, cobra rejects
70			// `translate "hola"` as an unknown command once subcommands exist.
71			Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
72			RunE: runRoot,
73		}
74		f := root.PersistentFlags()
75		f.StringVarP(&flagTo, "to", "t", "", "target language (fuzzy; e.g. en, chinese)")
76		f.StringVarP(&flagFrom, "from", "f", "", "source language (\"auto\" to detect)")
77		f.StringVar(&flagModel, "model", "", "LLM model id override")
78		f.StringVar(&flagProvider, "provider", "", "provider name (e.g. copilot, ollama)")
79		f.StringVar(&flagEngine, "engine", "", "engine: auto|<provider>|google|dict")
80		f.StringVar(&flagTier, "tier", "", "model tier: default|fast|max")
81		f.StringVar(&flagPreset, "preset", "", "LLM prompt style: concise|contextual|dictionary")
82		f.StringVar(&flagInstructions, "instructions", "", "extra system-prompt guidance (domain focus, etc.)")
83		f.BoolVar(&flagPair, "pair", false, "bidirectional mode: home-language input → --pair-with, else → --to")
84		f.StringVar(&flagPairWith, "pair-with", "", "the other language for --pair (e.g. en)")
85		f.BoolVar(&flagLearn, "learn", false, "learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)")
86		f.BoolVarP(&flagBilingual, "bilingual", "2", false, "bilingual pipe mode: keep original (with color) + translation beneath (stdin only)")
87		f.StringVar(&flagBilingualMode, "bilingual-mode", "doc", "bilingual strategy: doc (context-aware, one LLM call) | blocks (per-block)")
88		f.BoolVar(&flagJSON, "json", false, "emit the full result as JSON")
89		f.BoolVar(&flagStream, "stream", false, "force token streaming to stdout even when it is not a TTY (for piped consumers, e.g. the Raycast extension)")
90		f.BoolVar(&flagNoHistory, "no-history", false, "do not record this translation in history")
91		f.BoolVar(&flagDebug, "debug", false, "log intermediate decisions (routing, engine choice, dict hit/miss)")
92		f.BoolVarP(&flagSpeak, "speak", "s", false, "speak the foreign side of the result aloud (free TTS)")
93		f.StringVar(&flagSpeakLang, "speak-lang", "", "force the spoken language (e.g. en, zh-TW)")
94	
95		root.SuggestionsMinimumDistance = 2
96		root.AddCommand(newConfigCmd(), newLangCmd(), newDefineCmd(), newHistoryCmd(), newInitCmd(), newDictCmd(), newSpeakCmd(), newServeCmd(), newMcpCmd())
97		return root
98	}

100	// Execute runs the root command with the given (cancellable) context.
101	func Execute(ctx context.Context) error {
102		// Stamp the writing app version into any config Save this run makes.
103		config.Generator = shortVersion()
104		return NewRootCmd().ExecuteContext(ctx)
105	}
106	
107	// overrides collects the explicitly-set flag values.
108	func overrides() config.Overrides {
109		return config.Overrides{
110			Source:       flagFrom,
111			Target:       flagTo,
112			Engine:       flagEngine,
113			Provider:     flagProvider,
114			Model:        flagModel,
115			Tier:         flagTier,
116			Preset:       flagPreset,
117			Instructions: flagInstructions,
118			Pair:         flagPair,
119			PairWith:     flagPairWith,
120			Learn:        flagLearn,
121			Debug:        flagDebug,
122		}
123	}
124	
125	// invocationMode reports whether this run is the one-shot CLI (arguments or piped
126	// stdin) or the interactive TUI (a TTY with no arguments). It mirrors the dispatch
127	// switch in runRoot and is computed before Resolve so the [cli]/[tui] overlay applies.
128	func invocationMode(args []string) config.Mode {
129		if len(args) > 0 {
130			return config.ModeCLI
131		}
132		if !term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdin.Fd())) {
133			return config.ModeCLI
134		}
135		return config.ModeTUI
136	}
137	
138	func runRoot(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
139		ctx := cmd.Context()
140	
141		cfg, created, err := config.Load()
142		if err != nil {
143			return err
144		}
145		if created {
146			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: wrote default config to %s (run `translate init` to customize)\n", config.Path())
147		} else if cfg.Outdated() {
148			// Schema bumps so far are additive: Load already filled any new fields with
149			// their Default() values in memory, so re-saving materializes them on disk
150			// (every existing value preserved) and re-stamps the schema — no wizard
151			// needed. A genuinely breaking change would instead need an explicit
152			// migration here before the re-save.
153			from := cfg.Schema
154			if err := config.Save(cfg); err != nil {
155				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: config is outdated but auto-upgrade failed (%v) — run `translate init`\n", err)
156			} else {
157				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: upgraded config schema v%d→v%d (new settings use defaults; `translate init` to review)\n", from, config.SchemaVersion)
158			}
159		}
160	
161		res := cfg.Resolve(overrides(), invocationMode(args))
162		if res.Debug {
163			// The one-shot CLI logs to stderr; the TUI logs to a file, since its
164			// alt-screen would be corrupted by stderr writes.
165			if invocationMode(args) == config.ModeCLI {
166				debug.Enable(os.Stderr)
167			} else if w := openDebugLog(); w != nil {
168				debug.Enable(w)
169			}
170		}
171		applyLastPair(cfg, &res) // remember_last_pair: seed source/target from state
172		src, tgt := resolvePair(res.Source, res.Target)
173		pairWith := ""
174		if res.Pair {
175			pwm, _ := lang.Resolve(res.PairWith)
176			pairWith = pwm.Code
177		}
178		// Learn mode is bidirectional; ensure a distinct "away" (foreign) language so
179		// direction routing has two sides to choose between.
180		if res.Learn && (pairWith == "" || strings.EqualFold(pairWith, tgt)) {
181			pairWith = defaultAway(tgt)
182		}
183		debug.Logf("resolved: engine=%s tier=%s preset=%s source=%s target=%s pair=%v pair_with=%s learn=%v",
184			res.Engine, res.Tier, res.Preset, src, tgt, res.Pair, pairWith, res.Learn)
185		if res.Pair && !res.Learn && (pairWith == "" || strings.EqualFold(pairWith, tgt)) {
186			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: pair mode is on but pair-with (%q) equals the target (%q) — pair mode is a no-op; set a different pair_with (run `translate init`)\n", pairWith, tgt)
187		}
188	
189		if res.Provider == nil && res.Engine != "auto" {
190			return fmt.Errorf("no provider configured; check %s", config.Path())
191		}
192		eng, err := appcore.BuildEngine(res)
193		if err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196	
197		// The one-shot CLI path routes a learn request through a bare LLM engine
198		// (bypassing smart-auto/dictionary); the TUI keeps its normal primary engine and
199		// toggles learn at runtime against Params.LearnEngine.
200		learnCLI := res.Learn && invocationMode(args) == config.ModeCLI
201		if learnCLI && res.Provider == nil {
202			return fmt.Errorf("learn mode requires an LLM provider; check %s", config.Path())
203		}
204		oneShotEng := eng
205		if learnCLI {
206			oneShotEng = appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig(res)
207		}
208	
209		st := openStore(cfg)
210		if st != nil {
211			defer st.Close()
212		}
213	
214		switch {
215		case len(args) > 0:
216			text := strings.Join(args, " ")
217			effTgt := appcore.EffectiveTarget(res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, text)
218			r, err := oneShot(ctx, oneShotEng, text, src, effTgt, res.Stream, res.Preset, res.Instructions, res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, res.Learn)
219			if err != nil {
220				return err
221			}
222			recordAndRemember(ctx, st, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, tgt)
223			if shouldSpeak(cfg) {
224				speakResult(ctx, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, speakForeign(cfg, pairWith))
225			}
226			return nil
227	
228		case !term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdin.Fd())):
229			b, err := io.ReadAll(os.Stdin)
230			if err != nil {
231				return err
232			}
233			// Strip ANSI/SGR escapes so colored piped input (e.g. `tldr rg | translate`)
234			// never pollutes the prompt. The raw bytes are retained only for --bilingual,
235			// which needs the original styling for display.
236			text := strings.TrimSpace(bitext.Strip(string(b)))
237			if text == "" {
238				return fmt.Errorf("no input on stdin")
239			}
240			// Bilingual is a multi-block reading view; --json/--learn keep their own
241			// structured output and take precedence.
242			if flagBilingual && !flagJSON && !res.Learn {
243				// doc mode needs an LLM (structured JSON, empty Text confuses
244				// smartauto/chain routing) — build a bare LLM like learn mode; nil when
245				// no provider, in which case runBilingual falls back to per-block.
246				var docEng engine.Engine
247				if res.Provider != nil {
248					docEng = appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig(res)
249				}
250				return runBilingual(ctx, oneShotEng, docEng, string(b), src, tgt, res.Instructions, flagBilingualMode)
251			}
252			effTgt := appcore.EffectiveTarget(res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, text)
253			r, err := oneShot(ctx, oneShotEng, text, src, effTgt, res.Stream, res.Preset, res.Instructions, res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, res.Learn)
254			if err != nil {
255				return err
256			}
257			recordAndRemember(ctx, st, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, tgt)
258			if shouldSpeak(cfg) {
259				speakResult(ctx, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, speakForeign(cfg, pairWith))
260			}
261			return nil
262	
263		default:
264			return runTUI(ctx, eng, res, st, src, tgt, pairWith)
265		}
266	}
267	
268	// openDebugLog opens (append) the TUI debug log file, creating the state dir.
269	// Returns nil on failure (debug simply stays off).
270	func openDebugLog() io.Writer {
271		if err := xdgpath.EnsureDirs(); err != nil {
272			return nil
273		}
274		f, err := os.OpenFile(filepath.Join(xdgpath.StateDir(), "debug.log"),
275			os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_APPEND, 0o600)
276		if err != nil {
277			return nil
278		}
279		return f
280	}
281	
282	// applyLastPair overrides the resolved source/target with the persisted last
283	// pair when remember_last_pair is on and the user did not pass flags/env.
284	func applyLastPair(cfg *config.Config, res *config.Resolved) {
285		if !cfg.General.RememberLastPair {
286			return
287		}
288		// Pair (and learn) mode anchors BOTH languages from config: Target is the home
289		// language, PairWith is the away language, and routing is decided per input. A
290		// remembered target must not override the home here — if the last session
291		// happened to translate into the away language, restoring it as the home makes
292		// home == away and pair mode collapses to a no-op (the "en⇄en" bug). Source is
293		// always auto-detected in pair mode too, so skip the whole override.
294		if res.Pair {
295			debug.Logf("remember_last_pair: skipped (pair mode anchors languages from config)")
296			return
297		}
298		stt, err := state.Load()
299		if err != nil || stt == nil {
300			return
301		}
302		if flagFrom == "" && os.Getenv("TRANSLATE_SOURCE") == "" && stt.Source != "" {
303			res.Source = stt.Source
304			debug.Logf("remember_last_pair: source ← %s (from state)", stt.Source)
305		}
306		if flagTo == "" && os.Getenv("TRANSLATE_TARGET") == "" && stt.Target != "" {
307			res.Target = stt.Target
308			debug.Logf("remember_last_pair: target ← %s (from state)", stt.Target)
309		}
310	}

312	// openStore opens the history store, or returns nil when history is disabled or
313	// suppressed with --no-history.
314	func openStore(cfg *config.Config) store.Store {
315		if !cfg.History.Enabled || flagNoHistory {
316			return nil
317		}
318		path := cfg.History.Path
319		if path == "" {
320			path = xdgpath.HistoryFile()
321		}
322		st, err := store.OpenJSONL(path)
323		if err != nil {
324			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: history disabled (%v)\n", err)
325			return nil
326		}
327		return st
328	}
329	
330	// recordAndRemember writes the translation to history and persists the last pair.
331	//
332	// target is the effective target actually used (for history); rememberTarget is
333	// the stable home target (== target unless pair mode redirected this one input),
334	// so persisting it keeps pair mode from drifting its home to the away language.
335	func recordAndRemember(ctx context.Context, st store.Store, cfg *config.Config, res *engine.TranslateResult, input, source, target, rememberTarget string) {
336		if st != nil {
337			_, _ = st.Add(ctx, appcore.ToRecord(res, input, source, target))
338		}
339		if cfg.General.RememberLastPair {
340			saveLastPair(source, rememberTarget, res.Engine)
341		}
342	}
343	
344	// saveLastPair persists the source/target pair and source mode.
345	func saveLastPair(source, target, engineName string) {
346		mode := "fixed"
347		if source == "auto" {
348			mode = "auto"
349		}
350		_ = state.Save(&state.State{
351			Source:     source,
352			Target:     target,
353			SourceMode: mode,
354			Engine:     engineName,
355		})
356	}

358	// runTUI launches the interactive Bubble Tea front-end and persists the last
359	// pair on exit.
360	func runTUI(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, res config.Resolved, st store.Store, source, target, pairWith string) error {
361		// A model source for the ^p model picker: the resolved LLM provider (if any).
362		var modelSrc engine.ModelLister
363		modelProvider := ""
364		if res.Provider != nil {
365			modelSrc = appcore.LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model)
366			modelProvider = res.Provider.Name
367		}
368		// Learn mode (^n) runs against a bare LLM engine; nil when no provider is
369		// configured, in which case the toggle refuses.
370		var learnEng engine.Engine
371		if res.Provider != nil {
372			learnEng = appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig(res)
373		}
374		p := tui.Params{
375			Engines:       buildEngineSet(res, eng),
376			ModelSource:   modelSrc,
377			ModelProvider: modelProvider,
378			Store:         st,
379			Source:        source,
380			Target:        target,
381			Pair:          res.Pair,
382			PairWith:      pairWith,
383			Learn:         res.Learn,
384			LearnEngine:   learnEng,
385			Model:         res.Model,
386			Preset:        res.Preset,
387			Instructions:  res.Instructions,
388			Live:          res.LiveTranslate,
389			DebounceMs:    res.DebounceMs,
390			Speaker:       tuiSpeaker(res.Cfg),
391			Foreign:       speakForeign(res.Cfg, pairWith),
392		}
393		final, err := tea.NewProgram(tui.New(ctx, p), tea.WithContext(ctx)).Run()
394		if err != nil {
395			return err
396		}
397		if res.Cfg.General.RememberLastPair {
398			if fm, ok := final.(tui.Model); ok {
399				s, t := fm.Pair()
400				saveLastPair(s, t, "")
401			}
402		}
403		return nil
404	}

406	// resolvePair fuzzy-resolves the source and target languages, printing an
407	// "(interpreted X as Y)" note on stderr when a fuzzy correction was applied.
408	func resolvePair(rawSource, rawTarget string) (source, target string) {
409		sm, _ := lang.Resolve(rawSource)
410		tm, _ := lang.Resolve(rawTarget)
411		if !sm.Exact && sm.Score > 0 && !strings.EqualFold(rawSource, sm.Code) {
412			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: interpreted source %q as %s (%s)\n", rawSource, sm.Code, sm.Name)
413		}
414		if !tm.Exact && tm.Score > 0 && !strings.EqualFold(rawTarget, tm.Code) {
415			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: interpreted target %q as %s (%s)\n", rawTarget, tm.Code, tm.Name)
416		}
417		return sm.Code, tm.Code
418	}
419	
420	// oneShot translates text once and prints the result, returning it for history.
421	//
422	// Tokens stream live to stdout only when stdout is a TTY (so `translate x | pbcopy`
423	// stays clean) and --json was not requested. Piped output is the plain translation
424	// with no ANSI; --json emits the full structured result.
425	func oneShot(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, text, source, target string, streamPref bool, preset, instructions string, pair bool, pairHome, pairAway string, learn bool) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
426		stdoutTTY := term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd()))
427		// Stream when the config asks for it on a TTY, or when --stream forces it (a
428		// piped consumer like the Raycast extension). --json/--learn are structured
429		// and never stream.
430		stream := (flagStream || (streamPref && stdoutTTY)) && !flagJSON && !learn
431	
432		req := engine.Request{
433			Text:     text,
434			Source:   source,
435			Target:   target,
436			Mode:     engine.ModeTranslate,
437			Stream:   stream,
438			Preset:   preset,
439			Extra:    instructions,
440			Pair:     pair,
441			PairHome: pairHome,
442			PairAway: pairAway,
443			Learn:    learn,
444		}
445		ch, err := eng.Translate(ctx, req)
446		if err != nil {
447			return nil, err
448		}
449	
450		// streamed tracks whether any visible token actually reached stdout. We may
451		// request streaming (stream == true) yet the engine that answers ignores it and
452		// returns a single terminal result with zero tokens — every non-streaming engine
453		// does (the dictionary/smart-dict single-word path, google, a provider that fell
454		// back to a non-streaming completion). In that case nothing was printed during
455		// draining, so the final result must still be emitted below.
456		var onTok func(string)
457		streamed := false
458		if stream {
459			onTok = func(t string) {
460				if t != "" {
461					streamed = true
462				}
463				fmt.Print(t)
464			}
465		}
466		res, err := engine.Drain(ch, onTok)
467		if err != nil {
468			if streamed {
469				fmt.Println() // terminate any partial streamed line before the error surfaces
470			}
471			return nil, err
472		}
473	
474		// Never downgrade silently: if the auto-chain fell back, say which engine
475		// failed and why, and how to switch.
476		for _, w := range res.Warnings {
477			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: %s\n", w)
478		}
479		if len(res.Warnings) > 0 && res.Learn == nil {
480			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: used %q (switch with --engine, or check the model/provider)\n", res.Engine)
481		}
482	
483		switch {
484		case flagJSON:
485			enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
486			enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
487			if err := enc.Encode(res); err != nil {
488				return nil, err
489			}
490		case res.Learn != nil:
491			fmt.Print(renderLearnCLI(res))
492		case streamed:
493			fmt.Println() // newline after the streamed tokens
494		default:
495			// Piped output, or a non-streaming engine answered a stream request with no
496			// tokens (dictionary single-word, google, …): emit the full result now.
497			fmt.Println(res.Translation)
498		}
499		return res, nil
500	}
501	
502	// runBilingual renders the "immersive" bilingual view for piped input: every
503	// original block is printed verbatim (ANSI/color intact) and a translation is shown
504	// beneath each prose block; indented command/code blocks are echoed untranslated.
505	// mode "doc" (default) translates the whole document in one context-aware call via
506	// docEng (a bare LLM); "blocks" (or a doc-mode fallback) translates each prose block
507	// in isolation via blockEng. Pair and learn routing are out of scope for this view.
508	func runBilingual(ctx context.Context, blockEng, docEng engine.Engine, raw, source, target, instructions, mode string) error {
509		blocks := bitext.Split(raw)
510		if len(blocks) == 0 {
511			return fmt.Errorf("no input on stdin")
512		}
513	
514		var translations map[int]string
515		switch mode {
516		case "blocks":
517			translations = bilingualBlocks(ctx, blockEng, blocks, source, target, instructions)
518		default: // "doc"
519			if docEng != nil {
520				if t, ok := bilingualDoc(ctx, docEng, blocks, source, target, instructions); ok {
521					translations = t
522				}
523			}
524			if translations == nil { // no LLM provider, or the doc call failed/was unparseable
525				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "translate: bilingual: doc mode unavailable, using per-block")
526				translations = bilingualBlocks(ctx, blockEng, blocks, source, target, instructions)
527			}
528		}
529	
530		dim := dimFunc(term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd())))
531		fmt.Print(bitext.Render(blocks, translations, dim))
532		return nil
533	}
534	
535	// bilingualBlocks translates each prose block in isolation (concurrent, bounded).
536	// The original strategy: works with any engine, but has no cross-block context.
537	func bilingualBlocks(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, blocks []bitext.Block, source, target, instructions string) map[int]string {
538		translations := make(map[int]string)
539		errs := make(map[int]error)
540		var mu sync.Mutex
541		var wg sync.WaitGroup
542		sem := make(chan struct{}, 5) // bound concurrent LLM calls
543	
544		for i, blk := range blocks {
545			if blk.Kind != bitext.Prose {
546				continue
547			}
548			wg.Add(1)
549			go func(i int, plain string) {
550				defer wg.Done()
551				sem <- struct{}{}
552				defer func() { <-sem }()
553	
554				// Force concise (Stream:false, Preset:"") so each block maps to exactly
555				// one translation — contextual/dictionary presets would reshape output.
556				r, err := translateOnce(ctx, eng, engine.Request{
557					Text:   plain,
558					Source: source,
559					Target: target,
560					Mode:   engine.ModeTranslate,
561					Extra:  instructions,
562				})
563				mu.Lock()
564				defer mu.Unlock()
565				if err != nil {
566					errs[i] = err
567					return
568				}
569				tr := strings.TrimSpace(r.Translation)
570				// Drop echoes (proper nouns / already-target text): nothing to add beneath.
571				if tr != "" && !strings.EqualFold(tr, strings.TrimSpace(plain)) {
572					translations[i] = tr
573				}
574			}(i, blk.Plain)
575		}
576		wg.Wait()
577	
578		// Never fail silently: report untranslated blocks (originals still printed).
579		if len(errs) > 0 {
580			var sample error
581			for _, e := range errs {
582				sample = e
583				break
584			}
585			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: %d block(s) not translated (%v)\n", len(errs), sample)
586		}
587		return translations
588	}
589	
590	// bilingualDoc translates the whole document in ONE context-aware structured call:
591	// the model sees every block (prose + code as context) and returns a JSON map of
592	// prose-segment number → translation. Returns ok=false when structured output isn't
593	// available (no LLM, error, or unparseable/empty reply) so the caller falls back.
594	func bilingualDoc(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, blocks []bitext.Block, source, target, instructions string) (map[int]string, bool) {
595		var segs []engine.Segment
596		proseBlock := make(map[int]int) // prose-segment number (1-based) → block index
597		n := 0
598		for i, blk := range blocks {
599			switch blk.Kind {
600			case bitext.Prose:
601				n++
602				proseBlock[n] = i
603				segs = append(segs, engine.Segment{Text: blk.Plain})
604			case bitext.Code:
605				segs = append(segs, engine.Segment{Text: blk.Plain, Code: true})
606			}
607		}
608		if n == 0 {
609			return map[int]string{}, true // nothing to translate
610		}
611	
612		r, err := translateOnce(ctx, eng, engine.Request{
613			Bilingual: true,
614			Segments:  segs,
615			Source:    source,
616			Target:    target,
617			Mode:      engine.ModeTranslate,
618			Extra:     instructions,
619		})
620		if err != nil {
621			debug.Logf("bilingual doc: LLM call failed: %v", err)
622			return nil, false
623		}
624		if r == nil || len(r.Bilingual) == 0 {
625			warn := ""
626			if r != nil && len(r.Warnings) > 0 {
627				warn = r.Warnings[0]
628			}
629			debug.Logf("bilingual doc: empty/unparseable structured result (warnings: %q)", warn)
630			return nil, false
631		}
632	
633		translations := make(map[int]string)
634		for num, tr := range r.Bilingual {
635			bi, ok := proseBlock[num]
636			if !ok {
637				continue
638			}
639			t := strings.TrimSpace(tr)
640			if t != "" && !strings.EqualFold(t, strings.TrimSpace(blocks[bi].Plain)) {
641				translations[bi] = t
642			}
643		}
644		return translations, true
645	}
646	
647	// translateOnce runs a single non-streaming translation and returns the result,
648	// draining the engine channel with no token callback. It is the printing-free core
649	// shared by bilingual mode.
650	func translateOnce(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, req engine.Request) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
651		ch, err := eng.Translate(ctx, req)
652		if err != nil {
653			return nil, err
654		}
655		return engine.Drain(ch, nil)
656	}
657	
658	// dimFunc returns the styler for bilingual translation lines. It dims (grey) only
659	// when stdout is a TTY and NO_COLOR is unset, so piping the output onward stays
660	// clean; otherwise it is the identity function. The original block's own ANSI is
661	// never touched — only our added translation lines are styled.
662	func dimFunc(stdoutTTY bool) func(string) string {
663		if !stdoutTTY || os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") != "" {
664			return func(s string) string { return s }
665		}
666		style := lg.NewStyle().Foreground(lg.Color("#6C6C6C"))
667		return func(s string) string { return style.Render(s) }
668	}
669	
670	// defaultAway picks the "away" (foreign) language for learn/pair mode when none is
671	// configured: English speakers default to learning zh-TW, everyone else to en. It
672	// mirrors the TUI ^g heuristic so the CLI and TUI agree.
673	func defaultAway(home string) string {
674		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(home), "en") {
675			return "zh-TW"
676		}
677		return "en"
678	}
679	
680	// renderLearnCLI formats a learn-mode result as plain text (no ANSI, pipe-safe).
681	func renderLearnCLI(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
682		l := res.Learn
683		if l == nil {
684			return res.Translation + "\n"
685		}
686		var b strings.Builder
687		if l.Direction == "correct" {
688			corrected := strings.TrimSpace(l.Corrected)
689			if corrected == "" {
690				corrected = res.Translation
691			}
692			b.WriteString("✔ " + corrected + "\n")
693			if s := strings.TrimSpace(l.Translation); s != "" {
694				b.WriteString("  ↳ " + s + "\n")
695			}
696			for _, is := range l.Issues {
697				frag := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(is.Span+" → "+is.Fix, " → "), " → "))
698				expl := strings.TrimSpace(is.Explanation)
699				line := expl
700				switch {
701				case frag != "" && expl != "":
702					line = frag + ": " + expl
703				case frag != "":
704					line = frag
705				}
706				if line != "" {
707					b.WriteString("  ✎ " + line + "\n")
708				}
709			}
710		} else {
711			tr := strings.TrimSpace(l.Translation)
712			if tr == "" {
713				tr = res.Translation
714			}
715			b.WriteString(tr + "\n")
716			for _, v := range l.Vocab {
717				head := "  • " + v.Term
718				if v.Pos != "" {
719					head += " (" + v.Pos + ")"
720				}
721				if v.Phonetic != "" {
722					head += " " + v.Phonetic
723				}
724				if v.Meaning != "" {
725					head += " — " + v.Meaning
726				}
727				b.WriteString(head + "\n")
728			}
729			for _, ex := range l.Examples {
730				b.WriteString("  ✎ " + ex.Foreign + "\n")
731				if s := strings.TrimSpace(ex.Native); s != "" {
732					b.WriteString("    ↳ " + s + "\n")
733				}
734			}
735		}
736		if s := strings.TrimSpace(l.Notes); s != "" {
737			b.WriteString("  ⓘ " + s + "\n")
738		}
739		return b.String()
740	}
741

1	
2	## Releasing & versioning
3	
4	`translate --version` is derived from Go build info (`cmd/version.go` →
5	`debug.ReadBuildInfo`), so **the version *is* the git tag** — there is no version
6	constant to edit. `go install …@latest` and the chezmoi/ansible pin both resolve
7	to a published **tag**, not to `main`; a commit on `main` does **not** reach an
8	installed binary until it is pushed **and** tagged.
9	
10	SemVer, pre-1.0 (`0.y.z`):
11	
12	- backward-compatible feature (new mode/flag, e.g. `--learn`) → bump **minor** (`0.1.0 → 0.2.0`)
13	- bug fix only → bump **patch** (`0.2.0 → 0.2.1`)
14	- breaking CLI/flag/config change → still a minor bump while `0.x`; call it out in the tag message
15	- cut **`v1.0.0`** only once the CLI/flags/config surface is considered stable
16	
17	**Config schema:** when a release adds a `config.toml` field/default, bump
18	`config.SchemaVersion` (`internal/config/config.go`). On the next run a config with
19	`schema < SchemaVersion` is **auto-migrated** — `runRoot` re-saves it so new fields land at
20	their `Default()` values (existing values preserved) and the schema is re-stamped; no re-init
21	is needed for additive changes. A **breaking** change (renamed/removed/re-meaning a key) needs
22	an explicit migration in `runRoot` before the re-save. `Save` stamps schema + the writing app
23	version (`config.Generator`, set in `cmd.Execute`).
24	
25	To ship the current `main` to this machine via chezmoi:
26	
27	1. `go test ./...` green, working tree clean.
28	2. `git push origin main`
29	3. `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "<highlights>"` && `git push origin vX.Y.Z`
30	4. verify: `go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@vX.Y.Z && translate --version` → `vX.Y.Z`
31	5. install on this machine (dotfiles repo): run `just upgrade-go` — it installs each go
32	   tool at `@latest` (= the new tag) into `~/.local/bin`. The `go_tools` pin in
33	   `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml` is only the *fresh-install floor*
34	   (its header says **don't** bump it for upgrades); `chezmoi apply`/ansible is
35	   install-only and won't move an already-installed binary. Make sure no stale copy
36	   shadows `~/.local/bin` earlier on `PATH` (e.g. a hand-built one in `~/.dotfiles/bin`).
37	
38	There is no CHANGELOG; the annotated tag message is the release note. Keep commit
39	subjects in `feat(scope): …` / `fix(scope): …` form so `git log <prev-tag>..<tag>`
40	reads as a coherent changelog.

47	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
48	
49	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
50	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
51	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
52	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
53	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
54	
55	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
56	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
57	drift is caught immediately.

59	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
60	
61	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
62	
63	   ```
64	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
65	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
66	   ```
67	
68	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
69	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
70	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.

72	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):

237	 * stdout chunks (the `--stream` flag forces streaming over a pipe). Returns a
238	 * cancel function that kills the child (call it on unmount). Whether output arrives
239	 * progressively depends on the provider — ollama streams; copilot-proxy buffers its
240	 * claude responses. `--no-history` avoids duplicating a history row the live view
241	 * may already have recorded.
242	 */
243	export function spawnTranslateStream(
244	  text: string,
245	  opts: TranslateOptions,
246	  h: StreamHandlers,
247	): () => void {
248	  const bin = resolveBinary();
249	  const args = [text, "--to", opts.to ?? "en", "--stream", "--no-history"];
250	  if (opts.engine) args.push("--engine", opts.engine);
251	  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
252	  if (opts.tier) args.push("--tier", opts.tier);
253	
254	  const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
255	  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
256	  child.stdout?.on("data", (d: Buffer | string) => h.onData(d.toString()));
257	  child.on("close", (code) => h.onDone(code));
258	  child.on("error", (err) => h.onError(err));
259	  return () => {

261	  };

41	export default function Command(
42	  props: LaunchProps<{ launchContext?: { seed?: string; to?: string } }>,
43	) {
44	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
45	  const ctx = props.launchContext;
46	  const prefDebounce = Number(prefs.liveDebounceMs);
47	  const [debounceMs, setDebounceMs] = useState(
48	    prefDebounce > 0 ? Math.max(250, prefDebounce) : 700,
49	  );
50	  const [text, setText] = useState(ctx?.seed ?? "");
51	  const [to, setTo] = useState(ctx?.to || prefs.defaultTarget || "");
52	  const [engine, setEngine] = useState("");
53	
54	  // Inherit the default target + debounce from the CLI config (~/.config/translate)
55	  // when the matching Raycast preference is empty. Falls back to "en"/700ms.
56	  useEffect(() => {
57	    if (to && prefs.liveDebounceMs) return; // nothing to inherit
58	    readConfig()
59	      .then((cfg) => {
60	        if (!to && cfg.general?.default_target)
61	          setTo(cfg.general.default_target);
62	        if (!prefs.liveDebounceMs && cfg.general?.debounce_ms)
63	          setDebounceMs(Math.max(250, cfg.general.debounce_ms));
64	      })
65	      .catch(() => {
66	        /* fall back to defaults */
67	      })
68	      .finally(() => setTo((t) => t || "en"));
69	  }, []);
70	
71	  // On first open, seed the input from the current selection (or clipboard), per the
72	  // "Prefill input from" preference — unless we were launched with a seed (from
73	  // Translate Selection). Empty when there's nothing to grab, so you can also type.
74	  useEffect(() => {
75	    if (ctx?.seed) return;
76	    const mode = prefs.prefill ?? "selection";
77	    if (mode === "none") return;
78	    (async () => {
79	      let seed = "";
80	      if (mode === "selection") {
81	        try {
82	          seed = (await getSelectedText()).trim();
83	        } catch {
84	          seed = "";
85	        }
86	      } else if (mode === "clipboard") {
87	        seed = ((await Clipboard.readText()) ?? "").trim();
88	      }
89	      if (seed) setText(seed);
90	    })();
91	  }, []);

237	  if (r.warnings?.length)

1	import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
2	
3	/** Debounce a value so an expensive call only fires after the user pauses typing. */
4	export function useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
5	  const [debounced, setDebounced] = useState(value);
6	  useEffect(() => {
7	    const id = setTimeout(() => setDebounced(value), delayMs);
8	    return () => clearTimeout(id);
9	  }, [value, delayMs]);
10	  return debounced;
11	}
12

1	import { ActionPanel, Action, Icon, List } from "@raycast/api";
2	
3	/**
4	 * A Google-style "did you mean?" section built from the engine's fuzzy dictionary
5	 * suggestions — returned (in `TranslateResult.suggestions`) when a single-word
6	 * lookup/translation has no exact match, e.g. "cononical" → ["canonical", …].
7	 * Picking one re-runs the search with the corrected term. Full sentences skip this
8	 * (they go to the LLM, which corrects typos implicitly).
9	 */
10	export function DidYouMean({
11	  suggestions,
12	  onPick,
13	}: {
14	  suggestions: string[];
15	  onPick: (s: string) => void;
16	}) {
17	  const [best, ...rest] = suggestions;
18	  return (
19	    <List.Section title="Did you mean?">
20	      {[best, ...rest].map((s, i) => (
21	        <List.Item
22	          key={s}
23	          title={s}
24	          icon={i === 0 ? Icon.Checkmark : Icon.MagnifyingGlass}
25	          accessories={i === 0 ? [{ text: "closest" }] : undefined}
26	          actions={
27	            <ActionPanel>
28	              <Action
29	                title="Use This"
30	                icon={Icon.ArrowRight}
31	                onAction={() => onPick(s)}
32	              />
33	            </ActionPanel>
34	          }
35	        />
36	      ))}
37	    </List.Section>
38	  );
39	}

13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/engine"
14	)

16	var (
17		flagDefinePlain bool
18		flagDefineSmart bool
19	)
20	
21	func newDefineCmd() *cobra.Command {
22		c := &cobra.Command{
23			Use:   "define <word>",
24			Short: "Look up a word in the dictionary (exact → fuzzy → LLM)",
25			Args:  cobra.MinimumNArgs(1),
26			RunE:  runDefine,
27		}
28		c.Flags().BoolVar(&flagDefinePlain, "plain", false, "force the offline dictionary (no LLM fallback)")
29		c.Flags().BoolVar(&flagDefineSmart, "smart", false, "force smart-dict (LLM fallback on a miss)")
30		return c
31	}
32	
33	func runDefine(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
34		cfg, _, err := config.Load()
35		if err != nil {
36			return err
37		}
38		if !cfg.Dict.Enabled {
39			return fmt.Errorf("dictionary is disabled in %s", config.Path())
40		}
41		res := cfg.Resolve(overrides(), config.ModeCLI)
42		de := appcore.DefineEngine(res, flagDefinePlain, flagDefineSmart)
43		word := strings.Join(args, " ")
44	
45		ch, err := de.Translate(cmd.Context(), engine.Request{Text: word, Mode: engine.ModeDict, Stream: false})
46		if err != nil {
47			return err
48		}
49		res2, err := engine.Drain(ch, nil)
50		if err != nil {
51			return err
52		}
53	
54		if flagJSON {
55			enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
56			enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
57			return enc.Encode(res2)
58		}
59		// Surface an LLM-fallback downgrade the same way the CLI translate path does.
60		for _, w := range res2.Warnings {
61			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: %s\n", w)
62		}
63		fmt.Print(renderDict(res2))
64		if flagSpeak && cfg.TTS.Enabled {
65			speakDefine(cmd.Context(), cfg, res2)
66		}
67		return nil
68	}
69	
70	// renderDict formats a dictionary result as plain text (no ANSI, pipe-safe).
71	func renderDict(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
72		d := res.Dictionary
73		if d == nil {
74			if len(res.Suggestions) > 0 {
75				return "no exact match — did you mean: " + strings.Join(res.Suggestions, ", ") + "\n"
76			}
77			return res.Translation + "\n"
78		}
79		var b strings.Builder
80		head := d.Word
81		if d.Phonetic != "" {
82			head += "  " + d.Phonetic
83		}
84		b.WriteString(head + "\n")
85		for _, m := range d.Meanings {
86			b.WriteString("  " + m.PartOfSpeech + "\n")
87			for i, def := range m.Definitions {
88				if i >= 4 { // cap definitions per part of speech
89					break
90				}
91				b.WriteString("    • " + def.Text + "\n")
92				if def.Example != "" {
93					b.WriteString("      \"" + def.Example + "\"\n")
94				}
95			}
96		}
97		return b.String()
98	}

22			Short: "Show recent translation history",
23			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
24				recs, err := loadHistory(cmd, func(st store.Store) ([]store.Record, error) {
25					return st.Recent(cmd.Context(), limit)
26				})
27				if err != nil {

29				}
30				return printRecords(recs, tsv)
31			},

34		c.Flags().BoolVar(&tsv, "tsv", false, "tab-separated output (for scripting / tv)")

41				q := strings.Join(args, " ")
42				recs, err := loadHistory(cmd, func(st store.Store) ([]store.Record, error) {
43					return st.Search(cmd.Context(), q, limit)
44				})
45				if err != nil {

48				return printRecords(recs, tsv)
49			},
50		}
51		search.Flags().IntVar(&limit, "limit", 20, "max entries")
52		search.Flags().BoolVar(&tsv, "tsv", false, "tab-separated output")
53		c.AddCommand(search)

57	// loadHistory opens the store and runs a query, handling the disabled case.
58	func loadHistory(cmd *cobra.Command, query func(store.Store) ([]store.Record, error)) ([]store.Record, error) {
59		cfg, _, err := config.Load()
60		if err != nil {
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		st := openStore(cfg)
64		if st == nil {
65			return nil, fmt.Errorf("history is disabled in %s", config.Path())
66		}
67		defer st.Close()
68		return query(st)
69	}
70	
71	func printRecords(recs []store.Record, tsv bool) error {
72		if flagJSON {
73			enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
74			enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
75			return enc.Encode(recs)
76		}
77		if tsv {
78			for _, r := range recs {
79				fmt.Printf("%s\t%s\t%s>%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n",
80					r.ID, r.TS.Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05"),
81					r.SourceLang, r.TargetLang, r.Engine,
82					escapeTSV(r.Input), escapeTSV(r.Output))
83			}
84			return nil
85		}
86		w := tabwriter.NewWriter(os.Stdout, 0, 2, 2, ' ', 0)
87		for _, r := range recs {
88			fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s→%s\t%s\t→ %s\t(%s)\n",
89				r.SourceLang, r.TargetLang, oneline(r.Input, 40), oneline(r.Output, 40), r.Engine)
90		}
91		return w.Flush()
92	}
93	
94	func escapeTSV(s string) string {
95		r := strings.NewReplacer("\t", " ", "\n", " ", "\r", " ")
96		return r.Replace(s)
97	}
98	
99	func oneline(s string, n int) string {
100		s = strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimSpace(s), "\n", " ")
101		rs := []rune(s)
102		if len(rs) <= n {
103			return s
104		}
105		return string(rs[:n-1]) + "…"
106	}

17			Short: "Show or locate the configuration",
18		}
19		c.AddCommand(
20			&cobra.Command{
21				Use:   "path",
22				Short: "Print the config file path",
23				RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
24					fmt.Println(config.Path())
25					return nil
26				},
27			},
28			&cobra.Command{
29				Use:   "show",
30				Short: "Print the effective configuration as TOML (or JSON with --json)",
31				RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
32					cfg, _, err := config.Load()
33					if err != nil {
34						return err
35					}
36					b, err := toml.Marshal(cfg)
37					if err != nil {
38						return err
39					}
40					if flagJSON {
41						// Round-trip TOML → map → JSON so the JSON keys match the TOML
42						// (snake_case, e.g. general.default_target) without adding json
43						// tags to every config struct. Lets other front-ends (the Raycast
44						// extension) read the effective config.
45						var m map[string]any
46						if err := toml.Unmarshal(b, &m); err != nil {
47							return err
48						}
49						enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
50						enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
51						return enc.Encode(m)
52					}
53					_, err = os.Stdout.Write(b)
54					return err
55				},
56			},
57		)
58		return c
59	}

26				fmt.Printf("%s -> %s (%s) [%s, score %.2f]\n", args[0], m.Code, m.Name, kind, m.Score)
27				for _, a := range alts {
28					fmt.Printf("  ~ %s (%s) %.2f\n", a.Code, a.Name, a.Score)
29				}
30				return nil
31			},
32		})
33		return c
34	}
35
```

```text
1	# Raycast integration — reference
2	
3	How `translate` plugs into [Raycast](https://raycast.com), the options we
4	weighed, how the shipped integration works, and how it compares to existing
5	translation extensions. This is present-tense reference reading; the actual code
6	lives in [`../raycast/`](../raycast/), and store-publishing is tracked in
7	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
8	
9	**Core principle: reuse the binary, don't reimplement.** Every tier below shells
10	out to the existing `translate` CLI (`--json`) and renders the result. No
11	translation, engine, or dictionary logic is duplicated in TypeScript/bash.
12	
13	## Integration tiers
14	
15	Raycast offers four ways to surface functionality. We ship the middle two.
16	
17	| Tier | Reuses binary? | Effort | Selection → translate | Persisted defaults | Rich UI / history | Streaming | Distribution |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **Quick Link** | ✗ (can't exec) | 5 min | via deeplink only | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | launcher only |
20	| **Script Command** (bash) — *shipped* | ✓ | ~0.5 h | ✗ (needs `pbpaste`) | ✗ (no prefs) | ✗ (plain text) | only `fullOutput` | Add Script Directory |
21	| **TS Extension** (`@raycast/api`) — *shipped* | ✓ | 1–2 d | ✓ `getSelectedText()` | ✓ preferences | ✓ List/Detail/Actions | ✓ (manual `spawn`) | `npm run dev` / store |
22	| **AI Extension** (tools) | ✓ | +0.5 d | AI-orchestrated | — | AI Chat | `AI.ask` | store; **Pro-gated** |
23	
24	- **Quick Links** open a URL/file/app/`raycast://` deeplink — they have no
25	  shell-exec surface, so they can't run the CLI directly. Useful only as a hotkey
26	  that deeplinks into a real command.
27	- **AI Extensions** expose "tools" the Raycast AI can call. Feasible (a tool file
28	  can `execFile` the binary and return its `--json`), but the AI API requires
29	  **Raycast Pro**, so it's an additive Pro-only layer — deferred.
30	
31	## How Raycast extensions work
32	
33	- **Manifest** (`package.json`): a `commands[]` array; each command has a
34	  required `mode`:
35	  - `view` — default-exports a React (TSX) component (our `Translate`).
36	  - `no-view` — default-exports an async function; runs and exits, no UI
37	    (our `Translate Selection` → `getSelectedText` → `Clipboard.paste` + `showHUD`).
38	  - `menu-bar` — a persistent `MenuBarExtra` (not used yet).
39	- **Running the binary:** extensions run in a Node runtime, so `child_process`
40	  works. We use `execFile` (typed wrapper in
41	  [`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
42	  rather than the `useExec` hook, because `useExec` buffers with a 10 s default
43	  timeout that LLM engines exceed (and its `timeout: 0` is coerced back to 10000).
44	  The CLI's **`--stream` flag** forces token streaming even when stdout is piped
45	  (which Raycast always is; without it the CLI treats non-TTY as buffered). A
46	  streaming `Detail` view can spawn `translate … --stream` and append `stdout`
47	  chunks into React state bound to `Detail.markdown`. Caveat: visible progressive
48	  output depends on the provider — ollama streams; **copilot-proxy currently buffers
49	  its claude `/v1/messages` responses**, so the result appears after first-token
50	  latency. The default live view uses `--json` (buffered, structured), which returns
51	  fast enough.
52	- **Preferences** (`getPreferenceValues()`): persisted per-extension settings —
53	  our `binaryPath`, `defaultTarget`, `engine`, `tier`.
54	- **Input/UI:** `getSelectedText()` (frontmost app's selection),
55	  `Clipboard.copy/paste`, `Action.CopyToClipboard`/`Action.Paste`; `List` +
56	  `List.Dropdown` (searchBarAccessory, `storeValue` to remember the last target);
57	  `Detail`/`List.Item.Detail` with `.Metadata` for structured fields; `showHUD`/
58	  `showToast` for feedback.
59	- **Tooling:** the `ray` CLI (ships in the extension's dev deps). `ray develop`
60	  (`npm run dev`) registers the extension with the running Raycast app and
61	  hot-reloads; **it persists in root search after you stop dev** — no store
62	  publish needed for personal use. `ray build`/`ray lint` type-check and lint.
63	
64	## Gotchas (learned the hard way)
65	
66	- **launchd PATH:** Raycast launches under launchd and does *not* inherit your
67	  shell PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `ENOENT` / `command not found`.
68	  Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path (preference first, then probe
69	  `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`). Always test
70	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
71	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
72	- **HOME / config, not shell env:** the CLI reads providers/keys from
73	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, *not* environment variables. A key exported
74	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd — put it in the config (`translate init`).
75	  We pass `HOME` through so the CLI finds its config.
76	- **Exit code is 0 even on engine failure** (auto-fallback), so we read
77	  `warnings[]` from `--json` rather than branching on exit codes. The extension
78	  surfaces warnings in the Detail pane / HUD; the plain-text scripts don't.
79	- **Extension icons must be a real PNG** (512×512) — emoji icons work only for
80	  Script Commands. `ray build`/`lint` complains otherwise.
81	
82	## Competitive landscape (2026)
83	
84	The Raycast translation category is crowded, but the field is almost entirely
85	remote-API/cloud-LLM wrappers configured via extension preferences.
86	
87	| Extension | Backend | Streaming | TTS | History | Offline dict |
88	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
89	| gebeto/translate (Google) | Google web (keyless) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
90	| tisfeng/Easydict | 10 remote providers + Apple `say`/Shortcuts | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ (remote) |
91	| douo/openai-translator | multi-LLM incl. Ollama / custom endpoint | ✓ | ✗ (roadmap) | ✓ | ✗ |
92	| deepcast / itranslate | DeepL / multi (BYO API key) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
93	| Raycast built-in Translate | unstated | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (Pro-gated) |
94	
95	**What `translate` does that they don't:**
96	
97	- **Shells out to a dedicated local translator CLI** — no surveyed extension
98	  wraps a standalone translator binary (Easydict shells to `osascript`/Apple
99	  Shortcuts; none to a CLI like this).
100	- **Automatic multi-engine failover** — competitors that support multiple engines
101	  do *parallel aggregation*, not "try A, on failure fall back to B".
102	- **Offline CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries** via `translate define` — all
103	  competitors' dictionaries are remote.
104	- **Unified, searchable history** (`translate history [search]`).
105	- **Free local TTS** (`--speak`) — note openai-translator lists TTS as an
106	  unshipped roadmap item, so this is a real gap.
107	- **Fuzzy language resolution** (`translate lang resolve`, `chinees → zh`).
108	
109	Frame differentiation as **offline-resilient + auto-fallback + unified history**,
110	*not* "local LLM" (openai-translator already reaches Ollama) and *not* "study
111	modes" (Anki / Vocabulary Builder already exist in the store).
112	
113	## How ours is built
114	
115	- **Script Commands** — [`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/):
116	  `translate-text` (dropdown language + text, `fullOutput`), `translate-and-copy`
117	  (`silent`, copies; blank arg → clipboard), `define-word`. Install:
118	  `just raycast-scripts`, then add the directory in Raycast once.
119	- **TS extension** — [`../raycast/extension/`](../raycast/extension/): commands
120	  `translate` (view: type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
121	  Copy/Paste/Speak, typo "did you mean?" suggestions, opt-in selection prefill),
122	  `translate-selection` (no-view:
123	  grabs the selection/clipboard and opens Translate prefilled via `launchCommand` —
124	  editable, not blind-paste), `define` (view: dictionary lookup +
125	  LLM fallback + "did you mean" suggestions), and `history` (view: browse/search
126	  past translations). All share `src/lib/translate.ts` (binary resolve + typed
127	  `execFile` wrappers mirroring `internal/engine/engine.go`'s `TranslateResult`).
128	  Run: `just raycast-dev` (`build`/`lint` variants exist). Live translate is
129	  debounced + abortable to avoid an LLM call per keystroke, with an opt-in `⌘↵`
130	  streaming view (`spawnTranslateStream` → `translate … --stream` → live `Detail`).
131	  Typo suggestions reuse the engine's fuzzy `suggestions[]` (a shared
132	  `did-you-mean.tsx` component) — no CLI change; single-word lookups route to the
133	  offline dict, full sentences to the LLM which corrects implicitly. Default target,
134	  live-debounce, and tier are inherited from the CLI config (`config show --json`)
135	  when the matching Raycast preference is empty, so `config.toml` is the single
136	  source of truth (a Raycast preference overrides it).
137	
138	## Publishing & distribution
139	
140	The journey from local development to the store, and why we default to
141	local/personal for now.
142	
143	### Three distribution paths
144	
145	| Path | Review | Audience | How | Our stance |
146	|---|---|---|---|---|
147	| **Local dev** | none | just you | `just raycast-dev` (`ray develop`) — persists in root search after you stop dev | **current default** |
148	| **Private / org store** | none (org-gated) | your Raycast org | set `owner` in package.json → `npm run publish`; needs Raycast Pro/Team | option if sharing to a team |
149	| **Public store** | **human review** | everyone | `npm run publish` opens a PR to `raycast/extensions` → CI + Raycast-team review → merge auto-publishes | deferred → [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md) |
150	
151	### It is *not* like PyPI
152	
153	PyPI is self-service: register + `twine upload`, published instantly, no review.
154	The Raycast **public** store is curated — closer to Homebrew core:
155	
156	- `npm run publish` (= `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`) **authenticates with
157	  GitHub** and auto-opens a pull request into `github.com/raycast/extensions`.
158	- Automated CI checks run, then the **Raycast team reviews** and "request[s] changes
159	  when required"; on merge it auto-publishes. Turnaround is days, not seconds.
160	- Auth is **GitHub** (for the PR). Your **Raycast account** only supplies the
161	  validated `author` handle (ours: `da-wei_lee`).
162	
163	### Public-store requirements (checklist)
164	
165	Verified against developers.raycast.com. `✓` = done in this repo.
166	
167	- `✓` `author` = registered Raycast username; `license: "MIT"`; ≥1 category;
168	  one-sentence description; `platforms`; `package-lock.json`; `npm run build` +
169	  `ray lint` clean.
170	- `✓` **512×512 PNG icon** that reads in light + dark (not the default Raycast icon).
171	- `✓` **`CHANGELOG.md`** at the extension root (h2 headers; `{PR_MERGE_DATE}` placeholder).
172	- `✓` **`README.md`** at the extension root (setup/onboarding; media under a top-level
173	  `media/` folder).
174	- `☐` **≥3 (max 6) screenshots at 2000×1250 PNG** — captured from the *running*
175	  extension (a GUI step; not scriptable here).
176	- `☐` `npm run publish` (GitHub auth) + choose public vs private.
177	
178	### The binary-dependency hurdle
179	
180	The store guideline *"Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads"* is exactly
181	our case — the extension needs a user-installed `translate` (brew / `go install`).
182	"Calling known system binaries" is allowed, but a custom go-install CLI is a gray
183	area reviewers may push back on. Mitigations already in place:
184	
185	- Extension `README.md` documents the dependency + install commands.
186	- A graceful **binary-not-found onboarding** view (`src/lib/binary-not-found.tsx`) with
187	  copyable install commands + a jump to preferences — instead of a bare error.
188	- We do **not** bundle the ~22 MB Go binary (store discourages "heavy" binaries;
189	  shipping release binaries is a separate item — `backlog/release-binaries.md`).
190	
191	This friction is why the public store is deferred and local/private is the current
192	path; the analysis lives in [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
193	
194	## References
195	
196	- Raycast API — manifest, commands, UI: https://developers.raycast.com/
197	- `useExec`: https://developers.raycast.com/utilities/react-hooks/useexec
198	- AI Extensions: https://developers.raycast.com/ai
199	- Script Commands: https://github.com/raycast/script-commands
200	- Prepare / Publish / Teams: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store
201
```

1	# Publish the Raycast extension to the store
2	
3	**Status**: P? — local-dev shipped; publish deferred
4	**Effort**: L
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` P? · `raycast/extension/` · [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) · [homebrew-distribution.md](homebrew-distribution.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07. The Raycast integration shipped as two local tracks (`raycast/script-commands/`
10	bash + `raycast/extension/` TypeScript). The TS extension runs via `just raycast-dev`
11	(`ray develop`) and **persists in root search after dev stops**, so personal use needs
12	no store at all. The open question is whether — and how — to distribute it beyond this
13	machine.
14	
15	## Investigation
16	
17	- **Calling a user-installed binary is a sanctioned pattern** ("✅ Calling known system
18	  binaries"). The store's hard rule targets *bundling opaque/heavy binaries*, which we
19	  don't do — we shell out to a Homebrew/`go install` `translate`.
20	- **Soft guideline friction**: the store discourages requiring users to manually install
21	  external tools ("avoid... automate where possible"). Our binary dependency is exactly
22	  that — advisory, not an auto-reject, but the most likely reviewer comment. Mitigate
23	  with graceful binary detection + a "not installed → install instructions" onboarding
24	  view + README.
25	- **Private org store** (Raycast for Teams/Pro): publish via `owner` in package.json +
26	  `npm run publish`; visible only to org members, **no public human review**. Best fit if
27	  distributing to a controlled group who all have the binary.
28	- **Public store requirements**: `author` = a *registered Raycast username* (currently
29	  fails `ray lint` — `daviddwlee84` 404s against Raycast's user API), `license: MIT`
30	  (wrapper only; the Go binary's license is untouched since we don't bundle it), a custom
31	  512×512 icon (the current one is a placeholder), ≥3 screenshots (2000×1250), a
32	  `CHANGELOG.md`, a Title-Case category, `package-lock.json`, and `ray lint` clean.
33	- **No telemetry, no Keychain**. If published, expose the openrouter API key via the
34	  Raycast preferences API (`required: true`), not by reading `config.toml`.
35	- **Platform**: mark `platforms: ["macOS"]` (already set) — the binary shell-out doesn't
36	  work on Raycast's iOS/Windows clients.
37	
38	## Options considered
39	
40	| Option | What | Verdict |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| A. Local dev only (personal) | `ray develop`, per-machine, no review | current default — done |
43	| B. Private org store (Pro/Team) | `owner` + `npm run publish`, internal-only | best if sharing to a team; needs Pro |
44	| C. Public store | PR to raycast/extensions, automated + human review | widest reach; expect binary-dependency review friction |
45	
46	## Current blocker / open questions
47	
48	- Is public publication worth it given the crowded category, or is local/private enough?
49	  (Differentiators are real — see [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md)
50	  competitive section — but the binary dependency is a review headwind.)
51	- What's the binary-not-found onboarding UX (detection + actionable install view)?
52	- Register/confirm the Raycast `author` handle before any publish (blocks `ray lint`).
53	
54	## Decision (if any)
55	
56	`2026-07 deferred` — ship the local-dev extension first and dogfood it; **private/
57	personal is the current path**, public store stays deferred.
58	
59	Publish prerequisites now IN PLACE: registered author (`da-wei_lee`), `license: MIT`,
60	a designed 512×512 icon (`assets/extension-icon.png`, source `.svg`), `CHANGELOG.md`,
61	an extension `README.md`, and a graceful binary-not-found onboarding view. Remaining
62	before a public PR: **3–6 screenshots (2000×1250, GUI capture)** and a decision on the
63	binary-dependency review friction (a private org store sidesteps it entirely). The
64	full dev→publish process is documented in
65	[../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) "Publishing & distribution".

70	- Publish: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/publish-an-extension
71	- Teams / private extensions: https://developers.raycast.com/teams/publish-a-private-extension

1	# Frequency-aware "did you mean" suggestion ranking
2	
3	**Status**: P? — needs a spike
4	**Effort**: S–M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` P? · `internal/engine/{smartdict,ecdict}.go` · `raycast/extension/src/lib/did-you-mean.tsx` · [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07, surfaced while adding the Raycast "did you mean?" UX. The dictionary engine
10	returns fuzzy `suggestions[]` for single-word typos (consumed by Raycast
11	Translate/Define, and the CLI `define`). Ranking is **edit-distance only**, so the
12	obvious correction doesn't always surface first:
13	
14	- `recieve` → `[relieve, believe, reachieve, recarve, recede, receive, recidive]`
15	  (`receive` is 6th)
16	- `cononical` → `[canonical, acanonical, canonicals, …]` (`canonical` happens to be 1st)
17	
18	Google ranks by frequency ("Showing results for **canonical**"). We want the common
19	word on top.
20	
21	## Investigation
22	
23	- **ECDICT has frequency data** — `frq`, `bnc` columns (+ collins/oxford flags). A
24	  re-rank by `(editDistance asc, frequency desc)` would float common words up.
25	- Suggestions are produced in `internal/engine` (smart-dict / ecdict fuzzy lookup), so
26	  re-ranking there benefits **all** frontends at once — CLI `define`, Raycast, and the
27	  new `serve` / `mcp` adapters.
28	- `TranslateResult.SuggestDistance` exists but is `json:"-"` (not serialized). Exposing
29	  it (e.g. `suggest_distance`) would let a frontend auto-apply a confident correction
30	  ("Showing results for X · search instead for Y", Google-style) instead of only listing.
31	
32	## Options considered
33	
34	| Option | What | Verdict |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| A. Edit-distance only (current) | fuzzy by Levenshtein | simple; the right word is often not on top |
37	| B. Frequency-weighted re-rank | sort by (distance, then ECDICT `frq`/`bnc`) | best value; small change in the dict engine; helps every frontend |
38	| C. Expose `SuggestDistance` in `--json` | frontend decides auto-correct vs. list | pairs with B for a Google-style "showing results for X" |
39	| D. Keyboard-adjacency (qwerty) weighting | typo model | marginal over B; more complex |
40	
41	## Current blocker / open questions
42	
43	- Does the bundled ECDICT actually populate `frq`/`bnc` for enough headwords? (verify)
44	- Chinese suggestions are prefix matches with no distance/frequency — leave as-is, or
45	  pinyin/stroke rank?
46	- Threshold/cap: only show suggestions within distance N; how many to return.
47	
48	## Decision (if any)
49	
50	`2026-07 deferred` — the extension already surfaces the full list (usable, just not
51	ideally ordered). Do **B** (and optionally **C**) when polishing the did-you-mean UX.
52	Frontends need no change for B; C would let Translate/Define auto-apply the top
53	correction.
54	
55	## References
56	
57	- ECDICT schema (`frq`/`bnc`/collins/oxford): https://github.com/skywind3000/ECDICT
58	- Raycast did-you-mean component: `raycast/extension/src/lib/did-you-mean.tsx`
59
```

2	import { ActionPanel, Action, Icon, List, showHUD } from "@raycast/api";
3	import { usePromise } from "@raycast/utils";
4	import {
5	  runDefine,
6	  speak,
7	  isBinaryMissing,
8	  TranslateResult,
9	} from "./lib/translate";
10	import { useDebouncedValue } from "./lib/hooks";
11	import { BinaryNotFound } from "./lib/binary-not-found";
12	import { DidYouMean } from "./lib/did-you-mean";
13	
14	export default function Command() {
15	  const [word, setWord] = useState("");
16	  const debounced = useDebouncedValue(word, 500);
17	  const abortable = useRef<AbortController>();
18	
19	  const { data, isLoading, error } = usePromise(
20	    async (w: string): Promise<TranslateResult | undefined> => {
21	      const trimmed = w.trim();
22	      if (!trimmed) return undefined;
23	      return runDefine(trimmed, abortable.current?.signal);
24	    },
25	    [debounced],
26	    { abortable },
27	  );
28	
29	  const pending = word.trim().length > 0 && word.trim() !== debounced.trim();
30	  const showSuggestions =
31	    !!data && !data.dictionary && !!data.suggestions?.length;
32	
33	  return (
34	    <List
35	      isLoading={isLoading || pending}
36	      searchText={word}
37	      onSearchTextChange={setWord}
38	      searchBarPlaceholder="Look up a word…"
39	      isShowingDetail={!!data && !showSuggestions}
40	    >
41	      {error ? (
42	        isBinaryMissing(error) ? (
43	          <BinaryNotFound />
44	        ) : (
45	          <List.EmptyView
46	            icon={Icon.Warning}
47	            title="Lookup failed"
48	            description={String(error.message ?? error)}
49	          />
50	        )
51	      ) : !data ? (
52	        <List.EmptyView
53	          icon={Icon.Book}
54	          title="Define"
55	          description="Type a word to look it up."
56	        />
57	      ) : showSuggestions ? (
58	        <DidYouMean suggestions={data.suggestions!} onPick={setWord} />
59	      ) : (
60	        <List.Item
61	          title={data.dictionary?.word ?? word}
62	          subtitle={data.engine}
63	          detail={
64	            <List.Item.Detail
65	              markdown={renderDefine(data, word)}
66	              metadata={renderMetadata(data)}
67	            />
68	          }
69	          actions={
70	            <ActionPanel>
71	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
72	                title="Copy Definition"
73	                content={data.translation}
74	              />
75	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
76	                title="Copy Word"
77	                content={data.dictionary?.word ?? word}
78	                shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd"], key: "i" }}
79	              />
80	              <Action
81	                title="Speak"
82	                icon={Icon.SpeakerHigh}
83	                onAction={async () => {
84	                  speak(
85	                    data.dictionary?.word ?? word.trim(),
86	                    data.target || "en",
87	                  );
88	                  await showHUD("Speaking…");
89	                }}
90	              />
91	            </ActionPanel>
92	          }
93	        />
94	      )}
95	    </List>

99	function renderDefine(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
100	  const d = r.dictionary;
101	  if (d) {
102	    const lines = [`# ${d.word}`];
103	    if (d.phonetic) lines.push(`*/${d.phonetic}/*`);
104	    lines.push("");
105	    for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
106	      lines.push(`## ${m.part_of_speech}`);
107	      for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) {
108	        lines.push(
109	          `- ${def.definition}${def.example ? `\n  - _${def.example}_` : ""}`,
110	        );
111	      }
112	      lines.push("");
113	    }
114	    return lines.join("\n");
115	  }
116	  // No dictionary entry — LLM fallback lives in `translation`.
117	  const lines = [`# ${word}`, "", r.translation, ""];
118	  if (r.warnings?.length) lines.push("---", ...r.warnings.map((w) => `> ${w}`));
119	  return lines.join("\n");
120	}
121	
122	function renderMetadata(r: TranslateResult) {
123	  return (
124	    <List.Item.Detail.Metadata>
125	      <List.Item.Detail.Metadata.Label title="Engine" text={r.engine ?? "—"} />
126	      {r.dictionary?.phonetic ? (
127	        <List.Item.Detail.Metadata.Label

130	        />
131	      ) : null}
132	      {r.model ? (

134	      ) : null}
135	      {r.dictionary?.source_url ? (

138	          target={r.dictionary.source_url}
139	          text="link"
140	        />
141	      ) : null}

17	 * clipboard, and to an empty Translate when there's nothing to grab. An optional

30	    await launchCommand({

33	      context: { seed, to: props.arguments?.to || undefined },

1	import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
2	import { ActionPanel, Action, Detail } from "@raycast/api";
3	import { spawnTranslateStream } from "./translate";
4	
5	/** A pushed Detail that streams `translate … --stream` output token-by-token.
6	 *  Opt-in from the Translate view (⌘↵) — useful for long text and streaming
7	 *  engines; on a buffering provider it simply appears after first-token latency. */
8	export function StreamView({
9	  text,
10	  to,
11	  engine,
12	}: {
13	  text: string;
14	  to: string;
15	  engine?: string;
16	}) {
17	  const [md, setMd] = useState("");
18	  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
19	  const acc = useRef("");
20	
21	  useEffect(() => {
22	    acc.current = "";
23	    setMd("");
24	    setIsLoading(true);
25	    const cancel = spawnTranslateStream(
26	      text,
27	      { to, engine: engine || undefined },
28	      {
29	        onData: (chunk) => {
30	          acc.current += chunk;
31	          setMd(acc.current);
32	        },
33	        onDone: () => setIsLoading(false),
34	        onError: (err) => {
35	          acc.current += `\n\n> error: ${err.message}`;
36	          setMd(acc.current);
37	          setIsLoading(false);
38	        },
39	      },
40	    );
41	    return cancel;
42	  }, [text, to, engine]);
43	
44	  return (
45	    <Detail
46	      isLoading={isLoading}
47	      markdown={md || "…"}
48	      navigationTitle={`Translate → ${to}`}
49	      actions={
50	        <ActionPanel>
51	          <Action.CopyToClipboard title="Copy Translation" content={md} />
52	          <Action.Paste title="Paste Translation" content={md} />
53	        </ActionPanel>
54	      }
55	    />
56	  );
57	}
