1	
2	## Releasing & versioning
3	
4	`translate --version` is derived from Go build info (`cmd/version.go` →
5	`debug.ReadBuildInfo`), so **the version *is* the git tag** — there is no version
6	constant to edit. `go install …@latest` and the chezmoi/ansible pin both resolve
7	to a published **tag**, not to `main`; a commit on `main` does **not** reach an
8	installed binary until it is pushed **and** tagged.
9	
10	SemVer, pre-1.0 (`0.y.z`):
11	
12	- backward-compatible feature (new mode/flag, e.g. `--learn`) → bump **minor** (`0.1.0 → 0.2.0`)
13	- bug fix only → bump **patch** (`0.2.0 → 0.2.1`)
14	- breaking CLI/flag/config change → still a minor bump while `0.x`; call it out in the tag message
15	- cut **`v1.0.0`** only once the CLI/flags/config surface is considered stable
16	
17	**Config schema:** when a release adds a `config.toml` field/default, bump
18	`config.SchemaVersion` (`internal/config/config.go`). On the next run a config with
19	`schema < SchemaVersion` is **auto-migrated** — `runRoot` re-saves it so new fields land at
20	their `Default()` values (existing values preserved) and the schema is re-stamped; no re-init
21	is needed for additive changes. A **breaking** change (renamed/removed/re-meaning a key) needs
22	an explicit migration in `runRoot` before the re-save. `Save` stamps schema + the writing app
23	version (`config.Generator`, set in `cmd.Execute`).
24	
25	To ship the current `main` to this machine via chezmoi:
26	
27	1. `go test ./...` green, working tree clean.
28	2. `git push origin main`
29	3. `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "<highlights>"` && `git push origin vX.Y.Z`
30	4. verify: `go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@vX.Y.Z && translate --version` → `vX.Y.Z`
31	5. install on this machine (dotfiles repo): run `just upgrade-go` — it installs each go
32	   tool at `@latest` (= the new tag) into `~/.local/bin`. The `go_tools` pin in
33	   `dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml` is only the *fresh-install floor*
34	   (its header says **don't** bump it for upgrades); `chezmoi apply`/ansible is
35	   install-only and won't move an already-installed binary. Make sure no stale copy
36	   shadows `~/.local/bin` earlier on `PATH` (e.g. a hand-built one in `~/.dotfiles/bin`).
37	
38	There is no CHANGELOG; the annotated tag message is the release note. Keep commit
39	subjects in `feat(scope): …` / `fix(scope): …` form so `git log <prev-tag>..<tag>`
40	reads as a coherent changelog.
41	
42	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance -->
43	<!-- Snippet for the project's agent contract file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md /
44	     similar). The bundled scripts/init.sh appends this between sentinel
45	     markers; safe to re-run. -->
46	
47	### Long-term backlog → `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
48	
49	When the user surfaces an idea explicitly **not** being implemented this
50	session (signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
51	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來"), add an entry to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using
52	the priority + effort tag schema. Do **not** create new `ROADMAP.md` /
53	`IDEAS.md` / `BACKLOG.md` files — `TODO.md` is the single index.
54	
55	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates the format. Run it
56	(`scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md`) after editing so syntax
57	drift is caught immediately.
58	
59	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
60	
61	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
62	
63	   ```
64	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
65	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
66	   ```
67	
68	   Inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane and
69	   re-runs the validator. Add `--backlog` to also scaffold
70	   `backlog/<slug>.md` from the bundled template.
71	
72	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
73	
74	   ```
75	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
76	   ```
77	
78	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox", run
79	   `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`. It prompts for the missing fields per loose
80	   line and calls `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs
81	   that only formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
82	
83	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh; run
84	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
85	
86	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` companion doc when the item meets any of:
87	
88	- carries a `P?` tag (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
89	- captures a paused troubleshooting session that you intend to fix later
90	  (preserve the error trace + root cause analysis before context evaporates)
91	- weighs multiple options (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
92	- is `[L]` or `[XL]` (architectural; needs design before code)
93	
94	`[S]` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the `TODO.md` line is
95	usually enough. See [`backlog/README.md`](backlog/README.md) for the full
96	template and "when to add a doc" rules.
97	
98	When implementing a `TODO.md` item, in the same commit:
99	
100	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`
101	   to move the entry into `## Done` with the dated syntax and re-validate.
102	2. Mark the corresponding `backlog/<slug>.md` (if any) `Status: shipped`
103	   and keep it as a historical record (don't delete — future-you may
104	   revisit adjacent decisions).
105	
106	`backlog/` is excluded from N/A (no packaging — these files stay in the repo) (see N/A); it
107	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
108	
109	### Past pitfalls → `pitfalls/`
110	
111	When you spend more than ~15 minutes debugging something that wasn't
112	googleable and the fix is non-obvious, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
113	capturing:
114	
115	1. **Verbatim symptom** — copy-paste error messages exactly, do not
116	   paraphrase (preserves grep-ability for future-you / future agent)
117	2. **Root cause** — why this happens (with source / docs / upstream issue link)
118	3. **Workaround** — copy-pasteable commands or config diff
119	4. **Prevention** — how to avoid stepping on this again
120	
121	Title the doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause (you'll search by what
122	you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned). See
123	[`pitfalls/README.md`](pitfalls/README.md) for the full template and
124	when-to-add rules.
125	
126	**Pitfall vs Hard invariant**: a pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant in
127	this file when it (a) recurs across machines/agents/sessions despite being
128	documented, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
129	enough that "remember to do X" isn't safe. When graduating, leave the
130	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the new
131	invariant.
132	
133	`pitfalls/` is excluded from N/A (no packaging — these files stay in the repo) (see N/A) and
134	**not** auto-redacted; review for secrets before committing.
135	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:agent-guidance --> (end)

13	func newDictCmd() *cobra.Command {
14		c := &cobra.Command{
15			Use:   "dict",
16			Short: "Manage the local bilingual dictionary (CC-CEDICT + ECDICT)",
17		}
18		c.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
19			Use:   "update [cedict|ecdict|all]",
20			Short: "Download/build the local dictionaries (~67 MB one-time)",
21			Args:  cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
22			RunE:  runDictUpdate,
23		})
24		return c
25	}
26	
27	func runDictUpdate(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
28		cfg, _, err := config.Load()
29		if err != nil {
30			return err
31		}
32		what := "all"
33		if len(args) == 1 {
34			what = args[0]
35		}
36		dir := engine.DictDir(cfg.Dict.Dir)
37		ctx := cmd.Context()
38		prog := func(s string) { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "  "+s) }
39	
40		if what == "cedict" || what == "all" {
41			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "CC-CEDICT (Chinese→English):\n")
42			if err := engine.DownloadCedict(ctx, cfg.Dict.CedictURL, engine.CedictPath(dir), prog); err != nil {
43				return fmt.Errorf("cedict: %w", err)
44			}
45			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  -> %s\n", engine.CedictPath(dir))
46		}
47		if what == "ecdict" || what == "all" {
48			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "ECDICT (English→Chinese, this takes a minute):\n")
49			if err := engine.BuildEcdictDB(ctx, cfg.Dict.EcdictURL, engine.EcdictDBPath(dir), prog); err != nil {
50				return fmt.Errorf("ecdict: %w", err)
51			}
52			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  -> %s\n", engine.EcdictDBPath(dir))
53		}
54		if what != "cedict" && what != "ecdict" && what != "all" {
55			return fmt.Errorf("unknown target %q (use cedict|ecdict|all)", what)
56		}
57		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "done. Dictionary mode (^e) is now bilingual zh↔en.")
58		return nil
59	}

```text
1	# translate
2	
3	A fast CLI/TUI translation tool for the terminal — one-shot from the shell or an
4	interactive live-translating TUI. Backed by an auto fallback chain over your
5	local LLM providers (copilot-proxy → Ollama), a free web API (Google), and a
6	dictionary, with typo-tolerant language resolution and translation history.
7	
8	## Install
9	
10	```sh
11	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate               # macOS/Linux via Homebrew (builds from source)
12	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest   # or with a Go toolchain, into $GOBIN (~/.local/bin)
13	```
14	
15	## Build & run
16	
17	```sh
18	go build -o translate .      # Go 1.25+ (developed on 1.26)
19	./translate "hola mundo" --to en          # one-shot
20	echo "bonjour" | ./translate --to en      # pipe
21	./translate                               # interactive TUI
22	```
23	
24	First run writes a default config to `~/.config/translate/config.toml`; run
25	`./translate init` for a guided setup that probes which providers are up.
26	
27	## Usage
28	
29	| Command | What it does |
30	|---|---|
31	| `translate <text>` / `… \| translate` | One-shot translation (streams to a TTY; plain text when piped) |
32	| `translate` (no args, TTY) | Interactive TUI |
33	| `translate --to <lang> --from <lang>` | Language override; both are fuzzy (`chinees` → `zh`) |
34	| `translate --json` | Emit the full structured result |
35	| `… \| translate --bilingual` (`-2`) | Bilingual pipe view: keep the original (with color) + translation beneath (stdin only) |
36	| `translate define <word>` | Dictionary lookup (bilingual: zh↔en local, or English API) |
37	| `translate history` / `history search <q>` | Recent history / fuzzy search (`--tsv`, `--json`) |
38	| `translate init` | Interactive config wizard (probes providers) |
39	| `translate config path\|show` · `lang resolve <q>` | Introspection helpers |
40	
41	Flags: `--engine smartauto|auto|<provider>|google`, `--provider`, `--model`, `--tier default|fast|max`, `--preset concise|contextual|dictionary`, `--instructions`, `--pair`/`--pair-with`, `--bilingual`/`-2`, `--no-history`, `--debug`.
42	Env overrides: `TRANSLATE_TARGET`, `TRANSLATE_SOURCE`, `TRANSLATE_ENGINE`, `TRANSLATE_PROVIDER`, `TRANSLATE_MODEL`, `TRANSLATE_CONFIG`, `TRANSLATE_DEBUG`.
43	Precedence: **flag > env > `[cli]`/`[tui]` > `[general]` > default**.
44	
45	### Per-front-end defaults (`[cli]` / `[tui]`)
46	
47	The CLI (arguments or piped stdin) and the interactive TUI share `[general]`, but
48	either can override any subset of it via an optional `[cli]` or `[tui]` table — e.g.
49	a snappy concise CLI and a richer, higher-tier TUI:
50	
51	```toml
52	[general]
53	preset = "contextual"
54	tier   = "fast"
55	
56	[cli]                 # one-shot / piped translation
57	preset = "concise"
58	
59	[tui]                 # interactive front-end
60	tier          = "max"
61	live_translate = true
62	```
63	
64	Only keys you list are overridden; the rest inherit `[general]`. Flags and env vars
65	still win over both.
66	
67	## TUI keys
68	
69	`↵` translate · live-debounce auto-translates ~700ms after you stop typing (off by default) ·
70	`^y` copy · `^l` toggle live · `^e` cycle engine · `^t` target language · `^p` model ·
71	`^o` style · `^g` toggle pair mode · `^u` clear · `⇥` switch input/output focus · `^r` history · `⌥↵` newline · `^c`/`esc` quit.
72	
73	`⇥` (Tab) moves keyboard focus between the input box and the result box; the focused
74	box gets an accent border. With the result focused, `↑/↓ j/k PgUp/PgDn g/G space` scroll
75	it; typing any character snaps focus back to the input. A mouse click focuses the box
76	it lands in.
77	
78	## Engines & fallback
79	
80	The `auto` engine tries `chain.order` in turn, failing over **before the first
81	token** (so a down provider switches cleanly; a mid-stream error surfaces rather
82	than restarting):
83	
84	- **copilot-proxy** — OpenAI-compatible at `http://localhost:4141/v1`, no API key.
85	  Default tier is **fast** (`claude-haiku-4-5`); `--tier default` → `claude-sonnet-5`,
86	  `--tier max` → `claude-opus-4-8`. Claude models are served only via the proxy's
87	  Anthropic Messages endpoint (`/v1/messages`) — the engine routes `claude-*` ids
88	  there automatically (they 400 on `/chat/completions`).
89	- **Ollama** — `http://localhost:11434/v1` (offline; `llama3.2:3b`).
90	- **Google** — free, keyless; also reports the detected source language.
91	- **openrouter** — configured but off the default chain; needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
92	
93	> ⚠️ Using a GitHub Copilot subscription to back non-GitHub tools (copilot-proxy)
94	> may violate Copilot's Terms of Service. Reorder `chain.order` (drop `copilot`,
95	> lead with `ollama`/`google`) in the config if that matters to you.
96	
97	Config lives at `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, history at
98	`~/.local/share/translate/history.jsonl`, last-pair state at
99	`~/.local/state/translate/state.json` (XDG-honored on macOS and Linux).
100	
101	### Smart auto (`smartauto`)
102	
103	The recommended default (choose it in `translate init`). It routes by input shape:
104	a **single word/term** is looked up in the dictionary (with the same LLM fallback as
105	`smart-dict` on a miss), while a **phrase or sentence** is translated by the LLM. Set
106	`engine = "smartauto"` in `[general]` (or `--engine smartauto`). It composes with
107	pair mode, so a single word and a full sentence both translate in the right direction.
108	
109	### Pair mode (bidirectional)
110	
111	With `pair = true` + `pair_with`, the tool detects which of the two languages your
112	input is in and translates it into the **other** — one box, both directions
113	(`你好 → hi`, `test → 測試`). For a CJK/non-CJK pair (e.g. `zh-TW`⇄`en`) direction is
114	decided by script, so even short input routes correctly; the LLM translate prompt is
115	also told to detect-and-route and to **never echo** the input. `pair_with` must differ
116	from the target (`translate init` enforces this; a degenerate config warns).
117	
118	### Bilingual mode (`--bilingual` / `-2`)
119	
120	Pipe colored docs and read both languages at once — inspired by Immersive
121	Translate. `cmd | translate --to <lang> --bilingual` keeps each original block
122	verbatim (its ANSI/color intact) and prints the translation beneath each **prose**
123	block, dimmed on a TTY:
124	
125	```sh
126	tldr rg | translate --to zh-TW --bilingual     # or -2
127	```
128	
129	Indented command/example blocks are echoed **untranslated** (so `rg pattern` stays
130	runnable), and blank-line spacing is preserved. It is opt-in and **stdin-only** —
131	never the pipe default, so plain `cmd | translate | less`/`grep` stays clean
132	single-output. Best for prose docs (tldr, man, `--help`); tabular output
133	(`ls -l`, `git status`) and hard-wrapped prose don't interleave cleanly.
134	`--json`/`--learn` take precedence. Design notes + why per-word recoloring was
135	rejected: [`backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md`](backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md).
136	
137	Two strategies, via `--bilingual-mode`:
138	
139	- **`doc`** (default) — one **context-aware** call: the whole document is sent as
140	  numbered segments (prose to translate, commands as context), so the model knows a
141	  bare `rg` is the command being documented (not an abbreviation), stays in one
142	  target variant, and doesn't leak reasoning. Fewer tokens than per-block, and needs
143	  an LLM provider.
144	- **`blocks`** — the older per-block strategy (each block translated in isolation,
145	  concurrent, works with any engine). `doc` automatically falls back to this when no
146	  LLM is available or the structured reply can't be parsed.
147	
148	Separately, ANSI escapes are now **stripped from piped input** before translating,
149	so colored input (e.g. `grep --color=always`) no longer pollutes the prompt.
150	
151	### Debugging
152	
153	`--debug` (or `TRANSLATE_DEBUG=1`, or `[general] debug = true`) logs the intermediate
154	decisions — resolved settings, pair routing, word-vs-phrase classification, dictionary
155	hit/miss, and chain fallback. The one-shot CLI logs to **stderr**; the TUI logs to
156	`~/.local/state/translate/debug.log` (its alt-screen hides stderr).
157	
158	## Dictionary mode
159	
160	`^e` cycles to the dictionary engine (or use `translate define <word>`). It is an
161	**offline bilingual** dictionary that routes by script — Chinese → CC-CEDICT
162	(zh→en), English → ECDICT (en→zh):
163	
164	```sh
165	translate dict update all      # one-time ~67 MB download/build into ~/.local/share/translate/dict
166	```
167	
168	Until then, English lookups fall back to dictionaryapi.dev (`[dict] api_fallback`),
169	and Chinese lookups prompt you to run the update. Misses show a ranked "did you
170	mean" list. Set `[dict] source = "api"` to use only dictionaryapi.dev.
171	
172	### Smart dictionary (`smart-dict`)
173	
174	A distinct engine that keeps the offline dictionary fast and deterministic, but on
175	a miss — no entry, or a fuzzy match too far off — falls back to the LLM for a gloss
176	plus example sentences (never silently: the result carries a `⚠ … defined via <provider> (LLM)`
177	warning). Close typos (edit distance ≤ `[smartdict] close_distance`, default 1) still
178	show "did you mean" without calling the LLM.
179	
180	```sh
181	translate define serendipity        # exact ECDICT entry
182	translate define zzzznotaword       # miss → LLM definition (⚠ warning on stderr)
183	translate define helllo             # distance-1 typo → "did you mean: hello, …"
184	translate define --plain <word>     # force the offline dictionary, no LLM fallback
185	```
186	
187	`translate define` uses smart-dict whenever an LLM provider is reachable
188	(`[smartdict] define_default`, `--smart`/`--plain` to force); in the TUI, `^e`
189	cycles to a `smart-dict` engine alongside the plain `dictionary`.
190	
191	```toml
192	[smartdict]
193	close_distance = 1            # en edit-distance ≤ this stays "did you mean"; beyond → LLM
194	preset         = "dictionary" # LLM output style for the fallback
195	define_default = true         # `translate define` prefers smart-dict when a provider is up
196	```
197	
198	Data: **CC-CEDICT** (CC BY-SA 4.0, © Paul Andrew Denisowski / MDBG) and
199	**ECDICT** (MIT, © skywind3000).
200	
201	## HTTP API server (`translate serve`)
202	
203	Run a persistent **loopback** HTTP service so other clients (Raycast, Alfred,
204	editors, `curl`, a browser) reuse one warm engine instead of spawning the binary
205	per call:
206	
207	```sh
208	translate serve                       # http://127.0.0.1:4155  (docs at /docs)
209	translate serve --port 8080 --token "$TOK"
210	```
211	
212	Endpoints (JSON in, JSON out — same shape the CLI emits with `--json`):
213	
214	```sh
215	curl -s localhost:4155/v1/translate -d '{"text":"hello","target":"zh-TW"}'
216	curl -s localhost:4155/v1/define    -d '{"word":"ephemeral"}'
217	curl -s 'localhost:4155/v1/history?q=hello&limit=10'
218	curl -N 'localhost:4155/v1/translate/stream?text=hello&target=zh-TW'   # SSE
219	```
220	
221	- **Docs**: interactive Swagger UI at `/docs`, spec at `/openapi.json` (both embedded, offline).
222	- **Security**: binds `127.0.0.1` only — a non-loopback `--bind` is refused unless a
223	  token is set. `/v1/history` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when a token
224	  is configured (`[server].token`, or `token_env` to keep it out of `config.toml`).
225	- **Streaming caveat**: SSE token cadence depends on the provider — copilot-proxy
226	  buffers Claude `/v1/messages`, so Claude models still arrive in a burst.
227	
228	```toml
229	[server]
230	port      = 4155
231	bind      = "127.0.0.1"
232	token_env = "TRANSLATE_API_TOKEN"   # optional; guards /v1/history
233	```
234	
235	## MCP server (`translate mcp`)
236	
237	Expose translate as tools to any MCP host (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, …) over
238	**stdio** — no port, no token, history never leaves the pipe. Register:
239	
240	```json
241	{ "command": "translate", "args": ["mcp"] }
242	```
243	
244	Tools: `translate` (text + optional target/source), `define` (word), `history`
245	(query + limit). Each returns readable text plus a typed structured result.
246	Built on the official Go MCP SDK.
247	
248	## Developer note — Charm v2 (`charm.land/*`)
249	
250	This project pins the **v2** Charm stack on the `charm.land/*` vanity module paths
251	(`charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, `bubbles/v2`, `lipgloss/v2`, `huh/v2`) — **not**
252	`github.com/charmbracelet/*`. v1 code will not compile here. When editing the TUI:
253	`View()` returns `tea.View` (wrap strings with `tea.NewView`); keys arrive as
254	`tea.KeyPressMsg`; alt-screen is the declarative `View.AltScreen` field; window
255	size is requested via `tea.RequestWindowSize`.
256	
257	## Architecture
258	
259	The `internal/engine` and `internal/store` layers are pure Go (no TUI imports);
260	the one-shot CLI and the Bubble Tea TUI drive the identical engine values and
261	diverge only at presentation. A single monotonic `seq` counter in the TUI drives
262	debounce-collapse, in-flight cancellation, and stale-result dropping.
263	
264	`internal/appcore` is the transport-agnostic core: it holds the engine builders and
265	a `Service` (a warm engine + history store) that the one-shot CLI, the HTTP server
266	(`internal/server`), and the MCP server (`internal/mcpserver`) all drive — so every
267	front-end shares one translation path and `appcore` never imports `tui` or `cmd`.
268	
269	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:readme-roadmap -->
270	<!-- Snippet for project's README.md, placed near other meta sections like
271	     "Customization" or "Contributing". -->
272

283	scratch.
284	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:readme-roadmap --> (end)
285

```text
1	# Raycast integration for `translate`
2	
3	Bring `translate` into [Raycast](https://raycast.com) — translate from root
4	search or a global hotkey, backed by the **existing `translate` binary** (this
5	directory contains no translation logic; it shells out to the CLI).
6	
7	There are two independent tracks. **The TypeScript extension is the primary,
8	full-featured path;** the script commands are an optional zero-Node fallback.
9	
10	| Track | Path | Build | Best for |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| **TypeScript extension** (primary) | [`extension/`](extension/) | `npm` / `ray` | full UI: live translate, selection prefill, define, history, engine switch, streaming |
13	| **Script Commands** (bash, optional) | [`script-commands/`](script-commands/) | none | zero-Node fallback; one-shot translate/define |
14	
15	Everything requires the `translate` CLI on the machine:
16	
17	```sh
18	just install                                  # → ~/.local/bin/translate
19	# or
20	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
21	```
22	
23	## Track A — Script Commands (optional)
24	
25	The TypeScript extension (Track B) supersedes these; keep them only if you want a
26	zero-Node fallback that runs without `ray develop`.
27	
28	```sh
29	just raycast-scripts   # chmod +x the scripts and print the directory to add
30	```
31	
32	Then, **one time** in Raycast: **Settings → Extensions → Script Commands →
33	Add Script Directory** → select `raycast/script-commands`. (There is no CLI to
34	register a script directory; this step is manual.)
35	
36	Commands: **Translate Text** (language dropdown + text), **Translate & Copy**
37	(copies the result; leave the text blank to translate the clipboard — Script
38	Commands can't read the selection), **Define Word** (dictionary lookup).
39	
40	## Track B — TypeScript extension (local dev)
41	
42	```sh
43	just raycast-dev       # npm install (first run) + `ray develop`
44	```
45	
46	`ray develop` registers the extension with the running Raycast app and hot-reloads.
47	Four commands appear in root search and **stay installed after you stop
48	`ray develop`** — no store publish needed for personal use:
49	**Translate** (type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
50	streaming ⌘↵, Copy/Paste/Speak), **Translate Selection** (grabs the selection or
51	clipboard and opens Translate prefilled, with an optional target-language argument),
52	**Define** (dictionary lookup + LLM fallback), and **History** (browse/search past
53	translations). `just raycast-build` / `just raycast-lint` type-check and lint.
54	
55	Configure the binary path and defaults in the extension's **Preferences**
56	(the binary is auto-probed in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`,
57	`/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`; override with an absolute path if it lives elsewhere).
58	Translate-as-you-type is **debounced** (default 700 ms, tunable via the
59	"Live translate debounce" preference) and cancels superseded in-flight requests,
60	so typing a phrase doesn't fire an LLM call per keystroke. Opening **Translate**
61	seeds the input from the current selection (or clipboard) per the "Prefill input
62	from" preference — set it to "Nothing" to always start empty.
63	
64	## Gotchas (both tracks)
65	
66	- **Raycast runs under launchd with a restricted PATH** — it does *not* inherit
67	  your shell's PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `command not found` /
68	  `spawn translate ENOENT`. Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path. Always test
69	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
70	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
71	- **API keys must live in `translate`'s config**, not shell env — a key exported
72	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd. Put providers/keys in
73	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml` (run `translate init`); `HOME` is passed
74	  through so the CLI finds it.
75	- **Exit code is 0 even when an engine fails** (it falls back). The extension
76	  surfaces `warnings[]` from `--json`; the plain-text scripts don't show them.
77	
78	See [`../docs/raycast-extension.md`](../docs/raycast-extension.md) for how Raycast
79	extensions work, the full integration-tier comparison, and the competitive
80	landscape. Store publishing is tracked in
81	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
82
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Translate
2	
3	Translate, define, and speak text from Raycast — backed by the local
4	[`translate`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/translate) CLI. Multi-engine
5	auto-fallback (local LLM via copilot-proxy / Ollama, keyless Google, offline
6	CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries), unified history, and free TTS.
7	
8	## Requirements
9	
10	This extension **shells out to the `translate` CLI** — it does not translate on its
11	own. Install the binary first:
12	
13	```sh
14	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
15	# or, with a Go toolchain:
16	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest
17	```
18	
19	On first run, `translate init` sets up your providers/config
20	(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`). The extension auto-detects the binary in
21	`~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, and `~/go/bin`; if it lives
22	elsewhere, set **“translate binary path”** in the extension preferences. (If it
23	isn’t found, the extension shows an install-instructions screen instead of failing.)
24	
25	> **Note:** Raycast runs under a restricted `PATH` and reads no shell env, so API
26	> keys must live in `translate`’s config file (via `translate init`), not in
27	> `~/.zshrc`. “Translate Selection” and selection-prefill need macOS **Accessibility**
28	> permission for Raycast (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).
29	
30	## Commands
31	
32	- **Translate** — type to translate; pick the target language; ⌘↵ for a streaming
33	  view; actions for Copy / Paste / Speak and an engine override.
34	- **Translate Selection** — grabs your selection (or clipboard) and opens Translate
35	  prefilled and editable.
36	- **Define** — dictionary lookup with phonetics and meanings (offline dictionaries,
37	  LLM fallback, and suggestions).
38	- **History** — browse and search your past translations.
39	
40	## Preferences
41	
42	Binary path, default target language, engine, model tier, live-translate debounce,
43	and how Translate prefills its input (selection / clipboard / nothing). Leave
44	**target / tier / debounce** empty to inherit them from the `translate` config
45	(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`, read via `config show --json`) — configure them
46	once and Raycast honors them; set a preference to override the config for Raycast.
47
```
</details></tool-use>

12	)
13	
14	func newServeCmd() *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			port      int
17			bind      string
18			token     string
19			noHistory bool
20		)
21		c := &cobra.Command{
22			Use:   "serve",
23			Short: "Run the local HTTP API server (loopback; JSON + SSE + OpenAPI)",
24			Long: "serve starts a persistent loopback HTTP service exposing the translate\n" +
25				"engine over JSON (and SSE streaming). It binds 127.0.0.1 by default; a\n" +
26				"non-loopback bind is refused unless a token is set. History is guarded by\n" +
27				"the token when one is configured.\n\n" +
28				"  translate serve                 # http://127.0.0.1:4155\n" +
29				"  translate serve --port 8080\n" +
30				"  translate serve --token \"$TOK\" --bind 0.0.0.0",
31			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
32			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
33				cfg, _, err := config.Load()
34				if err != nil {
35					return err
36				}
37				sc := cfg.ResolveServer(config.ServerOverrides{Port: port, Bind: bind, Token: token})
38				svc, err := appcore.NewService(cfg, appcore.Options{NoHistory: noHistory})
39				if err != nil {
40					return err
41				}
42				defer svc.Close()
43				srv, err := server.New(svc, server.Options{Bind: sc.Bind, Port: sc.Port, Token: sc.Token})
44				if err != nil {
45					return err
46				}
47				// Add SIGTERM to the inherited Ctrl-C context so a daemon stops cleanly.
48				ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), syscall.SIGTERM)
49				defer stop()
50				return srv.Run(ctx)
51			},
52		}
53		c.Flags().IntVar(&port, "port", 0, "listen port (default from [server].port, else 4155)")
54		c.Flags().StringVar(&bind, "bind", "", "bind address (default 127.0.0.1; loopback enforced without a token)")
55		c.Flags().StringVar(&token, "token", "", "bearer token guarding /v1/history (overrides config)")
56		c.Flags().BoolVar(&noHistory, "no-history", false, "do not read or write history")
57		return c
58	}

34	func newSpeaker(cfg *config.Config) tts.Speaker { return tts.New(speakOptions(cfg)) }
35	
36	// tuiSpeaker returns a Speaker for the TUI, or nil when TTS is disabled (so the
37	// TUI can show a "tts disabled" hint instead of silently doing nothing).
38	func tuiSpeaker(cfg *config.Config) tts.Speaker {
39		if !cfg.TTS.Enabled {
40			return nil
41		}
42		return newSpeaker(cfg)
43	}

46	// value, else the pair-mode "away" language (empty => Select derives it).
47	func speakForeign(cfg *config.Config, pairWith string) string {
48		if cfg.TTS.Foreign != "" {
49			return cfg.TTS.Foreign
50		}
51		return pairWith
52	}
53

60	// are reported to stderr and never abort the command.
61	func speakResult(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, res *engine.TranslateResult, srcText, srcLang, resLang, foreign string) {
62		ch, ok := tts.Select(tts.SelectInput{
63			SourceText: srcText,
64			SourceLang: srcLang,
65			ResultText: res.Translation,
66			ResultLang: resLang,
67			Foreign:    foreign,
68		})
69		if !ok {
70			return
71		}
72		applySpeakLangOverride(&ch)
73		if err := newSpeaker(cfg).Speak(ctx, ch.Text, ch.Lang); err != nil {
74			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: speech unavailable (%v)\n", err)
75		}
76	}
77	
78	// speakDefine speaks the looked-up head word itself (a `define --speak`
79	// pronounces the entry regardless of the foreign preference).
80	func speakDefine(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, res *engine.TranslateResult) {
81		word := ""
82		if res.Dictionary != nil {
83			word = res.Dictionary.Word
84		}
85		if strings.TrimSpace(word) == "" {
86			word = res.Translation
87		}
88		if strings.TrimSpace(word) == "" {
89			return
90		}
91		code := ""
92		if flagSpeakLang != "" {
93			if lm, _ := lang.Resolve(flagSpeakLang); lm.Code != "" {
94				code = lm.Code
95			}
96		}
97		if code == "" {
98			code = lang.Detect(word)
99		}
100		if err := newSpeaker(cfg).Speak(ctx, word, code); err != nil {
101			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: speech unavailable (%v)\n", err)
102		}
103	}

108			return
109		}
110		if lm, _ := lang.Resolve(flagSpeakLang); lm.Code != "" {
111			ch.Lang = lm.Code
112		}
113	}

```text
1	package cmd
2	
3	import (
4		"runtime/debug"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// version is injected at build time via
9	//
10	//	-ldflags "-X github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/cmd.version=v0.3.1"
11	//
12	// by packaged builds (the Homebrew formula, goreleaser, etc.). It overrides the
13	// build-info value below, which reports "(devel)" for a binary built from an
14	// extracted source tarball — no module version and no VCS metadata to read.
15	var version string
16	
17	// buildVersion reports a version string derived from the Go build info, so
18	// `translate --version` distinguishes a freshly-built dev binary from a stale
19	// installed one. For `go install <path>@<ver>` it shows the module version; for
20	// a local `go build`/`go install .` off a working tree it shows the VCS revision,
21	// a "+dirty" marker when the tree had uncommitted changes, and the build time.
22	// A build-time-injected version (above) takes precedence over both.
23	func buildVersion() string {
24		if version != "" {
25			return version
26		}
27		info, ok := debug.ReadBuildInfo()
28		if !ok {
29			return "(unknown; no build info)"
30		}
31		ver := info.Main.Version // e.g. "v0.1.0" or "(devel)"
32		var rev, when string
33		dirty := false
34		for _, s := range info.Settings {
35			switch s.Key {
36			case "vcs.revision":
37				rev = s.Value
38			case "vcs.time":
39				when = s.Value
40			case "vcs.modified":
41				dirty = s.Value == "true"
42			}
43		}
44		var b strings.Builder
45		b.WriteString(ver)
46		if rev != "" {
47			if len(rev) > 12 {
48				rev = rev[:12]
49			}
50			b.WriteString(" (" + rev)
51			if dirty {
52				b.WriteString("+dirty")
53			}
54			b.WriteString(")")
55		}
56		if when != "" {
57			b.WriteString(" commit " + when)
58		}
59		return b.String()
60	}
61	
62	// shortVersion is just the leading version token of buildVersion() (e.g.
63	// "v0.4.0" or "(devel)"), for stamping config.version and the outdated reminder.
64	func shortVersion() string {
65		v := buildVersion()
66		if i := strings.IndexByte(v, ' '); i > 0 {
67			return v[:i]
68		}
69		return v
70	}
71

17	// Config is the top-level config.toml schema.
18	type Config struct {
19		// Version is the app version (git tag) that last wrote this file, and Schema is
20		// the config schema generation (see SchemaVersion). Both are stamped by Save;
21		// Version is informational, Schema drives the "your config is outdated" reminder.
22		// Declared first so they serialize above the [general] table.
23		Version string `toml:"version,omitempty"`
24		Schema  int    `toml:"schema"`
25	
26		General   General    `toml:"general"`
27		CLI       *Overlay   `toml:"cli,omitempty"` // per-front-end overrides on [general]
28		TUI       *Overlay   `toml:"tui,omitempty"` // (nil unless the user adds the table)
29		Chain     Chain      `toml:"chain"`
30		Providers []Provider `toml:"provider"` // array-of-tables: [[provider]]
31		Google    Google     `toml:"google"`
32		Dict      Dict       `toml:"dict"`
33		SmartDict SmartDict  `toml:"smartdict"`
34		TTS       TTS        `toml:"tts"`
35		History   History    `toml:"history"`
36		Server    Server     `toml:"server"`
37	}
38	
39	// SchemaVersion is the current config schema generation. Bump it whenever a new
40	// field or default is added that `translate init` would materialize, so an older
41	// on-disk config (schema < this) can be detected and the user reminded to re-init.
42	// It is NOT the app version (which is the git tag; see cmd/version.go). History:
43	//
44	//	1 — smart-auto default, pair-mode home anchoring, debug, TTS/learn fields.
45	//	2 — [server] table (translate serve: HTTP API).
46	const SchemaVersion = 2
47	
48	// Generator is the app version string (git tag) stamped into config.version on
49	// Save. The cmd layer sets it at startup; it stays "" for library/test callers,
50	// in which case the version key is simply omitted.
51	var Generator string
52	
53	// Overlay is a partial [general] applied for one front-end ([cli] or [tui]). Every
54	// field is a pointer so a nil means "inherit from [general]"; only keys the user
55	// actually wrote override. Precedence: flag > env > [cli]/[tui] > [general] > default.
56	type Overlay struct {
57		Engine        *string `toml:"engine,omitempty"`
58		Tier          *string `toml:"tier,omitempty"`
59		Preset        *string `toml:"preset,omitempty"`
60		Instructions  *string `toml:"instructions,omitempty"`

63		DefaultSource *string `toml:"default_source,omitempty"`
64		Pair          *bool   `toml:"pair,omitempty"`
65		PairWith      *string `toml:"pair_with,omitempty"`
66		Learn         *bool   `toml:"learn,omitempty"`
67		Stream        *bool   `toml:"stream,omitempty"`
68		LiveTranslate *bool   `toml:"live_translate,omitempty"`
69		DebounceMs    *int    `toml:"debounce_ms,omitempty"`
70		Debug         *bool   `toml:"debug,omitempty"`
71	}

160	// Server configures the local HTTP API server (`translate serve`). The bind is
161	// loopback by default because history is personal data; a non-loopback bind is
162	// refused unless a token is set. Prefer token_env over an inline token so the
163	// secret stays out of config.toml.
164	type Server struct {
165		Port     int    `toml:"port"`                // listen port (default 4155)
166		Bind     string `toml:"bind"`                // bind address (default 127.0.0.1)
167		Token    string `toml:"token,omitempty"`     // inline bearer token (guards /v1/history)
168		TokenEnv string `toml:"token_env,omitempty"` // env var holding the token (preferred)
169	}
170	
171	// ServerOverrides carries explicit `translate serve` flag values (zero == unset).
172	type ServerOverrides struct {
173		Port  int
174		Bind  string
175		Token string
176	}
177	
178	// ResolvedServer is the effective server config after flags/env are applied.
179	type ResolvedServer struct {
180		Port  int
181		Bind  string
182		Token string // resolved token (inline or from token_env); "" => no auth
183	}
184	
185	// ResolveServer merges flag overrides over the [server] table and resolves the
186	// bearer token (flag > inline token > token_env), filling in the built-in
187	// defaults for an empty port/bind (an older config predating [server] reads 0/"").
188	func (c *Config) ResolveServer(o ServerOverrides) ResolvedServer {
189		port := c.Server.Port
190		if o.Port != 0 {
191			port = o.Port
192		}
193		if port == 0 {
194			port = 4155
195		}
196		bind := c.Server.Bind
197		if o.Bind != "" {
198			bind = o.Bind
199		}
200		if bind == "" {
201			bind = "127.0.0.1"
202		}
203		token := o.Token
204		if token == "" {
205			token = c.Server.Token
206		}
207		if token == "" && c.Server.TokenEnv != "" {
208			token = strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(c.Server.TokenEnv))
209		}
210		return ResolvedServer{Port: port, Bind: bind, Token: token}
211	}

319	// Path returns the config file path, honoring $TRANSLATE_CONFIG if set.
320	func Path() string {
321		if p := os.Getenv("TRANSLATE_CONFIG"); p != "" {
322			return p
323		}
324		return xdgpath.ConfigFile()
325	}
326	
327	// Load reads the config file. On first run (file missing) it writes Default() and
328	// returns it with created=true so the caller can hint the user to run `init`.
329	func Load() (cfg *Config, created bool, err error) {
330		p := Path()
331		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
332		if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
333			cfg = Default()
334			if werr := Save(cfg); werr != nil {
335				return cfg, false, fmt.Errorf("write default config: %w", werr)
336			}
337			return cfg, true, nil
338		}
339		if err != nil {
340			return nil, false, err
341		}
342		cfg = Default() // start from defaults so omitted keys keep sane values
343		if err := toml.Unmarshal(b, cfg); err != nil {
344			return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", p, err)
345		}
346		return cfg, false, nil
347	}
348	
349	// Save writes the config atomically (temp file + rename). It stamps the current
350	// schema generation and (when known) the writing app version, so a later build
351	// can detect an outdated config.
352	func Save(cfg *Config) error {
353		if err := xdgpath.EnsureDirs(); err != nil {
354			return err
355		}
356		cfg.Schema = SchemaVersion
357		if Generator != "" {
358			cfg.Version = Generator
359		}
360		b, err := toml.Marshal(cfg)
361		if err != nil {
362			return err
363		}
364		p := Path()
365		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(p), ".config-*.toml")
366		if err != nil {
367			return err
368		}
369		tmpName := tmp.Name()
370		defer os.Remove(tmpName) // no-op after successful rename
371		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
372			tmp.Close()
373			return err
374		}
375		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
376			return err
377		}
378		return os.Rename(tmpName, p)
379	}
380	
381	// Outdated reports whether the loaded config predates the current schema, i.e.
382	// it was written by an older build (or before schema tracking existed, in which
383	// case the key is absent and reads as 0). The caller uses it to nudge a re-init.
384	func (c *Config) Outdated() bool { return c.Schema < SchemaVersion }
385	
386	// ProviderByName returns the named provider, or nil if absent.
387	func (c *Config) ProviderByName(name string) *Provider {
388		for i := range c.Providers {
389			if c.Providers[i].Name == name {
390				return &c.Providers[i]
391			}
392		}
393		return nil
394	}
395	
396	// ModelForTier returns the provider's model id for the given tier
397	// ("default"/"fast"/"max"), falling back to the default model.
398	func (p *Provider) ModelForTier(tier string) string {
399		switch tier {
400		case "fast":
401			if p.ModelFast != "" {
402				return p.ModelFast
403			}
404		case "max":
405			if p.ModelMax != "" {
406				return p.ModelMax
407			}
408		}
409		return p.Model
410	}

1	// Package store persists translation history. v1 uses an append-only JSONL file
2	// with in-memory fuzzy search behind the Store interface; a sqlite+FTS5 backend
3	// can drop in later without changing callers.
4	package store
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"time"
9	)
10	
11	// Record is one history entry (also the JSONL line shape).
12	type Record struct {
13		ID           string    `json:"id"`
14		TS           time.Time `json:"ts"`
15		SourceLang   string    `json:"source_lang"`
16		TargetLang   string    `json:"target_lang"`
17		Engine       string    `json:"engine"`
18		Model        string    `json:"model,omitempty"`
19		Input        string    `json:"input"`
20		Output       string    `json:"output"`
21		Alternatives []string  `json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
22		Notes        string    `json:"notes,omitempty"`
23		Favorite     bool      `json:"favorite,omitempty"`
24	}
25	
26	// Store is the history persistence interface.
27	type Store interface {
28		// Add assigns an ID and timestamp, persists the record, and returns it.
29		Add(ctx context.Context, r Record) (Record, error)
30		// Recent returns up to limit records, newest first.
31		Recent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]Record, error)
32		// Search returns records fuzzy-matching query (over input+output), best first.
33		Search(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]Record, error)
34		// Close releases any resources.
35		Close() error
36	}
37
```

10	)

12	// Lang is one known language: its ISO-639-1 code, English name, and aliases
13	// (native names, ISO-639-2 codes, common misspellings).
14	type Lang struct {
15		Code    string
16		Name    string
17		Aliases []string
18	}
19	
20	// Match is the result of resolving a query to a language.

60		{"no", "norwegian", []string{"nor", "norsk", "nb", "nn"}},
61		{"fa", "persian", []string{"fas", "per", "farsi", "فارسی"}},
62		{"bn", "bengali", []string{"ben", "বাংলা"}},
63		{"ta", "tamil", []string{"tam", "தமிழ்"}},
64		{"ms", "malay", []string{"msa", "may", "bahasa melayu"}},
65		{"ca", "catalan", []string{"cat", "català"}},
66	}
67	
68	// candidate is one searchable token (code, name, or alias) pointing at a Lang.
69	type candidate struct {
70		token string
71		lang  *Lang
72		// weight scales the fuzzy score: exact code/name matches are preferred.
73		primary bool
74	}
75	
76	var candidates = buildCandidates()
77	
78	func buildCandidates() []candidate {
79		var cs []candidate
80		for i := range table {
81			l := &table[i]
82			cs = append(cs, candidate{token: strings.ToLower(l.Code), lang: l, primary: true})
83			cs = append(cs, candidate{token: strings.ToLower(l.Name), lang: l, primary: true})
84			for _, a := range l.Aliases {
85				cs = append(cs, candidate{token: strings.ToLower(a), lang: l})
86			}
87		}
88		return cs
89	}
90	
91	// Resolve maps a free-form query to a language, tolerating typos. It returns the
92	// best match plus ranked alternatives (for TUI disambiguation). "auto" and ""
93	// pass through as an auto-detect sentinel (Code "auto", Exact true).
94	func Resolve(q string) (Match, []Match) {
95		norm := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(q))
96		if norm == "" || norm == "auto" {
97			return Match{Code: "auto", Name: "auto-detect", Score: 1, Exact: true}, nil
98		}
99	
100		// Exact match on any code / name / alias.
101		for _, c := range candidates {
102			if c.token == norm {
103				return Match{Code: c.lang.Code, Name: c.lang.Name, Score: 1, Exact: true}, nil
104			}
105		}
106	
107		// Fuzzy: rank candidates by normalized Levenshtein similarity.
108		type scored struct {
109			lang  *Lang
110			score float64
111		}
112		best := map[string]scored{} // dedupe by language code, keep best score
113		for _, c := range candidates {
114			d := levenshtein.ComputeDistance(norm, c.token)
115			maxLen := max(len(norm), len(c.token))
116			if maxLen == 0 {
117				continue
118			}
119			sim := 1 - float64(d)/float64(maxLen)
120			if !c.primary {
121				sim -= 0.05 // slight preference for code/name over alias
122			}
123			if cur, ok := best[c.lang.Code]; !ok || sim > cur.score {
124				best[c.lang.Code] = scored{lang: c.lang, score: sim}
125			}
126		}
127	
128		ranked := make([]Match, 0, len(best))
129		for _, s := range best {
130			ranked = append(ranked, Match{Code: s.lang.Code, Name: s.lang.Name, Score: s.score})
131		}
132		sort.Slice(ranked, func(i, j int) bool { return ranked[i].Score > ranked[j].Score })
133	
134		if len(ranked) == 0 || ranked[0].Score < 0.5 {
135			// No confident match; echo the query back as an opaque code so callers
136			// can still attempt it (e.g. a code we don't have in the table).
137			return Match{Code: norm, Name: norm, Score: 0}, ranked
138		}
139		top := 3
140		if len(ranked) < top {
141			top = len(ranked)
142		}
143		return ranked[0], ranked[1:top]
144	}
145	
146	// List returns all known languages (for the target-language picker).
147	func List() []Lang {
148		out := make([]Lang, len(table))
149		copy(out, table)
150		return out
151	}
152	
153	// Name returns the English name for a code, or the code itself if unknown.
154	func Name(code string) string {
155		if strings.EqualFold(code, "auto") || code == "" {
156			return "auto-detect"
157		}
158		for i := range table {
159			if strings.EqualFold(table[i].Code, code) {
160				return table[i].Name
161			}
162		}
163		return code
164	}
165
```

1	package engine
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"net/http"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/agnivade/levenshtein"
16	)
17	
18	// suggestLimit caps the number of ranked "did you mean" candidates on a miss.
19	const suggestLimit = 7
20	
21	// DictConfig configures the dictionary engine.
22	type DictConfig struct {
23		Endpoint string // base, e.g. https://api.dictionaryapi.dev/api/v2/entries
24		Lang     string // e.g. "en"
25		Fuzzy    bool
26		Wordlist string // path to a newline word list; "" => /usr/share/dict/words
27		Timeout  time.Duration
28	}
29	
30	// DictEngine looks up word definitions via the Free Dictionary API, with an
31	// exact match first and a local fuzzy (nearest-headword) fallback on 404.
32	type DictEngine struct {
33		cfg  DictConfig
34		wl   *wordIndex
35		http *http.Client
36	}
37	
38	// NewDict builds a dictionary engine.
39	func NewDict(cfg DictConfig) *DictEngine {
40		if cfg.Endpoint == "" {
41			cfg.Endpoint = "https://api.dictionaryapi.dev/api/v2/entries"
42		}
43		if cfg.Lang == "" {
44			cfg.Lang = "en"
45		}
46		if cfg.Timeout == 0 {
47			cfg.Timeout = 5 * time.Second
48		}
49		path := cfg.Wordlist
50		if path == "" {
51			path = "/usr/share/dict/words"
52		}
53		return &DictEngine{cfg: cfg, wl: &wordIndex{path: path}, http: &http.Client{Timeout: cfg.Timeout}}
54	}
55	
56	// Name returns "dictionary".
57	func (e *DictEngine) Name() string { return "dictionary" }
58	
59	// Supports reports that this engine handles dictionary lookups only.
60	func (e *DictEngine) Supports(m Mode) bool { return m == ModeDict }
61	
62	// Detect is not meaningful for the dictionary engine.
63	func (e *DictEngine) Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error) { return "", nil }
64	
65	// Available probes the API with a common word.
66	func (e *DictEngine) Available(ctx context.Context) bool {
67		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 1500*time.Millisecond)
68		defer cancel()
69		_, status, err := e.fetch(ctx, "test")
70		return err == nil && status == http.StatusOK
71	}
72	
73	// Translate performs a dictionary lookup (exact, then fuzzy on 404).
74	func (e *DictEngine) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
75		word := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(req.Text))
76		if word == "" {
77			return nil, ErrEmptyInput
78		}
79	
80		entry, status, err := e.fetch(ctx, word)
81		if err == nil && status == http.StatusOK && entry != nil {
82			return single(e.result(entry, req), nil), nil
83		}
84		if err != nil {
85			return single(nil, fmt.Errorf("dictionary: %w", err)), nil
86		}
87	
88		// 404: return a ranked "did you mean" list (the frontend chooses one). Gated
89		// to English because the bundled wordlist (/usr/share/dict/words) is English.
90		if status == http.StatusNotFound && e.cfg.Fuzzy && strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(e.cfg.Lang), "en") {
91			if cands, best := e.wl.nearestN(word, 2, suggestLimit); len(cands) > 0 {
92				return single(&TranslateResult{Target: req.Target, Engine: e.Name(), Suggestions: cands, SuggestDistance: best}, nil), nil
93			}
94		}
95		return single(nil, fmt.Errorf("dictionary: %w: %q", ErrNoDictEntry, word)), nil
96	}
97	
98	func (e *DictEngine) result(entry *DictEntry, req Request) *TranslateResult {
99		return &TranslateResult{
100			Translation: entry.gloss(),
101			Target:      req.Target,
102			Engine:      e.Name(),
103			Dictionary:  entry,
104		}
105	}
106	
107	// --- Free Dictionary API wire types ---
108	
109	type apiEntry struct {
110		Word       string        `json:"word"`
111		Phonetic   string        `json:"phonetic"`
112		Phonetics  []apiPhonetic `json:"phonetics"`
113		Meanings   []apiMeaning  `json:"meanings"`
114		SourceURLs []string      `json:"sourceUrls"`
115	}
116	type apiPhonetic struct {
117		Text string `json:"text"`
118	}
119	type apiMeaning struct {
120		PartOfSpeech string          `json:"partOfSpeech"`
121		Definitions  []apiDefinition `json:"definitions"`
122		Synonyms     []string        `json:"synonyms"`
123		Antonyms     []string        `json:"antonyms"`
124	}
125	type apiDefinition struct {
126		Definition string `json:"definition"`
127		Example    string `json:"example"`
128	}
129	
130	// fetch requests one word; returns (entry, httpStatus, err). A 404 yields
131	// (nil, 404, nil) so the caller can trigger the fuzzy fallback.
132	func (e *DictEngine) fetch(ctx context.Context, word string) (*DictEntry, int, error) {
133		u := fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%s", strings.TrimRight(e.cfg.Endpoint, "/"), e.cfg.Lang, urlPathEscape(word))
134		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, u, nil)
135		if err != nil {
136			return nil, 0, err
137		}
138		resp, err := e.http.Do(req)
139		if err != nil {
140			return nil, 0, err
141		}
142		defer resp.Body.Close()
143		if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusNotFound {
144			_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)
145			return nil, http.StatusNotFound, nil
146		}
147		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
148			body, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 512))
149			return nil, resp.StatusCode, fmt.Errorf("http %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, strings.TrimSpace(string(body)))
150		}
151		var entries []apiEntry
152		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&entries); err != nil {
153			return nil, resp.StatusCode, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
154		}
155		if len(entries) == 0 {
156			return nil, http.StatusNotFound, nil
157		}
158		return mergeEntries(entries), http.StatusOK, nil
159	}
160	
161	// mergeEntries folds the API's per-entry results into one DictEntry.
162	func mergeEntries(entries []apiEntry) *DictEntry {
163		out := &DictEntry{Word: entries[0].Word}
164		for _, en := range entries {
165			if out.Phonetic == "" && en.Phonetic != "" {
166				out.Phonetic = en.Phonetic
167			}
168			for _, p := range en.Phonetics {
169				if out.Phonetic == "" && p.Text != "" {
170					out.Phonetic = p.Text
171				}
172			}
173			for _, m := range en.Meanings {
174				meaning := Meaning{PartOfSpeech: m.PartOfSpeech, Synonyms: m.Synonyms, Antonyms: m.Antonyms}
175				for _, d := range m.Definitions {
176					meaning.Definitions = append(meaning.Definitions, Definition{Text: d.Definition, Example: d.Example})
177				}
178				out.Meanings = append(out.Meanings, meaning)
179			}
180			if out.SourceURL == "" && len(en.SourceURLs) > 0 {
181				out.SourceURL = en.SourceURLs[0]
182			}
183		}
184		return out
185	}
186	
187	// gloss returns a short one-line definition for history/plain display.
188	func (d *DictEntry) gloss() string {
189		for _, m := range d.Meanings {
190			for _, def := range m.Definitions {
191				if def.Text != "" {
192					return def.Text
193				}
194			}
195		}
196		return d.Word
197	}
198	
199	func urlPathEscape(s string) string {
200		// dictionary words are simple; escape spaces defensively.
201		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, " ", "%20")
202	}
203	
204	// --- local fuzzy word index ---
205	
206	type wordIndex struct {
207		path  string
208		once  sync.Once
209		words []string
210	}
211	
212	func (wi *wordIndex) load() {
213		wi.once.Do(func() {
214			b, err := os.ReadFile(wi.path)
215			if err != nil {
216				return // no wordlist: fuzzy silently disabled
217			}
218			for _, line := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
219				w := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
220				if w != "" {
221					wi.words = append(wi.words, w)
222				}
223			}
224		})
225	}
226	
227	// nearestN returns up to n headwords within maxDist edits of word, closest first
228	// (ties broken alphabetically), excluding word itself. The second return is the
229	// best (smallest) edit distance among the results, or 0 when there are none.
230	func (wi *wordIndex) nearestN(word string, maxDist, n int) ([]string, int) {
231		wi.load()
232		type cand struct {
233			w string
234			d int
235		}
236		var cs []cand
237		for _, w := range wi.words {
238			if w == word || abs(len(w)-len(word)) > maxDist {
239				continue
240			}
241			if d := levenshtein.ComputeDistance(word, w); d <= maxDist {
242				cs = append(cs, cand{w, d})
243			}
244		}
245		sort.Slice(cs, func(i, j int) bool {
246			if cs[i].d != cs[j].d {
247				return cs[i].d < cs[j].d
248			}
249			return cs[i].w < cs[j].w
250		})
251		if len(cs) > n {
252			cs = cs[:n]
253		}
254		out := make([]string, len(cs))
255		for i, c := range cs {
256			out[i] = c.w
257		}
258		best := 0
259		if len(cs) > 0 {
260			best = cs[0].d // slice is sorted by distance ascending
261		}
262		return out, best
263	}
264	
265	func abs(n int) int {
266		if n < 0 {
267			return -n
268		}
269		return n
270	}
271

9	)

11	// Record is one history entry (also the JSONL line shape).
12	type Record struct {
13		ID           string    `json:"id"`
14		TS           time.Time `json:"ts"`
15		SourceLang   string    `json:"source_lang"`
16		TargetLang   string    `json:"target_lang"`
17		Engine       string    `json:"engine"`
18		Model        string    `json:"model,omitempty"`
19		Input        string    `json:"input"`
20		Output       string    `json:"output"`
21		Alternatives []string  `json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
22		Notes        string    `json:"notes,omitempty"`
23		Favorite     bool      `json:"favorite,omitempty"`
24	}
25	
26	// Store is the history persistence interface.
27	type Store interface {
28		// Add assigns an ID and timestamp, persists the record, and returns it.
29		Add(ctx context.Context, r Record) (Record, error)
30		// Recent returns up to limit records, newest first.
31		Recent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]Record, error)
32		// Search returns records fuzzy-matching query (over input+output), best first.
33		Search(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]Record, error)
34		// Close releases any resources.
35		Close() error
36	}

```text
1	# Backlog Research
2	
3	Long-form research, design notes, and paused troubleshooting for items listed in
4	[`../TODO.md`](../TODO.md). One file per topic, named with a slug that matches
5	the TODO entry.
6	
7	## Why this exists
8	
9	`TODO.md` is the **index** — short titles grouped by priority section with
10	effort tags. This folder
11	is the **knowledge base** — the actual investigation, options considered,
12	benchmarks, error messages, and decisions that informed the TODO entry. The goal
13	is **resume-friendliness**: when you (or an agent) come back to an item three
14	months later, the doc here lets you pick up in 5 minutes instead of re-running
15	30 minutes of investigation.
16	
17	This folder is maintainer-facing repo metadata. It lives in the git repo but
18	never reaches users — `go install` / `go build` compile only Go sources, so it
19	has no effect on the built binary.
20	
21	## When to add a doc here
22	
23	Add a `backlog/<slug>.md` file when **any** of these apply:
24	
25	- The TODO item carries a `P?` tag (it requires evaluation; record what was tried)
26	- You did meaningful troubleshooting but didn't ship a fix (capture the trace
27	  before it evaporates)
28	- Multiple options were considered (record the trade-offs, not just the winner)
29	- An external blocker exists (waiting on upstream release, host availability)

1	package store
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"crypto/rand"
6		"encoding/hex"
7		"encoding/json"
8		"os"
9		"path/filepath"
10		"strconv"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/sahilm/fuzzy"
16	)
17	
18	// jsonlStore is an append-only JSONL-backed Store with in-memory fuzzy search.
19	type jsonlStore struct {
20		path string
21		mu   sync.Mutex
22	}
23	
24	// OpenJSONL opens (creating parent dirs for) a JSONL history file.
25	func OpenJSONL(path string) (Store, error) {
26		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {
27			return nil, err
28		}
29		return &jsonlStore{path: path}, nil
30	}
31	
32	func (s *jsonlStore) Close() error { return nil }
33	
34	// Add stamps the record with an id + timestamp and appends it as one JSON line.
35	func (s *jsonlStore) Add(ctx context.Context, r Record) (Record, error) {
36		if r.ID == "" {
37			r.ID = newID()
38		}
39		if r.TS.IsZero() {
40			r.TS = time.Now()
41		}
42		line, err := json.Marshal(r)
43		if err != nil {
44			return r, err
45		}
46	
47		s.mu.Lock()
48		defer s.mu.Unlock()
49		f, err := os.OpenFile(s.path, os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
50		if err != nil {
51			return r, err
52		}
53		defer f.Close()
54		// Serialize appends across processes too (server + CLI): the in-process mutex
55		// only covers this process.
56		unlock, err := lockFile(f)
57		if err != nil {
58			return r, err
59		}
60		defer unlock()
61		if _, err := f.Write(append(line, '\n')); err != nil {
62			return r, err
63		}
64		return r, nil
65	}
66	
67	// readAll loads every record in chronological (file) order.
68	func (s *jsonlStore) readAll() ([]Record, error) {
69		s.mu.Lock()
70		defer s.mu.Unlock()
71		b, err := os.ReadFile(s.path)
72		if err != nil {
73			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
74				return nil, nil
75			}
76			return nil, err
77		}
78		var out []Record
79		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
80			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
81			if line == "" {
82				continue
83			}
84			var r Record
85			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &r) == nil {
86				out = append(out, r)
87			}
88		}
89		return out, nil
90	}
91	
92	// Recent returns up to limit records, newest first.
93	func (s *jsonlStore) Recent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]Record, error) {
94		all, err := s.readAll()
95		if err != nil {
96			return nil, err
97		}
98		reverse(all)
99		if limit > 0 && len(all) > limit {
100			all = all[:limit]
101		}
102		return all, nil
103	}
104	
105	// Search fuzzy-ranks records by "input ⏎ output", best match first.
106	func (s *jsonlStore) Search(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]Record, error) {
107		all, err := s.readAll()
108		if err != nil {
109			return nil, err
110		}
111		q := strings.TrimSpace(query)
112		if q == "" {
113			reverse(all)
114			if limit > 0 && len(all) > limit {
115				all = all[:limit]
116			}
117			return all, nil
118		}
119		hay := make([]string, len(all))
120		for i, r := range all {
121			hay[i] = r.Input + " " + r.Output
122		}
123		matches := fuzzy.Find(q, hay)
124		out := make([]Record, 0, len(matches))
125		for _, m := range matches {
126			out = append(out, all[m.Index])
127			if limit > 0 && len(out) >= limit {
128				break
129			}
130		}
131		return out, nil
132	}
133	
134	func reverse(rs []Record) {
135		for i, j := 0, len(rs)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
136			rs[i], rs[j] = rs[j], rs[i]
137		}
138	}
139	
140	// newID is a sortable-enough unique id: base36 nanos + 4 random bytes.
141	func newID() string {
142		var b [4]byte
143		_, _ = rand.Read(b[:])
144		return strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().UnixNano(), 36) + "-" + hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
145	}
146
```

1	// Package engine defines the translation backend abstraction and its
2	// implementations (LLM via OpenAI-compatible APIs, free web APIs, dictionaries).
3	//
4	// The engine layer is pure Go with context.Context and imports zero TUI code:
5	// the one-shot CLI and the Bubble Tea TUI drive the identical Engine values and
6	// diverge only at presentation.
7	package engine
8	
9	import "context"
10	
11	// Mode selects what kind of lookup a Request performs.
12	type Mode int
13	
14	const (
15		// ModeTranslate is register-aware, faithful translation (the default).
16		ModeTranslate Mode = iota
17		// ModeDict is a dictionary/definition lookup.
18		ModeDict
19	)
20	
21	// Request is the single input to every engine. A Source of "" or "auto" asks
22	// the engine to detect the source language.
23	type Request struct {
24		Text    string
25		Source  string // BCP-47-ish code or "auto"/""
26		Target  string // e.g. "en", "zh"
27		Mode    Mode
28		MaxAlts int    // cap on Alternatives; 0 => engine default
29		Stream  bool   // caller wants token streaming (LLM only; others ignore)
30		Model   string // optional per-request model override (LLM engines)
31		// ModelProvider scopes Model to one provider by name; other engines ignore
32		// the override (so a copilot model id never leaks to an Ollama fallback).
33		ModelProvider string
34		Preset        string // LLM prompt style: "" => concise (LLM translate only)
35		Extra         string // extra user instructions appended to the system prompt
36	
37		// Pair marks a bidirectional "pair" request: the text is written in one of
38		// two languages (PairHome/PairAway) and must be translated into the OTHER.
39		// The LLM translate prompt uses this to detect-and-route and, critically, to
40		// never echo the input unchanged. Target still carries the caller's routed
41		// best guess (for history/display and non-LLM engines).
42		Pair     bool
43		PairHome string // one pair language (e.g. the home target, "zh-TW")
44		PairAway string // the other pair language (e.g. "en")
45	
46		// Learn marks a language-learning request. It is bidirectional (implies Pair,
47		// with PairHome=native and PairAway=foreign) and adaptive: native-language input
48		// is translated-and-taught (glosses + examples), foreign-language input is
49		// grammar-corrected-and-explained. The LLM engine answers with a strict JSON
50		// object (parsed into TranslateResult.Learn) and, because the output is
51		// structured, always runs NON-STREAMING regardless of Stream.
52		Learn bool
53	
54		// Bilingual marks a whole-document bilingual ("doc mode") request: Segments
55		// carries the full ordered document (prose to translate + code shown only as
56		// context) and the LLM returns a JSON map of prose-segment number → translation.
57		// Context-aware and single-call. LLM engines only (google/dict ignore it), and
58		// like Learn it always runs NON-STREAMING.
59		Bilingual bool
60		Segments  []Segment
61	}
62	
63	// Segment is one unit of a Bilingual document request: a prose block to translate,
64	// or a command/code block included only as surrounding context (Code == true).
65	type Segment struct {
66		Text string
67		Code bool
68	}
69	
70	// TranslateResult is the "Marvin-lite" typed result. Every engine fills what it
71	// can; zero-value fields are simply absent. It is also the history record shape.
72	type TranslateResult struct {
73		Translation    string   `json:"translation"`
74		DetectedSource string   `json:"detected_source,omitempty"`
75		Target         string   `json:"target"`
76		Alternatives   []string `json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
77		Notes          string   `json:"notes,omitempty"`
78		Confidence     float64  `json:"confidence,omitempty"`
79	
80		// Warnings records non-fatal problems, e.g. a chain engine that failed before
81		// this (fallback) engine served the result — so a downgrade is never silent.
82		Warnings []string `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
83	
84		// Truncated is set when a streamed result ended before the model finished
85		// (no terminal marker, or stop_reason=="max_tokens"). The partial text is
86		// still returned so the caller can show it, but it must not be cached or
87		// persisted as if complete. Transient: not serialized.
88		Truncated bool `json:"-"`
89	
90		// Provenance — stamped by the producing engine / chain.
91		Engine string `json:"engine,omitempty"`
92		Model  string `json:"model,omitempty"`
93	
94		// Dictionary payload (Mode == ModeDict); nil for translate mode.
95		Dictionary *DictEntry `json:"dictionary,omitempty"`
96		// Learn payload (Request.Learn); nil outside learn mode. Translation still holds
97		// the main foreign-language sentence (the corrected sentence, or the translation)
98		// so copy/history/speak keep working unchanged; the structured extras ride here.
99		Learn *LearnResult `json:"learn,omitempty"`
100		// Bilingual is the doc-mode payload: prose-segment number (1-based, as numbered
101		// in the prompt) → translation. nil outside bilingual doc mode. Transient.
102		Bilingual map[int]string `json:"-"`
103		// Suggestions is a ranked "did you mean" list, set by the dictionary engine
104		// when no exact entry was found (Dictionary and Translation stay empty). The
105		// frontend decides how to present/select — the engine no longer auto-picks.
106		Suggestions []string `json:"suggestions,omitempty"`
107	
108		// SuggestDistance is the edit distance of the best entry in Suggestions (English
109		// fuzzy lookups only; 0 when unknown/not applicable, e.g. Chinese prefix matches).
110		// The smart-dict engine reads it to tell a likely typo from a match too far off.
111		// Transient: not serialized.
112		SuggestDistance int `json:"-"`
113	}
114	
115	// DictEntry is a dictionary lookup payload (populated by the dictionary engine).
116	type DictEntry struct {
117		Word      string    `json:"word"`
118		Phonetic  string    `json:"phonetic,omitempty"`
119		Meanings  []Meaning `json:"meanings,omitempty"`
120		SourceURL string    `json:"source_url,omitempty"`
121	}
122	
123	// Meaning groups definitions by part of speech.
124	type Meaning struct {
125		PartOfSpeech string       `json:"part_of_speech"`
126		Definitions  []Definition `json:"definitions"`
127		Synonyms     []string     `json:"synonyms,omitempty"`
128		Antonyms     []string     `json:"antonyms,omitempty"`
129	}
130	
131	// Definition is a single sense of a word.
132	type Definition struct {
133		Text    string `json:"definition"`
134		Example string `json:"example,omitempty"`
135	}
136	
137	// LearnResult is the structured payload for learn/tutor mode (Request.Learn). The
138	// model fills only the fields relevant to the auto-detected direction; all glosses,
139	// explanations, and notes are written in the native (home) language.
140	type LearnResult struct {
141		Direction   string         `json:"direction"`           // "teach" (native→foreign) | "correct" (foreign→native)
142		Original    string         `json:"original"`            // the user's input as received
143		Corrected   string         `json:"corrected,omitempty"` // correct-direction: the fixed foreign sentence
144		Translation string         `json:"translation"`         // teach: foreign translation; correct: native translation of intent
145		Notes       string         `json:"notes,omitempty"`     // short tip/encouragement, in the NATIVE language
146		Issues      []LearnIssue   `json:"issues,omitempty"`    // correct-direction grammar/usage fixes
147		Vocab       []LearnGloss   `json:"vocab,omitempty"`     // teach-direction glosses
148		Examples    []LearnExample `json:"examples,omitempty"`  // teach-direction usage examples
149	}
150	
151	// LearnIssue is one grammar/usage correction (correct-direction).
152	type LearnIssue struct {
153		Span        string `json:"span"`        // the problematic fragment of the input
154		Fix         string `json:"fix"`         // the corrected fragment
155		Explanation string `json:"explanation"` // why — in the NATIVE language
156	}
157	
158	// LearnGloss is one vocabulary explanation (teach-direction).
159	type LearnGloss struct {
160		Term     string `json:"term"`               // foreign word/term
161		Pos      string `json:"pos,omitempty"`      // part of speech
162		Phonetic string `json:"phonetic,omitempty"` // KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese
163		Meaning  string `json:"meaning"`            // meaning in the NATIVE language
164	}
165	
166	// LearnExample is one usage example (teach-direction).
167	type LearnExample struct {
168		Foreign string `json:"foreign"` // example sentence in the foreign language
169		Native  string `json:"native"`  // its native-language translation
170	}
171	
172	// ChunkKind distinguishes streamed tokens from the terminal result/error.
173	type ChunkKind int
174	
175	const (
176		// ChunkToken is one streamed unit of translation text.
177		ChunkToken ChunkKind = iota
178		// ChunkDone carries the final structured result and ends the stream.
179		ChunkDone
180		// ChunkError carries a terminal error and ends the stream.
181		ChunkError
182	)
183	
184	// Chunk is one unit emitted on an engine's result channel.
185	type Chunk struct {
186		Kind   ChunkKind
187		Text   string           // token text (ChunkToken)
188		Result *TranslateResult // final result (ChunkDone)
189		Err    error            // terminal error (ChunkError)
190	}
191	
192	// Engine is the provider abstraction. Every method honors ctx cancellation.
193	//
194	// Translate returns a receive-only channel and MUST close it after sending
195	// exactly one terminal Chunk (ChunkDone or ChunkError). Streaming engines emit
196	// zero or more ChunkToken then one ChunkDone; non-streaming engines emit a
197	// single ChunkDone. This uniform "channel closed == finished" contract lets the
198	// TUI's self-resubscribing reader and the CLI's drain loop share one code path.
199	// The synchronous error return is only for immediate setup failures; all
200	// runtime/network errors flow as a terminal ChunkError.
201	type Engine interface {
202		Name() string
203		Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error)
204		Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error)
205		Available(ctx context.Context) bool
206		Supports(m Mode) bool
207	}
208	
209	// single is a helper for non-streaming engines: it returns a closed channel
210	// carrying exactly one terminal Chunk.
211	func single(res *TranslateResult, err error) <-chan Chunk {
212		ch := make(chan Chunk, 1)
213		if err != nil {
214			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: err}
215		} else {
216			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkDone, Result: res}
217		}
218		close(ch)
219		return ch
220	}
221	
222	// Drain consumes an engine channel to completion, returning the final result.
223	// It streams tokens to onToken (if non-nil) as they arrive. Used by the
224	// one-shot CLI path; the TUI drives the channel directly via its Update loop.
225	func Drain(ch <-chan Chunk, onToken func(string)) (*TranslateResult, error) {
226		for c := range ch {
227			switch c.Kind {
228			case ChunkToken:
229				if onToken != nil {
230					onToken(c.Text)
231				}
232			case ChunkDone:
233				return c.Result, nil
234			case ChunkError:
235				return nil, c.Err
236			}
237		}
238		return nil, ErrNoResult
239	}
