```text
1	# Bundle or prebuild the dictionary vs the 67 MB runtime `dict update`
2	
3	**Status**: P? — needs a spike
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` P? · `cmd/dictupdate.go` · `internal/engine/dictdata.go` · `internal/engine/localdict.go` · [release-binaries.md](release-binaries.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07. The offline bilingual dictionary (CC-CEDICT zh→en + ECDICT en→zh) is
10	**not** shipped with the binary. First use requires `translate dict update all`,
11	a one-time ~67 MB download + ECDICT sqlite build (the build "takes a minute").
12	Until then, Chinese lookups prompt to run the update and English lookups fall
13	back to dictionaryapi.dev. This is friction on a fresh machine, and it's
14	per-machine (data lands in `~/.local/share/translate/dict`).
15	
16	## Investigation
17	
18	- Acquisition today: `cmd/dictupdate.go` → `engine.DownloadCedict` (gz text) and
19	  `engine.BuildEcdictDB` (downloads ECDICT, builds a local sqlite via
20	  `modernc.org/sqlite`).
21	- The code comment marks explicit `dict update` as "the blessed path"
22	  (`AutoDownload: false`), deliberately not auto-downloading.
23	- Licensing: CC-CEDICT is **CC BY-SA 4.0** (© MDBG / Paul Denisowski); ECDICT is
24	  **MIT** (© skywind3000). Redistribution is allowed with attribution — so
25	  bundling/shipping is legally fine if attribution is preserved (already in
26	  README).
27	
28	## Options considered
29	
30	| Option | Pros | Cons |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| A. Runtime `dict update` (current) | tiny binary; user opts in; always fresh | 67 MB first-run download + minute-long build; per-machine |
33	| B. `go:embed` a trimmed/compressed DB | offline out of the box; one binary | binary balloons (tens of MB); rebuild to refresh data; embeds a snapshot |
34	| C. Ship prebuilt DB as a release asset | no per-host build; smaller than embed-all | needs the release pipeline ([release-binaries.md](release-binaries.md)); still a download |
35	| D. Prebuild sqlite in CI, `go:embed` only that | skips the slow local build step | still big; still a snapshot |
36	
37	## Current blocker / open questions
38	
39	- How big is a *trimmed* DB (common headwords only) vs full? Full ECDICT sqlite is
40	  the heavy part — measure before deciding embed vs asset.
41	- Is offline-on-first-run actually wanted, or is the API fallback + opt-in update
42	  the right default? (The author deliberately chose opt-in.)
43	- Option C couples to the release-binaries spike; do that first.
44	
45	## Decision (if any)
46	
47	`2026-07 deferred` — keep opt-in `dict update`. Reconsider embedding/shipping a
48	prebuilt DB if first-run friction becomes a real complaint, and prefer measuring
49	a trimmed-DB size before committing to `go:embed`.
50	
51	## References
52	
53	- CC-CEDICT: https://www.mdbg.net/chinese/dictionary?page=cedict
54	- ECDICT: https://github.com/skywind3000/ECDICT
55	- `go:embed`: https://pkg.go.dev/embed
56
```
</details></tool-use>

# Plan: Fix pair-mode routing for mixed-script (mostly-Latin + a few CJK) input

## Context

In bidirectional **pair mode** (`zh-TW⇄en`), pasting a mostly-English passage that
contains a few Chinese proper nouns (e.g. 李榮浩, 李白) came back **unchanged as
English** — an "English→English" no-op — and `^t` (re-pick target) didn't help.
The footer showed `detected: english` (correct), which disagreed with the actual
routing (to English), and that mismatch is the tell.

**Root cause:** `lang.PairTarget` (`internal/lang/detect.go`) routes a CJK⇄Latin
pair by `containsCJK(text)` — "does the text contain **any** CJK rune?". A single
Han character flips the whole routing to the Latin side, so mostly-English text
with a couple of Chinese names was treated as "CJK text" → target = English → the
model "translated" already-English text into English. `^t` can't change this
because the CJK-side decision ignores the target entirely; it's pure script
presence. The `detected: english` label (`lang.Detect`, whatlanggo) was correct
all along — the bug is in the **routing**, not detection.

## Change (already implemented in the working tree; awaiting approval)

`internal/lang/detect.go`
- Extract `isCJKRune(r rune) bool` (Han/Hiragana/Katakana/Hangul); `containsCJK`
  now calls it (kept — still a tested utility).
- Add `cjkDominant(text string) bool`: compares the CJK rune count against the
  number of **non-CJK words** (maximal runs of non-CJK letters, any script).
  Since one CJK rune ≈ a word, this measures which script *dominates* rather than
  mere presence — a few CJK proper nouns in a long Latin passage no longer flip
  routing, while genuinely CJK-heavy text still counts as CJK. Works for
  non-Latin "other" scripts too (e.g. zh⇄ru) because it counts any non-CJK letter.
```

182	// Translate performs a translation, streaming tokens when req.Stream is set.
183	// It always returns a channel that closes after exactly one terminal chunk, and
184	// dispatches to the Anthropic Messages API for Claude models.
185	func (e *LLMEngine) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
186		// A bilingual doc request carries its content in Segments, not Text.
187		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Text) == "" && !(req.Bilingual && len(req.Segments) > 0) {
188			return nil, ErrEmptyInput
189		}
190		model := NormalizeModelID(e.cfg.Model)
191		// Apply a per-request model override only when it targets this provider, so a
192		// copilot model id never reaches an Ollama fallback (which would 404).
193		if req.Model != "" && (req.ModelProvider == "" || req.ModelProvider == e.cfg.Name) {
194			model = NormalizeModelID(req.Model)
195		}
196		if isAnthropicModel(model) {
197			return e.translateAnthropic(ctx, req, model)
198		}
199		return e.translateOpenAI(ctx, req, model)
200	}

248	func usableModel(id string, endpoints []string) bool {

261	// finalize builds the terminal result from the accumulated translation text.
262	func (e *LLMEngine) finalize(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
263		res := &TranslateResult{
264			Translation: strings.TrimSpace(full),
265			Target:      req.Target,
266			Engine:      e.cfg.Name,
267			Model:       model,
268		}
269		// The plain-text prompt returns only the translation, so fill the detected
270		// source offline when the caller asked to auto-detect.
271		if src := strings.TrimSpace(req.Source); src == "" || src == "auto" {
272			res.DetectedSource = lang.Detect(req.Text)
273		}
274		return res
275	}

278	// tutor prompt for learn mode, else the plain translate prompt.
279	func promptFor(req Request) (system, user string) {
280		switch {
281		case req.Bilingual:
282			return buildBilingualPrompt(req)
283		case req.Learn:
284			return buildLearnPrompt(req)
285		default:
286			return buildTranslatePrompt(req)
287		}
288	}

290	// finalizeResult builds the terminal result, parsing structured learn output when
291	// the request asked for it.
292	func (e *LLMEngine) finalizeResult(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
293		switch {
294		case req.Bilingual:
295			return e.finalizeBilingual(full, model, req)
296		case req.Learn:
297			return e.finalizeLearn(full, model, req)
298		default:
299			return e.finalize(full, model, req)
300		}

303	// finalizeLearn parses the model's structured JSON reply into a LearnResult. It is
304	// defensive — it strips a markdown fence and slices to the outermost object before
305	// unmarshalling — and on any failure falls back to the raw text as the translation
306	// (with a warning), so a malformed reply degrades gracefully instead of erroring.
307	// res.Target is set to the FOREIGN (away) language because res.Translation always
308	// holds the foreign sentence (the corrected sentence, or the translation).
309	func (e *LLMEngine) finalizeLearn(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
310		res := &TranslateResult{
311			Target: req.PairAway,
312			Engine: e.cfg.Name,
313			Model:  model,
314		}
315		if src := strings.TrimSpace(req.Source); src == "" || src == "auto" {
316			res.DetectedSource = lang.Detect(req.Text)
317		}
318		lr, err := parseLearn(full)
319		if err != nil {
320			res.Translation = strings.TrimSpace(full)
321			res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, "learn: could not parse structured output — showing the raw reply")
322			return res
323		}
324		lr.Direction = learnDirection(req) // trust offline detection over the model's guess
325		if strings.TrimSpace(lr.Original) == "" {
326			lr.Original = req.Text
327		}
328		res.Learn = lr
329		if lr.Direction == "correct" && strings.TrimSpace(lr.Corrected) != "" {
330			res.Translation = strings.TrimSpace(lr.Corrected)
331		} else {
332			res.Translation = strings.TrimSpace(lr.Translation)
333		}
334		return res
335	}
336	
337	// parseLearn extracts and unmarshals a LearnResult from a model reply, returning an
338	// error when the JSON is absent/invalid or carries no main sentence.
339	func parseLearn(full string) (*LearnResult, error) {
340		var lr LearnResult
341		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(extractJSON(full)), &lr); err != nil {
342			return nil, err
343		}
344		if strings.TrimSpace(lr.Translation) == "" && strings.TrimSpace(lr.Corrected) == "" {
345			return nil, fmt.Errorf("learn: empty structured result")
346		}
347		return &lr, nil
348	}
349	
350	// finalizeBilingual parses the model's JSON reply (prose-segment number → translation)
351	// into TranslateResult.Bilingual. Defensive like finalizeLearn: on any parse failure
352	// it returns an empty result + a warning so the caller can fall back to per-block mode.
353	func (e *LLMEngine) finalizeBilingual(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
354		res := &TranslateResult{
355			Target: req.Target,
356			Engine: e.cfg.Name,
357			Model:  model,
358		}
359		m, err := parseBilingual(full)
360		if err != nil {
361			res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, "bilingual: could not parse structured output")
362			return res
363		}
364		res.Bilingual = m
365		return res
366	}
367	
368	// parseBilingual extracts a {"<n>": "<translation>"} JSON object from a model reply
369	// and converts it to a map keyed by the integer segment number, ignoring non-numeric
370	// keys defensively.
371	func parseBilingual(full string) (map[int]string, error) {
372		var raw map[string]string
373		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(extractJSON(full)), &raw); err != nil {
374			return nil, err
375		}
376		out := make(map[int]string, len(raw))
377		for k, v := range raw {
378			n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(k))
379			if err != nil {
380				continue
381			}
382			out[n] = v
383		}
384		if len(out) == 0 {
385			return nil, fmt.Errorf("bilingual: no numeric segment keys")
386		}
387		return out, nil
388	}
389	
390	// extractJSON returns the outermost JSON object in s, tolerating a surrounding
391	// markdown code fence or stray prose around it.
392	func extractJSON(s string) string {
393		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
394		if strings.HasPrefix(s, "```") { // strip ```json … ``` fence
395			if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
396				s = s[i+1:]
397			}
398			s = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(s), "```"))
399		}
400		start := strings.IndexByte(s, '{')
401		end := strings.LastIndexByte(s, '}')
402		if start >= 0 && end > start {
403			return s[start : end+1]
404		}
405		return s
406	}

408	// markTruncated flags a result whose stream ended before the model finished, so
409	// the caller keeps the partial text but never treats it as a complete answer.
410	func markTruncated(res *TranslateResult) {
411		res.Truncated = true
412		res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings,
413			"output was cut off before completion (stream truncated) — press Enter to retry")
414	}

416	// translateOpenAI uses the OpenAI /chat/completions endpoint.
417	func (e *LLMEngine) translateOpenAI(ctx context.Context, req Request, model string) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
418		system, user := promptFor(req)
419		stream := req.Stream && !req.Learn && !req.Bilingual // structured JSON output: parse at done
420		body := chatRequest{
421			Model: model,
422			Messages: []chatMessage{
423				{Role: "system", Content: system},
424				{Role: "user", Content: user},
425			},
426			Stream: stream,
427		}
428		buf, err := json.Marshal(body)
429		if err != nil {
430			return nil, err
431		}
432		httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, e.endpoint("/chat/completions"), bytes.NewReader(buf))
433		if err != nil {
434			return nil, err
435		}
436		httpReq.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
437		if stream {
438			httpReq.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
439		}
440		e.auth(httpReq)
441	
442		ch := make(chan Chunk, 32) // buffered so a fast stream doesn't block on renders
443		go func() {
444			defer close(ch)
445			resp, err := e.http.Do(httpReq)
446			if err != nil {
447				ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)}
448				return
449			}
450			defer resp.Body.Close()
451			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
452				ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: e.httpError(resp)}
453				return
454			}
455	
456			var full strings.Builder
457			complete := true
458			if stream {
459				var err error
460				complete, err = e.readSSE(ctx, resp.Body, ch, &full)
461				if err != nil {
462					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: err}
463					return
464				}
465			} else {
466				var cr chatResponse
467				if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&cr); err != nil {
468					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: decode response: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)}
469					return
470				}
471				if cr.Error != nil {
472					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", e.cfg.Name, cr.Error.Message)}
473					return
474				}
475				if len(cr.Choices) == 0 {
476					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: empty response", e.cfg.Name)}
477					return
478				}
479				full.WriteString(cr.Choices[0].Message.Content)
480				complete = cr.Choices[0].FinishReason != "length" // "length" => hit the cap
481			}
482			res := e.finalizeResult(full.String(), model, req)
483			if !complete {
484				markTruncated(res)
485			}
486			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkDone, Result: res}
487		}()
488		return ch, nil
489	}

570	// anthropicAuth sets the Anthropic auth header (x-api-key, not Bearer). The
571	// copilot-proxy needs none, so an empty key yields no header.
572	func (e *LLMEngine) anthropicAuth(r *http.Request) {
573		if e.key != "" {
574			r.Header.Set("x-api-key", e.key)
575		}
576	}
577	
578	// readSSE parses an OpenAI-style event stream, emitting a ChunkToken per content
579	// delta and accumulating the full text into full. It reports complete=true only
580	// when the stream ended on a terminal marker ([DONE] or finish_reason=="stop");
581	// a stream that closes with no marker, or on finish_reason=="length", is treated
582	// as truncated so the caller can flag it rather than silently accept partial text.
583	func (e *LLMEngine) readSSE(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, ch chan<- Chunk, full *strings.Builder) (bool, error) {
584		sc := bufio.NewScanner(r)
585		sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), 1<<20) // tolerate long SSE lines
586		sawDone := false
587		finish := ""
588		for sc.Scan() {
589			line := sc.Text()
590			if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "data:") {
591				continue
592			}
593			payload := strings.TrimSpace(line[len("data:"):])
594			if payload == "[DONE]" {
595				sawDone = true
596				break
597			}
598			var d streamDelta
599			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(payload), &d) != nil || len(d.Choices) == 0 {
600				continue
601			}
602			if fr := d.Choices[0].FinishReason; fr != nil && *fr != "" {
603				finish = *fr
604			}
605			tok := d.Choices[0].Delta.Content
606			if tok == "" {
607				continue
608			}
609			full.WriteString(tok)
610			select {
611			case ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkToken, Text: tok}:
612			case <-ctx.Done():
613				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, ctx.Err())
614			}
615		}
616		if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
617			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)
618		}
619		complete := finish != "length" && (sawDone || finish == "stop")
620		return complete, nil
621	}
622	
623	// readAnthropicSSE parses an Anthropic Messages event stream, emitting a
624	// ChunkToken per text_delta and accumulating the full text into full. It reports
625	// complete=true only when a terminal marker arrived (a message_stop event, or a
626	// message_delta with a natural stop_reason); a stream that closes with neither,
627	// or on stop_reason=="max_tokens", is treated as truncated.
628	func (e *LLMEngine) readAnthropicSSE(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, ch chan<- Chunk, full *strings.Builder) (bool, error) {
629		sc := bufio.NewScanner(r)
630		sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), 1<<20)
631		sawStop := false
632		stopReason := ""
633		for sc.Scan() {
634			line := sc.Text()
635			if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "data:") {
636				continue // ignore "event:" and blank lines
637			}
638			payload := strings.TrimSpace(line[len("data:"):])
639			if payload == "" {
640				continue
641			}
642			var ev anthropicStreamEvent
643			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(payload), &ev) != nil {
644				continue
645			}
646			if ev.Error != nil {
647				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", e.cfg.Name, ev.Error.Message)
648			}
649			switch ev.Type {
650			case "message_stop":
651				sawStop = true
652				continue
653			case "message_delta":
654				if ev.Delta.StopReason != "" {
655					stopReason = ev.Delta.StopReason
656				}
657				continue
658			}
659			if ev.Type != "content_block_delta" || ev.Delta.Type != "text_delta" || ev.Delta.Text == "" {
660				continue
661			}
662			full.WriteString(ev.Delta.Text)
663			select {
664			case ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkToken, Text: ev.Delta.Text}:
665			case <-ctx.Done():
666				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, ctx.Err())
667			}
668		}
669		if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
670			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)
671		}
672		complete := stopReason != "max_tokens" &&
673			(sawStop || stopReason == "end_turn" || stopReason == "stop_sequence")
674		return complete, nil
675	}
676	
677	// httpError reads an error body (best effort) into a descriptive error.
678	func (e *LLMEngine) httpError(resp *http.Response) error {
679		b, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 2<<10))
680		msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
681		if msg == "" {
682			msg = resp.Status
683		}
684		return fmt.Errorf("%s: http %d: %s", e.cfg.Name, resp.StatusCode, msg)
685	}
686
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Translate
2	
3	Translate, define, and speak text from Raycast — backed by the local
4	[`translate`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/translate) CLI. Multi-engine
5	auto-fallback (local LLM via copilot-proxy / Ollama, keyless Google, offline
6	CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries), unified history, and free TTS.
7	
8	## Requirements
9	
10	This extension **shells out to the `translate` CLI** — it does not translate on its
11	own. Install the binary first:
12	
13	```sh
14	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
15	# or, with a Go toolchain:
16	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest
17	```
18	
19	On first run, `translate init` sets up your providers/config
20	(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`). The extension auto-detects the binary in
21	`~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, and `~/go/bin`; if it lives
22	elsewhere, set **“translate binary path”** in the extension preferences. (If it
23	isn’t found, the extension shows an install-instructions screen instead of failing.)
24	
25	> **Note:** Raycast runs under a restricted `PATH` and reads no shell env, so API
26	> keys must live in `translate`’s config file (via `translate init`), not in
27	> `~/.zshrc`. “Translate Selection” and selection-prefill need macOS **Accessibility**
28	> permission for Raycast (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).
29	
30	## Commands
31	
32	- **Translate** — type to translate; pick the target language; ⌘↵ for a streaming
33	  view; actions for Copy / Paste / Speak and an engine override.
34	- **Translate Selection** — grabs your selection (or clipboard) and opens Translate
35	  prefilled and editable.
36	- **Define** — dictionary lookup with phonetics and meanings (offline dictionaries,
37	  LLM fallback, and suggestions).
38	- **History** — browse and search your past translations.
39	
40	## Preferences
41	
42	Binary path, default target language, engine, model tier, live-translate debounce,
43	and how Translate prefills its input (selection / clipboard / nothing). Leave
44	**target / tier / debounce** empty to inherit them from the `translate` config
45	(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`, read via `config show --json`) — configure them
46	once and Raycast honors them; set a preference to override the config for Raycast.
47
```

```text
1	# Raycast integration for `translate`
2	
3	Bring `translate` into [Raycast](https://raycast.com) — translate from root
4	search or a global hotkey, backed by the **existing `translate` binary** (this
5	directory contains no translation logic; it shells out to the CLI).
6	
7	There are two independent tracks. **The TypeScript extension is the primary,
8	full-featured path;** the script commands are an optional zero-Node fallback.
9	
10	| Track | Path | Build | Best for |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| **TypeScript extension** (primary) | [`extension/`](extension/) | `npm` / `ray` | full UI: live translate, selection prefill, define, history, engine switch, streaming |
13	| **Script Commands** (bash, optional) | [`script-commands/`](script-commands/) | none | zero-Node fallback; one-shot translate/define |
14	
15	Everything requires the `translate` CLI on the machine:
16	
17	```sh
18	just install                                  # → ~/.local/bin/translate
19	# or
20	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
21	```
22	
23	## Track A — Script Commands (optional)
24	
25	The TypeScript extension (Track B) supersedes these; keep them only if you want a
26	zero-Node fallback that runs without `ray develop`.
27	
28	```sh
29	just raycast-scripts   # chmod +x the scripts and print the directory to add
30	```
31	
32	Then, **one time** in Raycast: **Settings → Extensions → Script Commands →
33	Add Script Directory** → select `raycast/script-commands`. (There is no CLI to
34	register a script directory; this step is manual.)
35	
36	Commands: **Translate Text** (language dropdown + text), **Translate & Copy**
37	(copies the result; leave the text blank to translate the clipboard — Script
38	Commands can't read the selection), **Define Word** (dictionary lookup).
39	
40	## Track B — TypeScript extension (local dev)
41	
42	```sh
43	just raycast-dev       # npm install (first run) + `ray develop`
44	```
45	
46	`ray develop` registers the extension with the running Raycast app and hot-reloads.
47	Four commands appear in root search and **stay installed after you stop
48	`ray develop`** — no store publish needed for personal use:
49	**Translate** (type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
50	streaming ⌘↵, Copy/Paste/Speak), **Translate Selection** (grabs the selection or
51	clipboard and opens Translate prefilled, with an optional target-language argument),
52	**Define** (dictionary lookup + LLM fallback), and **History** (browse/search past
53	translations). `just raycast-build` / `just raycast-lint` type-check and lint.
54	
55	Configure the binary path and defaults in the extension's **Preferences**
56	(the binary is auto-probed in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`,
57	`/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`; override with an absolute path if it lives elsewhere).
58	Translate-as-you-type is **debounced** (default 700 ms, tunable via the
59	"Live translate debounce" preference) and cancels superseded in-flight requests,
60	so typing a phrase doesn't fire an LLM call per keystroke. Opening **Translate**
61	seeds the input from the current selection (or clipboard) per the "Prefill input
62	from" preference — set it to "Nothing" to always start empty.
63	
64	## Gotchas (both tracks)
65	
66	- **Raycast runs under launchd with a restricted PATH** — it does *not* inherit
67	  your shell's PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `command not found` /
68	  `spawn translate ENOENT`. Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path. Always test
69	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
70	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
71	- **API keys must live in `translate`'s config**, not shell env — a key exported
72	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd. Put providers/keys in
73	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml` (run `translate init`); `HOME` is passed
74	  through so the CLI finds it.
75	- **Exit code is 0 even when an engine fails** (it falls back). The extension
76	  surfaces `warnings[]` from `--json`; the plain-text scripts don't show them.
77	
78	See [`../docs/raycast-extension.md`](../docs/raycast-extension.md) for how Raycast
79	extensions work, the full integration-tier comparison, and the competitive
80	landscape. Store publishing is tracked in
81	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
82
```

8	// datedSuffix matches trailing dated model-id forms like "-20250514" or
9	// "@2025-05-14" that the copilot-proxy rejects.
10	var datedSuffix = regexp.MustCompile(`(-\d{8}|@\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})$`)
11	
12	// NormalizeModelID canonicalizes a model id for the copilot-proxy and other
13	// OpenAI-compatible backends:
14	//
15	//   - strips a trailing "[1m]" (or any "[...]") context-window hint, which is a
16	//     Claude-Code-only annotation the proxy rejects,
17	//   - drops a trailing dated suffix ("-YYYYMMDD" / "@YYYY-MM-DD"),
18	//   - trims surrounding whitespace.
19	//
20	// It leaves hyphenated ids like "claude-sonnet-5" and "gpt-5.4-mini" and Ollama
21	// ids like "llama3.2:3b" untouched.
22	func NormalizeModelID(id string) string {
23		id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
24		if i := strings.Index(id, "["); i >= 0 {
25			id = strings.TrimSpace(id[:i])
26		}
27		id = datedSuffix.ReplaceAllString(id, "")
28		return id
29	}

24			return dir
25		}

31	func EcdictDBPath(dir string) string { return filepath.Join(DictDir(dir), "ecdict.db") }

34	  word TEXT, word_lc TEXT, phonetic TEXT, translation TEXT,
35	  definition TEXT, pos TEXT, frq INTEGER, exchange TEXT);`
36	
37	// DownloadCedict fetches the gzipped CC-CEDICT, decompresses it, and writes the
38	// plain text file atomically (~9.4 MB).
39	func DownloadCedict(ctx context.Context, url, dst string, prog func(string)) error {
40		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o700); err != nil {
41			return err
42		}
43		if prog != nil {
44			prog("downloading CC-CEDICT…")
45		}
46		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
47		if err != nil {
48			return err
49		}
50		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
51		if err != nil {
52			return err
53		}
54		defer resp.Body.Close()
55		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
56			return fmt.Errorf("cedict download: http %d", resp.StatusCode)
57		}
58		gz, err := gzip.NewReader(resp.Body)
59		if err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		defer gz.Close()
63	
64		tmp := dst + ".tmp"
65		f, err := os.Create(tmp)
66		if err != nil {
67			return err
68		}
69		if _, err := io.Copy(f, gz); err != nil {
70			f.Close()
71			os.Remove(tmp)
72			return err
73		}
74		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
75			os.Remove(tmp)
76			return err
77		}
78		return os.Rename(tmp, dst)
79	}
80	
81	// BuildEcdictDB downloads the ECDICT CSV (~63 MB, MIT) and builds a queryable
82	// SQLite database (~80-100 MB) from it, atomically. Streams the CSV so it never
83	// holds the whole file in memory.
84	func BuildEcdictDB(ctx context.Context, csvURL, dbPath string, prog func(string)) (err error) {
85		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dbPath), 0o700); err != nil {
86			return err
87		}
88		if prog != nil {
89			prog("downloading ECDICT CSV (~63 MB)…")
90		}
91		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, csvURL, nil)
92		if err != nil {
93			return err
94		}
95		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
96		if err != nil {
97			return err
98		}
99		defer resp.Body.Close()
100		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
101			return fmt.Errorf("ecdict download: http %d", resp.StatusCode)
102		}
103	
104		tmp := dbPath + ".tmp"
105		_ = os.Remove(tmp)
106		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+tmp+"?_pragma=journal_mode(off)&_pragma=synchronous(off)")
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		// On any error, close and remove the partial db.
111		defer func() {
112			if err != nil {
113				db.Close()
114				os.Remove(tmp)
115			}
116		}()
117	
118		if _, err = db.ExecContext(ctx, ecdictSchema); err != nil {
119			return err
120		}
121		if prog != nil {
122			prog("importing entries…")
123		}
124		tx, err := db.BeginTx(ctx, nil)
125		if err != nil {
126			return err
127		}
128		stmt, err := tx.PrepareContext(ctx, `INSERT INTO entries(word,word_lc,phonetic,translation,definition,pos,frq,exchange) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`)
129		if err != nil {
130			return err
131		}
132	
133		r := csv.NewReader(resp.Body)
134		r.FieldsPerRecord = -1 // tolerate ragged rows
135		r.LazyQuotes = true
136		if _, err = r.Read(); err != nil { // header row
137			return err
138		}
139		n := 0
140		for {
141			if err = ctx.Err(); err != nil {
142				return err
143			}
144			rec, rerr := r.Read()
145			if rerr == io.EOF {
146				break
147			}
148			if rerr != nil || len(rec) < 4 {
149				continue
150			}
151			frq := 0
152			if len(rec) > 9 {
153				frq, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(rec[9]))
154			}
155			pos, exchange := "", ""
156			if len(rec) > 4 {
157				pos = rec[4]
158			}
159			if len(rec) > 10 {
160				exchange = rec[10]
161			}
162			if _, err = stmt.ExecContext(ctx, rec[0], strings.ToLower(rec[0]), rec[1], rec[3], rec[2], pos, frq, exchange); err != nil {
163				return err
164			}
165			n++
166		}
167		if err = tx.Commit(); err != nil {
168			return err
169		}
170		if _, err = db.ExecContext(ctx, `CREATE INDEX idx_word_lc ON entries(word_lc)`); err != nil {
171			return err
172		}
173		if err = db.Close(); err != nil {
174			return err
175		}
176		if prog != nil {
177			prog(fmt.Sprintf("built %d entries", n))
178		}
179		return os.Rename(tmp, dbPath)
180	}

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`

```text
1	# Raycast can't find `translate` (`spawn translate ENOENT` / "command not found") though it works in a terminal
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): a Raycast Script Command prints `translate: command not found`; a Raycast TS extension throws `Error: spawn translate ENOENT`; the exact same command works fine in a terminal but not from Raycast root search; translation works from the shell but the Raycast command errors or shows nothing.
4	**First seen**: 2026-07 (anticipated — designed around, not yet hit in prod)
5	**Affects**: Raycast (macOS) Script Commands + TypeScript extensions on this host; any GUI/launchd-launched process that calls the `translate` binary by bare name.
6	
7	## Symptom
8	
9	Calling `translate` by bare name from Raycast fails, e.g. a script's
10	`translate "$2" --to "$1"` yields `command not found`, or an extension's
11	`execFile("translate", …)` / `spawn("translate")` throws:
12	
13	```
14	Error: spawn translate ENOENT
15	```
16	
17	The identical invocation succeeds in Terminal/iTerm, which makes it look like the
18	binary is "missing" only under Raycast.
19	
20	## Root cause
21	
22	Raycast is launched by the macOS GUI (launchd), and GUI-launched processes do
23	**not** source your interactive shell's rc files (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`). So
24	`process.env.PATH` inside a Raycast extension/script is the minimal launchd PATH
25	and does **not** include `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, or
26	`~/go/bin` — exactly where `translate` gets installed (`go install` / `just install`
27	→ `~/.local/bin`; Homebrew → `/opt/homebrew/bin`). A bare-name lookup then fails.
28	
29	## Workaround
30	
31	Resolve an **absolute** path to the binary instead of trusting PATH.
32	
33	- Script Commands ([`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/)) —
34	  probe known dirs (already baked into every script):
35	
36	  ```sh
37	  find_translate() {
38	    for d in "$HOME/.local/bin" /opt/homebrew/bin /usr/local/bin "$HOME/go/bin"; do
39	      [ -x "$d/translate" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$d/translate"; return 0; }
40	    done
41	    command -v translate 2>/dev/null && return 0
42	    return 1
43	  }
44	  ```
45	
46	- TS extension ([`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
47	  — a `binaryPath` preference first, then the same 4-dir probe (`resolveBinary()`).
48	
49	Probe order must keep `~/.local/bin` **first** — the blessed install location
50	(see sibling below) — so a stray copy elsewhere can't win.
51	
52	## Prevention
53	
54	- Never call bare `translate` from any Raycast surface; always resolve an absolute
55	  path (preference or probe).
56	- **Test from Raycast, not a terminal.** A terminal inherits your full PATH and
57	  will happily find the binary, masking the bug entirely.
58	
59	## Related
60	
61	- Sibling: [duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md](duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md)
62	  (why `~/.local/bin` must be first in the probe)
63	- Reference: [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) "Gotchas"
64	- Backlog: `TODO.md` P? "Publish the Raycast extension to the store" ·
65	  [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md)
66
```
</details></tool-use>

34			Text:         r.Text,
35			Source:       r.Source,
36			Target:       r.Target,
37			Preset:       r.Preset,
38			Instructions: r.Instructions,

46		var req translateRequest
47		if !decodeJSON(w, r, &req) {
48			return
49		}

51			writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "empty_input", `field "text" is required`)
52			return
53		}
54		res, err := h.svc.Translate(r.Context(), req.params())
55		if err != nil {

57			return

59		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)

76		res, err := h.svc.Define(r.Context(), req.Word)
77		if err != nil {
78			writeEngineError(w, err)
79			return
80		}
81		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)
82	}
83	
84	// history serves GET /v1/history?q=&limit=. With q it fuzzy-searches, else it
85	// returns the most recent records. Token-guarded (personal data).
86	func (h *handlers) history(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
87		q := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("q"))
88		limit := parseLimit(r.URL.Query().Get("limit"), 20)
89		var (
90			recs []store.Record
91			err  error
92		)
93		if q != "" {
94			recs, err = h.svc.HistorySearch(r.Context(), q, limit)
95		} else {
96			recs, err = h.svc.HistoryRecent(r.Context(), limit)
97		}
98		if err != nil {
99			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "history_error", err.Error())
100			return
101		}
102		if recs == nil {
103			recs = []store.Record{} // encode [] not null when history is empty/disabled
104		}
105		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, recs)
106	}
107	
108	func (h *handlers) healthz(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
109		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
110	}
111	
112	// requireToken wraps a handler with bearer-token auth when a token is configured.
113	// With no token, it is a pass-through (loopback is the only guard).
114	func (h *handlers) requireToken(next http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
115		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
116			if h.token != "" {
117				got := bearerToken(r.Header.Get("Authorization"))
118				if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(got), []byte(h.token)) != 1 {
119					writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "missing or invalid bearer token")
120					return
121				}
122			}
123			next(w, r)
124		}
125	}
126	
127	// bearerToken extracts the token from an "Authorization: Bearer <token>" header.
128	func bearerToken(header string) string {
129		const prefix = "Bearer "
130		if len(header) >= len(prefix) && strings.EqualFold(header[:len(prefix)], prefix) {
131			return strings.TrimSpace(header[len(prefix):])
132		}
133		return ""
134	}
135	
136	// parseLimit parses a positive integer limit, falling back to def.
137	func parseLimit(s string, def int) int {
138		if s == "" {
139			return def
140		}
141		n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
142		if err != nil || n <= 0 {
143			return def
144		}
145		return n
146	}
147

15	// translateInput is the `translate` tool's arguments. Descriptions come from the
16	// jsonschema tags (the SDK infers the input schema from this struct).
17	type translateInput struct {
18		Text   string `json:"text" jsonschema:"the text to translate"`
19		Target string `json:"target,omitempty" jsonschema:"target language code, e.g. en or zh-TW (optional; server default otherwise)"`
20		Source string `json:"source,omitempty" jsonschema:"source language code, or auto to detect (optional)"`
21	}

23	// defineInput is the `define` tool's arguments.
24	type defineInput struct {
25		Word string `json:"word" jsonschema:"the word or short term to look up"`
26	}
27	
28	// historyInput is the `history` tool's arguments.
29	type historyInput struct {
30		Query string `json:"query,omitempty" jsonschema:"fuzzy search query; omit for the most recent entries"`
31		Limit int    `json:"limit,omitempty" jsonschema:"maximum number of records to return (default 20)"`
32	}
33	
34	// historyOutput wraps the record list (MCP structured output must be an object).
35	type historyOutput struct {
36		Records []store.Record `json:"records"`
37	}
38	
39	// translateHandler translates text. The structured output is the full
40	// TranslateResult; the text content is a human-readable rendering.
41	func translateHandler(svc Service) mcp.ToolHandlerFor[translateInput, engine.TranslateResult] {
42		return func(ctx context.Context, _ *mcp.CallToolRequest, in translateInput) (*mcp.CallToolResult, engine.TranslateResult, error) {
43			res, err := svc.Translate(ctx, appcore.Params{Text: in.Text, Target: in.Target, Source: in.Source})
44			if err != nil {
45				return toolError(err), engine.TranslateResult{}, nil
46			}
47			return textResult(renderTranslation(res)), *res, nil
48		}
49	}
50	
51	// defineHandler looks up a word. Structured output is the full TranslateResult
52	// (dictionary payload or suggestions); text content is a readable rendering.
53	func defineHandler(svc Service) mcp.ToolHandlerFor[defineInput, engine.TranslateResult] {
54		return func(ctx context.Context, _ *mcp.CallToolRequest, in defineInput) (*mcp.CallToolResult, engine.TranslateResult, error) {
55			res, err := svc.Define(ctx, in.Word)
56			if err != nil {
57				return toolError(err), engine.TranslateResult{}, nil
58			}
59			return textResult(renderDefine(res)), *res, nil
60		}
61	}
62	
63	// historyHandler lists or searches translation history.
64	func historyHandler(svc Service) mcp.ToolHandlerFor[historyInput, historyOutput] {
65		return func(ctx context.Context, _ *mcp.CallToolRequest, in historyInput) (*mcp.CallToolResult, historyOutput, error) {
66			limit := in.Limit
67			if limit <= 0 {
68				limit = 20
69			}
70			var (
71				recs []store.Record
72				err  error
73			)
74			if strings.TrimSpace(in.Query) != "" {
75				recs, err = svc.HistorySearch(ctx, in.Query, limit)
76			} else {
77				recs, err = svc.HistoryRecent(ctx, limit)
78			}
79			if err != nil {
80				return toolError(err), historyOutput{}, nil
81			}
82			return textResult(renderHistory(recs)), historyOutput{Records: recs}, nil
83		}
84	}
85	
86	// textResult builds a successful result carrying human-readable text. The SDK
87	// auto-populates StructuredContent from the typed Out value.
88	func textResult(text string) *mcp.CallToolResult {
89		return &mcp.CallToolResult{Content: []mcp.Content{&mcp.TextContent{Text: text}}}
90	}
91	
92	// toolError reports a tool-level failure as content (IsError), per the MCP spec —
93	// not as a protocol error — so the model can see what went wrong.
94	func toolError(err error) *mcp.CallToolResult {
95		return &mcp.CallToolResult{
96			IsError: true,
97			Content: []mcp.Content{&mcp.TextContent{Text: err.Error()}},
98		}
99	}
100	
101	func renderTranslation(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
102		var b strings.Builder
103		b.WriteString(res.Translation)
104		if len(res.Alternatives) > 0 {
105			b.WriteString("\n\nAlternatives:")
106			for _, a := range res.Alternatives {
107				b.WriteString("\n- " + a)
108			}
109		}
110		if s := strings.TrimSpace(res.Notes); s != "" {
111			b.WriteString("\n\nNotes: " + s)
112		}
113		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
114	}
115	
116	func renderDefine(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
117		d := res.Dictionary
118		if d == nil {
119			if len(res.Suggestions) > 0 {
120				return "No exact match. Did you mean: " + strings.Join(res.Suggestions, ", ")
121			}
122			return res.Translation
123		}
124		var b strings.Builder
125		b.WriteString(d.Word)
126		if d.Phonetic != "" {
127			b.WriteString("  " + d.Phonetic)
128		}
129		for _, m := range d.Meanings {
130			b.WriteString("\n" + m.PartOfSpeech)
131			for i, def := range m.Definitions {
132				if i >= 4 {
133					break
134				}
135				b.WriteString("\n  • " + def.Text)
136				if def.Example != "" {
137					b.WriteString("\n    \"" + def.Example + "\"")
138				}
139			}
140		}
141		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
142	}
143	
144	func renderHistory(recs []store.Record) string {
145		if len(recs) == 0 {
146			return "(no history)"
147		}
148		var b strings.Builder
149		for _, r := range recs {
150			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s → %s  [%s→%s]\n", r.Input, r.Output, r.SourceLang, r.TargetLang)
151		}
152		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
153	}

12	// EffectiveTarget applies pair mode: home-language input → away, else → home.
13	// It is the single source of truth for pair routing, shared by the one-shot CLI
14	// and the Service.
15	func EffectiveTarget(pair bool, home, away, text string) string {
16		if pair && away != "" {
17			t := lang.PairTarget(home, away, text)
18			debug.Logf("pair route: home=%s away=%s text=%q → target=%s", home, away, clip(text, 30), t)
19			return t
20		}
21		return home
22	}
23	
24	// clip shortens a string for a single-line debug label.
25	func clip(s string, n int) string {
26		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
27		r := []rune(s)
28		if len(r) > n {
29			return string(r[:n]) + "…"
30		}
31		return s
32	}
33	
34	// ToRecord builds a history Record from a translation result. When the source was
35	// "auto", the engine's detected language is substituted so history stays specific.
36	func ToRecord(res *engine.TranslateResult, input, source, target string) store.Record {
37		src := source
38		if src == "auto" && res.DetectedSource != "" {
39			src = res.DetectedSource
40		}
41		return store.Record{
42			SourceLang:   src,
43			TargetLang:   target,
44			Engine:       res.Engine,
45			Model:        res.Model,
46			Input:        input,
47			Output:       res.Translation,
48			Alternatives: res.Alternatives,
49			Notes:        res.Notes,
50		}
51	}

1	package engine
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"sync"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/debug"
10	)
11	
12	// Chain is the AUTO fallback router. It tries engines in configured order and
13	// fails over to the next one when the current engine is known-down or fails
14	// before producing any token. Once tokens have streamed, a mid-stream error is
15	// surfaced rather than restarting on another engine (which would garble output);
16	// the common "provider not running" case fails at connect time, pre-token, and
17	// switches cleanly.
18	type Chain struct {
19		engines []Engine
20		ttl     time.Duration
21	
22		mu    sync.Mutex
23		avail map[string]probeCache
24	}
25	
26	type probeCache struct {
27		ok bool
28		at time.Time
29	}
30	
31	// NewChain builds a chain from engines in priority order. ttl is how long a
32	// health verdict is cached (default 5s).
33	func NewChain(engines []Engine, ttl time.Duration) *Chain {
34		if ttl <= 0 {
35			ttl = 5 * time.Second
36		}
37		return &Chain{engines: engines, ttl: ttl, avail: map[string]probeCache{}}
38	}
39	
40	// Name reports the chain as the "auto" engine.
41	func (c *Chain) Name() string { return "auto" }
42	
43	// Supports reports true if any member supports the mode.
44	func (c *Chain) Supports(m Mode) bool {
45		for _, e := range c.engines {
46			if e.Supports(m) {
47				return true
48			}
49		}
50		return false
51	}
52	
53	// recentlyDown reports whether we have a fresh "down" verdict for e, so we can
54	// skip it without paying a probe on the hot path. Engines are otherwise tried
55	// optimistically (no pre-probe latency on the happy path).
56	func (c *Chain) recentlyDown(e Engine) bool {
57		c.mu.Lock()
58		defer c.mu.Unlock()
59		pc, ok := c.avail[e.Name()]
60		return ok && !pc.ok && time.Since(pc.at) < c.ttl
61	}
62	
63	func (c *Chain) mark(e Engine, ok bool) {
64		c.mu.Lock()
65		c.avail[e.Name()] = probeCache{ok: ok, at: time.Now()}
66		c.mu.Unlock()
67	}
68	
69	func (c *Chain) candidates(m Mode) []Engine {
70		var out []Engine
71		for _, e := range c.engines {
72			if e.Supports(m) {
73				out = append(out, e)
74			}
75		}
76		return out
77	}
78	
79	// Translate proxies the first working engine's stream. Failover happens only
80	// before the first token.
81	func (c *Chain) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
82		cands := c.candidates(req.Mode)
83		if len(cands) == 0 {
84			return nil, ErrNoEngineForMode
85		}
86		out := make(chan Chunk, 32)
87		go func() {
88			defer close(out)
89			var lastErr error
90			var warns []string // reasons earlier engines were skipped/failed
91			for _, e := range cands {
92				if ctx.Err() != nil { // request abandoned (e.g. user typed more)
93					out <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: ctx.Err()}
94					return
95				}
96				if c.recentlyDown(e) {
97					lastErr = fmt.Errorf("%s: recently unavailable", e.Name())
98					warns = append(warns, e.Name()+" skipped (recently unavailable)")
99					debug.Logf("chain: skip %s (recently unavailable)", e.Name())
100					continue
101				}
102				debug.Logf("chain: try %s", e.Name())
103				sub, err := e.Translate(ctx, req)
104				if err != nil {
105					lastErr = err
106					warns = append(warns, err.Error()) // engine errors are already name-prefixed
107					c.mark(e, false)
108					debug.Logf("chain: %s failed at connect: %v", e.Name(), err)
109					continue
110				}
111	
112				streamed, failed := false, false
113				for ch := range sub {
114					switch ch.Kind {
115					case ChunkToken:
116						streamed = true
117						out <- ch
118					case ChunkDone:
119						c.mark(e, true)
120						debug.Logf("chain: %s served the result", e.Name())
121						if ch.Result != nil && len(warns) > 0 {
122							ch.Result.Warnings = append(ch.Result.Warnings, warns...)
123						}
124						out <- ch
125						return
126					case ChunkError:
127						lastErr = ch.Err
128						failed = true
129						// Marking deferred until after the loop: a cancelled request
130						// (live-mode typing) must NOT be treated as an engine failure.
131					}
132				}
133	
134				if failed {
135					if ctx.Err() != nil { // cancelled: don't mark down, don't fail over
136						out <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: ctx.Err()}
137						return
138					}
139					c.mark(e, false)
140					warns = append(warns, lastErr.Error()) // already name-prefixed
141					if streamed {                          // already showed partial output: surface, don't restart
142						out <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: lastErr}
143						return
144					}
145					continue // clean pre-token failover
146				}
147			}
148			if lastErr == nil {
149				lastErr = ErrAllEnginesFailed
150			}
151			out <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrAllEnginesFailed, lastErr)}
152		}()
153		return out, nil
154	}
155	
156	// Detect returns the first available engine's detection, else "".
157	func (c *Chain) Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error) {
158		for _, e := range c.engines {
159			if c.recentlyDown(e) {
160				continue
161			}
162			if code, err := e.Detect(ctx, text); err == nil && code != "" {
163				return code, nil
164			}
165		}
166		return "", nil
167	}
168	
169	// Available reports whether any member is currently reachable.
170	func (c *Chain) Available(ctx context.Context) bool {
171		for _, e := range c.engines {
172			if e.Available(ctx) {
173				c.mark(e, true)
174				return true
175			}
176			c.mark(e, false)
177		}
178		return false
179	}
180

147		Vocab       []LearnGloss   `json:"vocab,omitempty"`     // teach-direction glosses
148		Examples    []LearnExample `json:"examples,omitempty"`  // teach-direction usage examples
149	}
150	
151	// LearnIssue is one grammar/usage correction (correct-direction).
152	type LearnIssue struct {
153		Span        string `json:"span"`        // the problematic fragment of the input
154		Fix         string `json:"fix"`         // the corrected fragment
155		Explanation string `json:"explanation"` // why — in the NATIVE language
156	}
157	
158	// LearnGloss is one vocabulary explanation (teach-direction).
159	type LearnGloss struct {
160		Term     string `json:"term"`               // foreign word/term
161		Pos      string `json:"pos,omitempty"`      // part of speech
162		Phonetic string `json:"phonetic,omitempty"` // KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese
163		Meaning  string `json:"meaning"`            // meaning in the NATIVE language
164	}
165	
166	// LearnExample is one usage example (teach-direction).
167	type LearnExample struct {
168		Foreign string `json:"foreign"` // example sentence in the foreign language
169		Native  string `json:"native"`  // its native-language translation
170	}
171	
172	// ChunkKind distinguishes streamed tokens from the terminal result/error.
173	type ChunkKind int
174	
175	const (
176		// ChunkToken is one streamed unit of translation text.
177		ChunkToken ChunkKind = iota
178		// ChunkDone carries the final structured result and ends the stream.
179		ChunkDone
180		// ChunkError carries a terminal error and ends the stream.
181		ChunkError
182	)
183	
184	// Chunk is one unit emitted on an engine's result channel.
185	type Chunk struct {
186		Kind   ChunkKind
187		Text   string           // token text (ChunkToken)
188		Result *TranslateResult // final result (ChunkDone)
189		Err    error            // terminal error (ChunkError)
190	}
191	
192	// Engine is the provider abstraction. Every method honors ctx cancellation.
193	//
194	// Translate returns a receive-only channel and MUST close it after sending
195	// exactly one terminal Chunk (ChunkDone or ChunkError). Streaming engines emit
196	// zero or more ChunkToken then one ChunkDone; non-streaming engines emit a
197	// single ChunkDone. This uniform "channel closed == finished" contract lets the
198	// TUI's self-resubscribing reader and the CLI's drain loop share one code path.
199	// The synchronous error return is only for immediate setup failures; all
```

```text
### Non-obvious constraints that shape the design (verified)
- **Raycast runs under launchd with a restricted PATH** that does *not* inherit
  your shell rc. `spawn("translate")` → `ENOENT`. Both tracks must resolve an
  **absolute** path (preference first, then probe `~/.local/bin`,
  `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`). Always test **from
  Raycast**, never a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug).
- **Exit code is 0 even when an engine fails** (it falls back), so callers read
  `warnings[]` from `--json`, never the exit code.
- **`useExec` buffers (no streaming) and its 10s timeout coerces `0`→10000**;
  LLM tiers exceed 10s. We use `execFile` with `timeout: 60_000`.
- **API keys must live in `translate`'s `config.toml`, not shell env** — a key
  exported in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd. We pass `HOME` through so the
  CLI finds its config; document this in `raycast/README.md`.

### Reuse (do not reimplement)
- JSON contract: `internal/engine/engine.go` — `TranslateResult` / `DictEntry`
  (the TS interfaces mirror these tags exactly).
- Flag surface: `cmd/root.go` — `--to/--from/--engine/--tier/--json/--no-history/--speak`.
- Install path + probe ordering rationale: `pitfalls/duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md`
  (`~/.local/bin` must come first in the probe).

---

## Directory tree (new top-level `raycast/`, sibling of `cmd/`, `internal/`, `backlog/`)
```

18	// Service is the subset of appcore.Service the HTTP handlers depend on.
19	// *appcore.Service satisfies it; tests inject a fake without touching the network.
20	type Service interface {
21		Translate(ctx context.Context, p appcore.Params) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
22		TranslateStream(ctx context.Context, p appcore.Params, onToken func(string)) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
23		Define(ctx context.Context, word string) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
24		HistoryRecent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]store.Record, error)
25		HistorySearch(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]store.Record, error)
26	}

28	// Options configures the HTTP server.
29	type Options struct {
30		Bind  string // bind address (loopback enforced unless Token is set)
31		Port  int
32		Token string // bearer token guarding /v1/history; "" => no auth
33	}
34	
35	// Server is the translate HTTP API server (loopback-only by default).
36	type Server struct {
37		httpSrv *http.Server
38		addr    string
39	}
40	
41	// New builds the server, enforcing the loopback-or-token rule and wiring routes.
42	func New(svc Service, opt Options) (*Server, error) {
43		if err := checkBind(opt.Bind, opt.Token); err != nil {
44			return nil, err
45		}
46		h := &handlers{svc: svc, token: opt.Token}
47		addr := net.JoinHostPort(opt.Bind, strconv.Itoa(opt.Port))
48		return &Server{
49			httpSrv: &http.Server{
50				Addr:              addr,
51				Handler:           newMux(h),
52				ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
53			},
54			addr: addr,
55		}, nil
56	}
57	
58	// newMux registers every route. Kept separate so tests can exercise the router
59	// directly and later phases (SSE, Swagger) can add routes in one place.
60	func newMux(h *handlers) *http.ServeMux {
61		mux := http.NewServeMux()
62		mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/translate", h.translate)
63		mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/translate/stream", h.translateStream)
64		mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/define", h.define)
65		mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/history", h.requireToken(h.history))
66		mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", h.healthz)
67		registerDocs(mux)
68		return mux
69	}
70	
71	// Addr is the resolved listen address (host:port).
72	func (s *Server) Addr() string { return s.addr }
73	
74	// Run serves until ctx is cancelled, then gracefully shuts down (5s drain).
75	func (s *Server) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
76		ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", s.httpSrv.Addr)
77		if err != nil {
78			return err
79		}
80		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: HTTP API on http://%s (docs: /docs)\n", s.addr)
81		errCh := make(chan error, 1)
82		go func() { errCh <- s.httpSrv.Serve(ln) }()
83	
84		select {
85		case <-ctx.Done():
86			shutCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
87			defer cancel()
88			return s.httpSrv.Shutdown(shutCtx)
89		case err := <-errCh:
90			if errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
91				return nil
92			}
93			return err
94		}
95	}
96	
97	// checkBind enforces the loopback-or-token rule: a non-loopback bind is refused
98	// unless a token is configured, since history is personal data.
99	func checkBind(bind, token string) error {
100		if isLoopback(bind) || token != "" {
101			return nil
102		}
103		return fmt.Errorf("refusing to bind non-loopback address %q without a token (history is personal data); bind 127.0.0.1 or set [server].token / token_env", bind)
104	}
105	
106	func isLoopback(bind string) bool {
107		if bind == "localhost" {
108			return true
109		}
110		ip := net.ParseIP(bind)
111		return ip != nil && ip.IsLoopback()
112	}

1	package tui

4	
5	// cacheKey identifies a translation result for the session cache. It is
6	// comparable, so it can be a map key. Keying on the *selected* engine name
7	// (e.g. "auto") means a chain fallback still caches under the user-visible engine.
8	// learn/pairMode/pairWith are included so a learn result, each pair direction
9	// (auto vs a forced target), and a plain translation of the same text never
10	// collide.
11	type cacheKey struct {
12		preset, engineName, model, source, target, text string
13		learn                                           bool
14		pairMode                                        pairMode
15		pairWith                                        string
16	}
17	
18	// cacheKeyFor builds the key for the given input text under the current settings.
19	func (m Model) cacheKeyFor(text string) cacheKey {
20		return cacheKey{
21			preset:     m.preset,
22			engineName: m.active().Name,
23			model:      m.modelOverride,
24			source:     m.source,
25			target:     m.target,
26			text:       text,
27			learn:      m.learn,
28			pairMode:   m.pairMode,
29			pairWith:   m.pairWith,
30		}
31	}
32	
33	// cacheStore is the session result cache. Session-scoped and unbounded (small);
34	// LLM output is nondeterministic so it is not persisted across sessions.
35	type cacheStore map[cacheKey]*engine.TranslateResult
36

1	# Frequency-aware "did you mean" suggestion ranking
2	
3	**Status**: P? — needs a spike
4	**Effort**: S–M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` P? · `internal/engine/{smartdict,ecdict}.go` · `raycast/extension/src/lib/did-you-mean.tsx` · [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07, surfaced while adding the Raycast "did you mean?" UX. The dictionary engine
10	returns fuzzy `suggestions[]` for single-word typos (consumed by Raycast
11	Translate/Define, and the CLI `define`). Ranking is **edit-distance only**, so the
12	obvious correction doesn't always surface first:
13	
14	- `recieve` → `[relieve, believe, reachieve, recarve, recede, receive, recidive]`
15	  (`receive` is 6th)
16	- `cononical` → `[canonical, acanonical, canonicals, …]` (`canonical` happens to be 1st)
17	
18	Google ranks by frequency ("Showing results for **canonical**"). We want the common
19	word on top.
20	
21	## Investigation
22	
23	- **ECDICT has frequency data** — `frq`, `bnc` columns (+ collins/oxford flags). A
24	  re-rank by `(editDistance asc, frequency desc)` would float common words up.
25	- Suggestions are produced in `internal/engine` (smart-dict / ecdict fuzzy lookup), so
26	  re-ranking there benefits **all** frontends at once — CLI `define`, Raycast, and the
27	  new `serve` / `mcp` adapters.
28	- `TranslateResult.SuggestDistance` exists but is `json:"-"` (not serialized). Exposing
29	  it (e.g. `suggest_distance`) would let a frontend auto-apply a confident correction
30	  ("Showing results for X · search instead for Y", Google-style) instead of only listing.
31	
32	## Options considered
33	
34	| Option | What | Verdict |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| A. Edit-distance only (current) | fuzzy by Levenshtein | simple; the right word is often not on top |
37	| B. Frequency-weighted re-rank | sort by (distance, then ECDICT `frq`/`bnc`) | best value; small change in the dict engine; helps every frontend |
38	| C. Expose `SuggestDistance` in `--json` | frontend decides auto-correct vs. list | pairs with B for a Google-style "showing results for X" |
39	| D. Keyboard-adjacency (qwerty) weighting | typo model | marginal over B; more complex |
40	
41	## Current blocker / open questions
42	
43	- Does the bundled ECDICT actually populate `frq`/`bnc` for enough headwords? (verify)
44	- Chinese suggestions are prefix matches with no distance/frequency — leave as-is, or
45	  pinyin/stroke rank?
46	- Threshold/cap: only show suggestions within distance N; how many to return.
47	
48	## Decision (if any)
49	
50	`2026-07 deferred` — the extension already surfaces the full list (usable, just not
51	ideally ordered). Do **B** (and optionally **C**) when polishing the did-you-mean UX.
52	Frontends need no change for B; C would let Translate/Define auto-apply the top
53	correction.
54	
55	## References
56	
57	- ECDICT schema (`frq`/`bnc`/collins/oxford): https://github.com/skywind3000/ECDICT
58	- Raycast did-you-mean component: `raycast/extension/src/lib/did-you-mean.tsx`
59

3	import (
4		"strings"
5		"unicode"
6	
7		"github.com/abadojack/whatlanggo"
8	)
9	
10	// Detect returns a best-effort ISO-639-1 source-language code for text, or "" if
11	// the guess is not confident. Used to fill DetectedSource on the LLM path (where
12	// the model returns only the translation) and as a fallback when APIs are down.
13	func Detect(text string) string {
14		info := whatlanggo.Detect(text)
15		if info.Confidence < 0.5 {
16			return ""
17		}
18		return info.Lang.Iso6391()
19	}
20	
21	// IsChinese reports whether text contains any Han characters — used to route
22	// dictionary lookups (Chinese → CC-CEDICT, else → ECDICT).
23	func IsChinese(text string) bool {
24		for _, r := range text {
25			if unicode.Is(unicode.Han, r) {
26				return true
27			}
28		}
29		return false
30	}
31	
32	// isCJKRune reports whether r is a CJK-script rune (Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or
33	// Hangul) — one such rune is roughly a word's worth of content.
34	func isCJKRune(r rune) bool {
35		return unicode.Is(unicode.Han, r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Hiragana, r) ||
36			unicode.Is(unicode.Katakana, r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Hangul, r)
37	}
38	
39	// containsCJK reports whether text contains any CJK-script rune (Han, Hiragana,
40	// Katakana, or Hangul). This is a reliable, offline signal for routing a
41	// CJK/non-CJK language pair — unlike trigram detection, it is confident even on
42	// very short input.
43	func containsCJK(text string) bool {
44		for _, r := range text {
45			if isCJKRune(r) {
46				return true
47			}
48		}
49		return false
50	}
51	
52	// cjkDominant reports whether CJK script dominates text, weighing content rather
53	// than mere presence: it compares the CJK rune count against the number of
54	// non-CJK "words" (maximal runs of non-CJK letters, any script). Because one CJK
55	// rune is roughly a word, this keeps a few CJK proper nouns embedded in a long
56	// Latin passage from flipping the routing — the bug where a mostly-English
57	// paragraph containing "李榮浩" was treated as Chinese and "translated" back into
58	// English — while genuinely CJK-heavy text still counts as CJK.
59	func cjkDominant(text string) bool {
60		var cjk, otherWords int
61		inWord := false
62		for _, r := range text {
63			switch {
64			case isCJKRune(r):
65				cjk++
66				inWord = false
67			case unicode.IsLetter(r):
68				if !inWord {
69					otherWords++
70					inWord = true
71				}
72			default:
73				inWord = false
74			}
75		}
76		return cjk > otherWords
77	}
78	
79	// isCJKLang reports whether a language code is Chinese, Japanese, or Korean.
80	func isCJKLang(code string) bool {
81		switch Base(code) {
82		case "zh", "ja", "ko":
83			return true
84		}
85		return false
86	}
87	
88	// PairTarget implements bidirectional "pair" mode: detect which of the two pair
89	// languages the text is written in and return the OTHER one (so "foreign → my
90	// language, my language → foreign" both work from one input box).
91	//
92	// When exactly one side of the pair is a CJK language, routing is decided by
93	// which script dominates the text — reliable and offline, and symmetric
94	// regardless of which side is "home". Dominance (not mere presence) is what lets
95	// short Latin input like "test" route to the CJK side, while a few CJK proper
96	// nouns inside a long Latin passage stay routed to the CJK side too (rather than
97	// flipping the whole thing to Latin). Same-script pairs (e.g. en⇄es) fall back to
98	// best-effort trigram detection.
99	func PairTarget(home, away, text string) string {
100		if away == "" || away == home {
101			return home
102		}
103		homeCJK, awayCJK := isCJKLang(home), isCJKLang(away)
104		if homeCJK != awayCJK {
105			cjk, latin := home, away
106			if awayCJK {
107				cjk, latin = away, home
108			}
109			if cjkDominant(text) {
110				return latin // predominantly CJK → the non-CJK language
111			}
112			return cjk // predominantly non-CJK → the CJK language
113		}
114		// Same-script pair (both or neither CJK): best-effort, symmetric detection.
115		inHome, inAway := inLang(text, home), inLang(text, away)
116		if inHome && !inAway {
117			return away
118		}
119		if inAway && !inHome {
120			return home
121		}
122		return home // inconclusive → default to home
123	}
124	
125	// inLang reports whether text is (best-effort) in the language of code. Chinese
126	// uses a reliable Han-script check; others fall back to offline detection.
127	func inLang(text, code string) bool {
128		base := Base(code)
129		switch base {
130		case "", "auto":
131			return false
132		case "zh":
133			return IsChinese(text)
134		default:
135			d := Detect(text)
136			return d != "" && d == base
137		}
138	}
139	
140	// Base strips a region suffix and normalizes case: "zh-TW" → "zh". It is the
141	// shared building block for region-insensitive language routing (used by the
142	// pair router here and by the tts voice/side selection).
143	func Base(code string) string {
144		code = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(code))
145		if i := strings.IndexByte(code, '-'); i > 0 {
146			return code[:i]
147		}
148		return code
149	}

// stubEngine is a canned engine.Engine for tests: it records the last request and
// replays a fixed sequence of chunks (or a synchronous setup error).
type stubEngine struct {
	name    string
	chunks  []engine.Chunk
	setErr  error
	lastReq engine.Request
}

func (s *stubEngine) Name() string                                   { return s.name }
func (s *stubEngine) Supports(engine.Mode) bool                      { return true }
func (s *stubEngine) Available(context.Context) bool                 { return true }
func (s *stubEngine) Detect(context.Context, string) (string, error) { return "", nil }

func (s *stubEngine) Translate(_ context.Context, req engine.Request) (<-chan engine.Chunk, error) {
	s.lastReq = req
	if s.setErr != nil {
		return nil, s.setErr
	}
	ch := make(chan engine.Chunk, len(s.chunks))
	for _, c := range s.chunks {
		ch <- c
	}
	close(ch)
	return ch, nil
}

2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. **Symptoms-first** knowledge base — when a
4	problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool combo),
5	grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround in
6	seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is maintainer-facing repo metadata. It lives in the git repo but
9	never reaches users — `go install` / `go build` compile only Go sources, so
10	`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` have no effect on the built binary.
11	
12	## Pitfalls vs the rest
13	
14	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
15	|---|---|---|---|
16	| `docs/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
17	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
18	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
19	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
20	
21	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant when the trap is serious enough
22	that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it recurs across
23	machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround is non-obvious
24	and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
25	as historical record and link to it from the new invariant.
26	
27	## When to add a pitfall doc
28	
29	Add `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
30	that wasn't googleable, AND any of:
31	
32	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (silent state, weird side
33	  effect, behaviour change without error)
34	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order"
35	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
36	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
37	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and failure at the
38	  wrong version is silent / confusing
39	
40	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
41	
42	- Trivially googleable (next person solves in 30 seconds)
43	- Already covered in `docs/<tool>.md` — cross-link from this README's
44	  "Cross-referenced pitfalls" table below instead of duplicating
45	- Already a Hard invariant (cross-link only)
46	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot)
47	
48	## File template
49	
50	See [`pitfall-doc.md.template`] in the
51	[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness)
52	for the per-doc template.
53	
54	Key sections (different from `backlog/` template — symptom-first, not
55	context-first):
56	
57	```markdown
58	# <Title describing the SYMPTOM, not the root cause>
59	
60	**Symptoms** (grep this section): <verbatim error messages, observable behaviour>
61	**First seen**: YYYY-MM
62	**Affects**: <tool/version/OS combo>
63	**Status**: workaround documented / fixed upstream in vX.Y / WONTFIX
64	
65	## Symptom
66	
67	Full error messages (verbatim — preserves grep-ability).
68	
69	## Root cause
70	
71	Why this happens, with source/docs/upstream issue link.
72	
73	## Workaround
74	
75	Copy-pasteable commands or config diff.
76	
77	## Prevention
78	
79	How to avoid stepping on this again.
80	
81	## Related
82	
83	Links to docs, sibling pitfalls, TODO entries, upstream issues.
84	```
85	
86	## Index
87	
88	Pitfalls owned by this folder. Keep alphabetical.
89	
90	| Slug | Symptom keywords | Status |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| `duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin` | two `translate` on PATH, `command -v -a`, reinstall has no effect, `~/.dotfiles/bin` shadows `~/.local/bin` | workaround; fix in TODO P2 |
93	| `go-install-module-path-mismatch` | `module declares its path as: translate`, `but was required as`, `parsing go.mod` | fixed (module renamed) |
94	| `gobin-points-at-mise-toolchain-dir` | binary vanishes after Go upgrade, `go env GOBIN` = `.../mise/installs/go/<ver>/bin` | workaround (pin GOBIN) |
95	| `llm-stream-truncation-silently-rendered-as-complete` | translation cut mid-word / half output, no error, `detected:` line still shown, streamed result truncated, copilot-proxy SSE dropped | fixed (assert stream completeness) |
96	| `raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found` | `spawn translate ENOENT`, `translate: command not found` in Raycast, works in terminal not Raycast, launchd PATH not inherited from shell | prevented (absolute-path probe) |
97	| `tui-lipgloss-block-padding-inflates-blank-lines-in-viewport` | TUI shows many blank lines / big gaps between paragraphs, excess vertical whitespace, but `^y` copy is clean, gap grows with paragraph length / narrow width / CJK | fixed (per-line styling) |
98	| `tui-viewport-clips-long-translation-no-softwrap` | TUI translation cut mid-sentence but CLI/curl shows full text, no `⚠`, long/multi-line results clipped, viewport SoftWrap | fixed (SoftWrap=true) |
99	
100	## Cross-referenced pitfalls (still in their original homes)
101	
102	These traps are documented elsewhere and aren't duplicated here — the table
103	exists so grepping `pitfalls/` still finds them. Move into this folder only
104	if their original location stops being a natural reading flow.
105	
106	| Trap | Lives in | Why not here |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| (example: Tool X version Y bug) | `docs/tool-x.md` → "Known issues" | Already part of the tool's normal config narrative |

154	// targetLangOptions builds the language dropdown options (name + code).
155	func targetLangOptions() []huh.Option[string] {
156		ls := lang.List()
157		opts := make([]huh.Option[string], 0, len(ls))
158		for _, l := range ls {
159			opts = append(opts, huh.NewOption(fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", l.Name, l.Code), l.Code))
160		}
161		return opts
162	}
163	
164	func probeLabel(name string, up bool) string {
165		if up {
166			return name + "  ● up"
167		}
168		return name + "  ○ down"
169	}
170	
171	func probeProvider(cfg *config.Config, name string) bool {
172		p := cfg.ProviderByName(name)
173		if p == nil {
174			return false
175		}
176		return probeURL(strings.TrimRight(p.BaseURL, "/")+"/models", 1500*time.Millisecond)
177	}
178	
179	func probeURL(url string, timeout time.Duration) bool {
180		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeout)
181		defer cancel()
182		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil)
183		if err != nil {
184			return false
185		}
186		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
187		if err != nil {
188			return false
189		}
190		defer resp.Body.Close()
191		return resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK
192	}

package engine

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"unicode"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/debug"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/lang"
)

// SmartAutoEngine is the "smart" default: it treats a single word/term as a
// dictionary lookup (delegating to the smart-dict engine, which itself falls back
// to the LLM on a miss) and a phrase or sentence as an LLM translation. It is
// bidirectional-friendly — the caller sets Pair/PairHome/PairAway and the routed
// Target, and both branches honor them.
//
// Because dictionary word lookups are direction-agnostic (script routes them to
// CC-CEDICT vs ECDICT) and phrase translation uses the pair-aware LLM prompt, a
// single word like "test" is answered from the dictionary instead of risking an
// LLM echo, and a full sentence is translated into the other pair language.
type SmartAutoEngine struct {
	smart Engine // dictionary + LLM fallback (serves ModeDict)
	llm   Engine // LLM translate, possibly a fallback chain (serves ModeTranslate)
}

// NewSmartAuto builds a smart-auto engine over a smart-dict engine (word lookups)
// and an LLM/translate engine (phrases).
func NewSmartAuto(smart, llm Engine) *SmartAutoEngine {
	return &SmartAutoEngine{smart: smart, llm: llm}
}

// Name returns "smart-auto".
func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Name() string { return "smart-auto" }

// Supports translate mode (the main-path request mode); it dispatches to a
// dictionary lookup internally when the input looks like a single word.
func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Supports(m Mode) bool { return m == ModeTranslate }

// Detect is not meaningful here (the LLM/dict sub-engines own detection).
func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error) {
	return "", nil
}

// Available reports true when either branch can serve.
func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Available(ctx context.Context) bool {
	return e.smart.Available(ctx) || e.llm.Available(ctx)
}

// Translate routes a single word/term to the dictionary (smart-dict) and a phrase
// to the LLM. Streaming is preserved by returning the chosen sub-engine's channel.
func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
	if isLookup(req.Text) {
		debug.Logf("smart-auto: %q → dictionary lookup (smart-dict), target=%s", truncateText(req.Text), req.Target)
		r := req
		r.Mode = ModeDict
		return e.smart.Translate(ctx, r)
	}
	debug.Logf("smart-auto: %q → LLM translate, target=%s pair=%v", truncateText(req.Text), req.Target, req.Pair)
	r := req
	r.Mode = ModeTranslate
	return e.llm.Translate(ctx, r)
}

// isLookup reports whether text should be treated as a dictionary lookup (a
// single word or short term) rather than a phrase to translate. Latin/other: one
// token of letters (plus '-' / apostrophe), up to 32 runes. CJK: a short run of
// Han without spaces (a word or idiom, up to 4 characters). Anything with
// internal whitespace is a phrase.
func isLookup(text string) bool {
	t := strings.TrimSpace(text)
	if t == "" {
		return false
	}
	if strings.ContainsAny(t, " \t\n\r") {
		return false // multiple tokens → phrase
	}
	if lang.IsChinese(t) {
		return len([]rune(t)) <= 4
	}
	for _, r := range t {
		if !unicode.IsLetter(r) && r != '-' && r != '\'' {
			return false // digits/punctuation → not a plain word
		}
	}
	return len([]rune(t)) <= 32
}

// truncateText shortens a string for a single-line debug label.
func truncateText(s string) string {
	s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
	r := []rune(s)
	if len(r) > 40 {
		return string(r[:40]) + "…"
	}
	return s
}

package engine

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"
)

type ecdictEntry struct {
	Word, Phonetic, Translation, Definition string
}

// ecdictDB queries the locally-built ECDICT SQLite (English → Chinese). Point
// lookups are on-disk (near-zero steady-state RAM). Opened lazily.
type ecdictDB struct {
	path string
	once sync.Once
	err  error
	db   *sql.DB
}

func newEcdictDB(path string) *ecdictDB { return &ecdictDB{path: path} }

func (e *ecdictDB) available() bool {
	_, err := os.Stat(e.path)
	return err == nil
}

func (e *ecdictDB) open() error {
	e.once.Do(func() {
		if _, err := os.Stat(e.path); err != nil {
			e.err = err
			return
		}
		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+e.path+"?_pragma=query_only(true)")
		if err != nil {
			e.err = err
			return
		}
		e.db = db
	})
	return e.err
}

// lookup returns the exact (case-insensitive) entry, or nil if not found.
func (e *ecdictDB) lookup(ctx context.Context, word string) (*ecdictEntry, error) {
	if err := e.open(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	row := e.db.QueryRowContext(ctx,
		`SELECT word, phonetic, translation, definition FROM entries WHERE word_lc = ? LIMIT 1`,
		strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(word)))
	var en ecdictEntry
	switch err := row.Scan(&en.Word, &en.Phonetic, &en.Translation, &en.Definition); err {
	case nil:
		return &en, nil
	case sql.ErrNoRows:
		return nil, nil
	default:
		return nil, err
	}
}

// splitEcdict splits ECDICT translation/definition fields — their senses are
// joined by a literal backslash-n, not a real newline.

	var out []string
	for _, p := range strings.Split(s, `\n`) {
